[[File:Ben Roethlisberger - snap.jpg|thumb|right|Roethlisberger takes a snap against the Bengals in 2006]]

When [[ESPN]] began broadcasting MAC games on Tuesdays and Wednesdays—days without other football on television—in 2000, nationwide "[[MACtion]]" audiences watched Roethlisberger's teams.<ref name="sherman20191119">{{cite web |last=Sherman |first=Rodger |date=November 19, 2019 |title=How the Rise of MACtion Forever Changed MAC Fandom |url=https://www.theringer.com/2019/11/19/20972679/mac-midweek-games-maction-television-networks-fan-experience |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=The Ringer |language=en |archive-date=November 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191120071432/https://www.theringer.com/2019/11/19/20972679/mac-midweek-games-maction-television-networks-fan-experience |url-status=live }}</ref> The success of the 2003 Miami Redhawks led to the expectation that he would be drafted early. At the combine, Roethlisberger scored a 25 on the [[Wonderlic]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Coolong |first=Neal |date=April 15, 2015 |title=Ben Roethlisberger once scored (allegedly) 25 on the Wonderlic Test |url=https://steelerswire.usatoday.com/2015/04/15/nfl-draft-jameis-winston-wonderlic-test-results-ben-roethlisberger/ |access-date=December 7, 2019 |website=Steelers Wire |language=en |archive-date=December 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207195300/https://steelerswire.usatoday.com/2015/04/15/nfl-draft-jameis-winston-wonderlic-test-results-ben-roethlisberger/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During the GMAC Bowl, commentators discussed some of his skills that would translate to success in the NFL. Roethlisberger was one of the players invited to attend the draft along with others in the "Green Room" and was featured on the show ''Hey Rookie, Welcome to the NFL''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hey Rookie, Welcome to the NFL |url=https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/hey-rookie-welcome-to-the-nfl/episode-2-season-3/hey-rookie-welcome-to-the-nfl/382141/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=TV Guide |archive-date=January 2, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190102143029/https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/hey-rookie-welcome-to-the-nfl/episode-2-season-3/hey-rookie-welcome-to-the-nfl/382141/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the [[2004 NFL draft]], Roethlisberger was the second-highest touted quarterback behind [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss]]' [[Eli Manning]]. He was projected to be taken by the [[New York Giants]] as the fourth overall pick, with the [[History of the San Diego Chargers|San Diego Chargers]] taking Manning first overall.<ref name="Linked">{{cite web |last=Youngmisuk |first=Ohm |date=November 2, 2012 |title=Giants, Steelers linked by the QBs |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/8583162/new-york-giants-almost-had-ben-roethlisberger-eli-manning |access-date=September 22, 2020 |website=[[ESPN]] |archive-date=May 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220501212541/https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/8583162/new-york-giants-almost-had-ben-roethlisberger-eli-manning |url-status=live }}</ref> While the Chargers drafted Manning, the Giants instead selected [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State]] quarterback [[Philip Rivers]] as part of a trade deal that sent Manning to the Giants and Rivers to the Chargers. The [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] selected Roethlisberger 11th overall, making him the highest-drafted quarterback to play for the team that picked him, and the highest draft pick the Steelers used on a quarterback since selecting [[Terry Bradshaw]] [[List of first overall National Football League Draft picks|first overall]] in 1970.<ref name="2004draft">{{Cite web |title=2004 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181101231250/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |archive-date=November 1, 2018 |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers All-Time Draft History |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406222700/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/draft.htm |archive-date=April 6, 2022 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Steelers almost didn't select Roethlisberger, as head coach [[Bill Cowher]] and director of football operations [[Kevin Colbert]] had planned to select [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas]] guard [[Shawn Andrews (American football)|Shawn Andrews]]. However, Steelers owner [[Dan Rooney]] overrode both Cowher and Colbert upon seeing that Roethlisberger was still available and the Steelers not wanting a repeat of passing on a franchise quarterback, as they had done in the [[1983 NFL draft]] when they drafted [[Gabriel Rivera]] while local product [[Dan Marino]] was still available.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Scott |date=April 24, 2014 |title=Big Ben pick returned Steelers to glory |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/pittsburgh-steelers/post/_/id/6043/big-ben-pick-returned-steelers-to-glory |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |archive-date=October 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026184201/https://www.espn.com/blog/pittsburgh-steelers/post/_/id/6043/big-ben-pick-returned-steelers-to-glory |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger was being interviewed [[Live television|live]] on ESPN by [[Suzy Kolber]] when he received the phone call from Cowher, confirming his selection before it was officially announced by [[Paul Tagliabue]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Bryan Anthony |date=April 23, 2020 |title=Draft Day Memories: A franchise quarterback slips to the Steelers in a big way |url=https://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/2020/4/23/21229110/draft-day-memories-a-franchise-qb-slips-to-the-steelers-in-a-big-way-ben-roethlisberger-steelers |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=Behind the Steel Curtain |language=en |archive-date=June 9, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200609131446/https://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/2020/4/23/21229110/draft-day-memories-a-franchise-qb-slips-to-the-steelers-in-a-big-way-ben-roethlisberger-steelers |url-status=live }}</ref>

Roethlisberger was one of 17 quarterbacks taken in the 2004 NFL draft, along with Manning and Rivers.<ref name="2004draft" /> All three would enjoy lengthy and successful careers with the teams that signed them and have been compared favorably to the aforementioned 1983 draft, which included [[Pro Football Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] quarterbacks [[John Elway]], [[Jim Kelly]], and Marino.<ref>{{cite web |last=Banks |first=Don |date=August 28, 2009 |title=Best quarterback class ever? Trio from '04 makes its case over '83 |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/don_banks/08/28/qbs/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090831150446/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/don_banks/08/28/qbs/index.html |archive-date=August 31, 2009 |access-date=July 27, 2010 |website=SI.com}}</ref> A two-time [[Super Bowl]] winner and six-time [[Pro Bowl]]er, Roethlisberger leads the three in wins, winning percentage, and postseason appearances, and had the longest career among them.<ref name="benpfr" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Eli Manning Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MannEl00.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220502191743/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MannEl00.htm |archive-date=May 2, 2022 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Philip Rivers Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RivePh00.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503231427/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RivePh00.htm |archive-date=May 3, 2022 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="2004draft" />

===2004===
{{See also|2004 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
[[File:Ben Roethlisberger 2005 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Roethlisberger before a game at [[Heinz Field]]]]
On August 4, Roethlisberger signed a six-year contract to the Steelers worth $22.26 million in salaries and bonuses, with an additional $17.73 million available via incentives. He was touted by Steelers head coach [[Bill Cowher]] in a press conference as a franchise quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bakay |first=Nick |date=May 26, 2010 |title=Pittsburgh proves it: Franchise QB = long-term success |url=http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/story?id=09000d5d80e973a2&template=with-video-with-comments&confirm=true |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110916141318/http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/story?id=09000d5d80e973a2&template=with-video-with-comments&confirm=true |archive-date=September 16, 2011 |access-date=December 11, 2011 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

He started his rookie season as the third quarterback on the depth chart behind veterans [[Tommy Maddox]] and [[Charlie Batch]]. When Batch was injured in the preseason, however, Roethlisberger took over the backup quarterback role. Maddox started, and won, the season opener against the [[2004 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] and started versus the [[2004 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], but after an ineffective outing and third-quarter injury to Maddox, Roethlisberger stepped in for his first NFL action.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at Pittsburgh Steelers - September 12th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200409120pit.htm |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Despite spurring a mild comeback, the Steelers lost to the Ravens by a score of 30–13. In his regular season debut against the Ravens, Roethlisberger completed 12 of 20 passes for 176-yards and two touchdowns, and two interceptions. During the game, he threw his first career touchdown, on a three-yard pass to [[Antwaan Randle El]] and also threw his first career interception to Ravens linebacker [[Adalius Thomas]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Baltimore Ravens – September 19th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200409190rav.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001507/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200409190rav.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Maddox's injury changed the Steelers' initial plan for Roethlisberger, which was for him to sit on the bench or play sparingly during the first season or two in order to learn the team's system. Instead, he started the third game of the season against the [[2004 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]], finishing the 13–3 victory with 12 of 22 completions, 163 passing yards, one touchdown, and an interception.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Miami Dolphins – September 26th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200409260mia.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115214633/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200409260mia.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 6, in a 24–20 victory over the [[2004 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]], he was 21 of 25 for 193 passing yards and two touchdowns to earn his first AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Dallas Cowboys – October 17th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200410170dal.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329131407/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200410170dal.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2004 NFL Week 6 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/week_6.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328201239/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/week_6.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

As a rookie, he went 13–0 in the regular season (14–1 including playoffs) as a starting quarterback, helping the Steelers become the first AFC team to have 15 wins (2–1 under Maddox [first two and last game], 13–0 under Roethlisberger) in a single regular season, surpassing former Steeler [[Mike Kruczek]] for the record for the best start by a rookie (6–0) and exceeding the mark for total wins as a rookie, set by [[Chris Chandler (American football)|Chris Chandler]] and [[Joe Ferguson]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Roethlisberger 2004 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2004 |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001533/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2004 |url-status=live }}</ref> On January 5, Roethlisberger was unanimously selected as the [[NFL Rookie of the Year Award|NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year]] by the Associated Press, the first quarterback in 34 years to be so honored.<ref>{{cite web |title=AP Offensive Rookie of the Year Winners |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/ap-offensive-rookie-of-the-year-award.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=November 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116080408/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/ap-offensive-rookie-of-the-year-award.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In addition, he was named to the NFL All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{cite web |title=2004 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2004.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328201237/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2004.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 31, he had one of his biggest games, leading the Steelers to a 34–20 victory over the defending [[Super Bowl]] champion and previously undefeated [[2004 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]], ending their NFL-record 21-game winning streak. He completed 18 of 24 pass attempts for 196 yards, two touchdowns, and no turnovers.<ref>{{cite web |title=New England Patriots at Pittsburgh Steelers – October 31st, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200410310pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001622/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200410310pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The next game, the Steelers defeated the also previously undefeated [[2004 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] 27–3, with Roethlisberger going 11 of 18 for 183 yards, with two touchdowns and one interception.<ref>{{cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Pittsburgh Steelers – November 7th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200411070pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001537/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200411070pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On December 5, he led the Steelers to a 17–16 victory over the [[2004 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He was near-perfect on the night, completing 14 of 17 passes for 226 yards and two touchdowns. Jeff Reed's 37-yard field goal in the final minute gave the Steelers and Roethlisberger their tenth straight win.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Jacksonville Jaguars – December 5th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200412050jax.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184503/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200412050jax.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Two weeks later, Roethlisberger faced off against the [[2004 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] and the first overall pick of the 2004 draft, Eli Manning. Roethlisberger posted his first career 300-yard passing game, with 18 of 28 passes for 316 yards and a touchdown. He led his fifth game-winning drive of the season, capping a drive with a Jerome Bettis touchdown run for a 33–30 victory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at New York Giants – December 18th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200412180nyg.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184430/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200412180nyg.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the [[2004–05 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 20, New York Jets 17 (OT)|Divisional Round]] of the playoffs against the [[2004 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], Roethlisberger threw two interceptions. One interception was returned for a touchdown, and the other was thrown with 2:03 left in the fourth quarter, which set up a potential game-winning field goal by Jets kicker [[Doug Brien]]. Brien missed the kick as time expired (his second missed kick in the last two minutes of the game), forcing the game into overtime. In overtime, Roethlisberger led the Steelers down the field and put them in position for the game-winning field goal, a 33-yard attempt that was made by [[Jeff Reed (American football)|Jeff Reed]], sending the Steelers into the AFC Championship for the fourth time in 10 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Divisional Round – New York Jets at Pittsburgh Steelers – January 15th, 2005 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200501150pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001431/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200501150pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 23 in the [[NFL playoffs, 2004–05#AFC: New England Patriots 41, Pittsburgh Steelers 27|AFC Championship Game]] in Pittsburgh, Roethlisberger completed 14 of 24 pass attempts for 226 yards and two touchdowns, but he also threw three costly interceptions, one of which was returned 87 yards for a touchdown by [[Rodney Harrison]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Cafardo |first=Nick |date=January 24, 2005 |title=Steel hurtin' |url=https://archive.boston.com/sports/football/patriots/articles/2005/01/24/steel_hurtin/ |access-date=December 6, 2019 |website=Boston.com |archive-date=December 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206073359/http://archive.boston.com/sports/football/patriots/articles/2005/01/24/steel_hurtin/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Steelers lost the game to the eventual [[Super Bowl XXXIX|Super Bowl]] champions, the New England Patriots, by a score of 41–27.<ref>{{cite web |title=AFC Championship – New England Patriots at Pittsburgh Steelers – January 23rd, 2005 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200501230pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115214631/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200501230pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2005: First Super Bowl championship===
{{See also|2005 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
[[File:Roethlisberger-Bettis-Berman.jpg|thumb|left|Roethlisberger signs autographs at Super Bowl XL media day]]
In the 2005 regular season, the Steelers finished with an 11–5 record. After securing an AFC Wild Card spot en route to victory in the Super Bowl, the Steelers pulled off upsets at Indianapolis and Denver in the AFC playoffs in addition to wins over the higher seed Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks.<ref>{{cite web |title=2005 Pittsburgh Steelers Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/2005.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=December 18, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218104328/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/2005.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the course of the regular 2005 season, Roethlisberger missed four games due to various knee injuries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |date=2005-10-12 |title=Roethlisberger's Injury Has Not Ended His Season |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/10/12/sports/football/roethlisbergers-injury-has-not-ended-his-season.html |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US}}</ref> The Steelers went 9–3 with Roethlisberger at quarterback and 2–2 without him. He led the league in yards per attempt, with an 8.90, and finished third in passer rating behind [[Peyton Manning]] and [[Carson Palmer]] with a 98.6.<ref>{{cite web |title=2005 NFL Passing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/passing.htm |access-date=December 7, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 31, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231155345/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/passing.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Ben Roethlisberger.JPG|thumb|upright|Roethlisberger at the Super Bowl Parade]]
The Super Bowl run began on January 8 as Roethlisberger helped lead the Steelers to a [[2005–06 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 31, Cincinnati Bengals 17|Divisional Round]] playoff win over the [[2005 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]]—an [[AFC North]] rival that had beaten the Steelers by seven points in the regular season to win the division championship. The rematch featured two teams with identical records, having split their regular season series since each team won on the road. Early in the game on Carson Palmer's first throw, a tackle by former Bengal [[Kimo von Oelhoffen]] resulted in Palmer's anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) being completely torn.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bell |first=Samuel Jr. |date=September 25, 2008 |title=Wounded Bengals: The Injury That Changed the Course of Two Franchises |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/61642-wounded-bengals-the-injury-that-changed-the-course-of-two-franchises |access-date=December 6, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en |archive-date=December 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206042949/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/61642-wounded-bengals-the-injury-that-changed-the-course-of-two-franchises |url-status=live }}</ref> The Bengals' backup quarterback, [[Jon Kitna]], came in and led the Bengals to leads of 10–0 and 17–7. However, the 17–7 lead midway through the second quarter was the last time in the 2005 postseason that the Steelers trailed an opponent by more than three points. After Kitna failed to produce, the Steelers took advantage by taking the next 24 straight points, and the win, in a 31–17 victory in Cincinnati.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wild Card – Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals – January 8th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200601080cin.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=August 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802220035/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200601080cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Their second road win came on January 15 when Roethlisberger led the Steelers against the [[2005 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in the [[2005–06 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 21, Indianapolis Colts 18|Divisional Round]], the NFL's top team throughout the season and a heavy favorite to represent the AFC in Super Bowl XL. Roethlisberger threw for 197 yards and recorded a game-saving tackle on Colts' defensive back [[Nick Harper (American football)|Nick Harper]], who had just recovered a [[Jerome Bettis]] [[fumble]] with less than two minutes left in the game. Pittsburgh led early, but had to survive a Colts comeback to win 21–18, after an errant call that the NFL later admitted was a mistake,<ref name="nfl">{{Cite web |last=Guzman |first=Hugo |date=January 16, 2006 |title=Oops! My bad...NFL admits blown call on Polamalu INT |url=http://www.realfootball365.com/nfl/articles/nfl-blown-call160106.php |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060126235903/http://www.realfootball365.com/nfl/articles/nfl-blown-call160106.php |archive-date=January 26, 2006 |access-date=December 11, 2011 |website=Realfootball365.com}}</ref> which overturned a [[Troy Polamalu]] interception that would have secured the game for the Steelers. Roethlisberger's tackle on Harper, dubbed by many as The Tackle II or The Immaculate Redemption, was compared by many to "[[Immaculate Reception|The Immaculate Reception]]" in 1972, when [[Franco Harris]] made a miraculous reception and scored the game-winning touchdown against the [[Oakland Raiders]]. The victory marked the first time in playoff history that a sixth-seeded NFL playoff team defeated the top-seeded team.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Breech |first=John |date=January 11, 2014 |title=NFL Playoffs: 6-seeds are 5–2 against No. 1 seeds since 2005 |work=CBSSports.com |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-playoffs-6-seeds-are-5-2-against-no-1-seeds-since-2005/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |archive-date=January 2, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190102094814/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-playoffs-6-seeds-are-5-2-against-no-1-seeds-since-2005/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 22, 2006, the Steelers defeated the [[2005 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] by a score of 34–17 in Denver to win the [[2005–06 NFL playoffs#AFC Championship: Pittsburgh Steelers 34, Denver Broncos 17|AFC Championship]] and advance to Super Bowl XL. Roethlisberger completed 21 of 29 passes for 275 yards and threw two touchdown passes and scored one touchdown himself on a four-yard [[Play action pass|play-action]] [[Bootleg play|bootleg]]. His run was the last touchdown of the game, sealing the win for the Steelers.<ref>{{cite web |title=AFC Championship – Pittsburgh Steelers at Denver Broncos – January 22nd, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200601220den.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=August 4, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804014449/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200601220den.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Steelers won Super Bowl XL 21–10 over the [[2005 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] in Detroit on February 5.<ref>{{cite web |last=Miller |first=Ira |date=February 6, 2006 |title=SUPER BOWL XL: Steelers 21, Seahawks 10 |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/SUPER-BOWL-XL-Steelers-21-Seahawks-10-A-BIG-2541925.php |access-date=December 6, 2019 |website=SFGate |archive-date=December 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206043008/https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/SUPER-BOWL-XL-Steelers-21-Seahawks-10-A-BIG-2541925.php |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger had one of the worst passing games of his career, completing just nine of 21 passes for 123 yards and two interceptions; his [[passer rating]] of 22.6 was the lowest in Super Bowl history by a winning quarterback. Though he did convert eight third-down situations in the game to help the Steelers win, none of them was bigger than his 37-yard pass to Super Bowl XL MVP Hines Ward on a third-and-28 that set up the Steelers' first touchdown (a one-yard quarterback sneak by Roethlisberger on third and goal). With the victory, Roethlisberger, at 23 years old, became the youngest quarterback to win the Super Bowl, a record previously held by [[Tom Brady]] of the New England Patriots.<ref>{{cite web | last=Maniece | first=Mykenna | title=The 10 youngest starting quarterbacks to win the Super Bowl | website=Business Insider | date=2024-02-07 | url=https://www.businessinsider.com/youngest-quarterbacks-to-win-super-bowl#:~:text=Ben%20Roethlisberger%20is%20the%20youngest,months%2C%20and%203%20days%20old.&text=%22Big%20Ben%22%20and%20the%20Pittsburgh,XL%20in%202006%2C%20ESPN%20reported. | access-date=2024-07-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sutelan |first=Edward |date=February 13, 2022 |title=Youngest QBs to win a Super Bowl: Bengals' Joe Burrow looks to join rare company |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/joe-burrow-super-bowl-youngest-qbs-to-win-bengals/jcir0mifm6ofamklhivns2mc |access-date=May 27, 2022 |website=www.sportingnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2006===
{{See also|2006 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
After an off-season motorcycle crash in which he was seriously injured, Roethlisberger missed the opening game of the 2006 season after having an emergency [[Appendicectomy|appendectomy]] on September 3.<ref>{{cite news |last=Pasquarelli |first=Len |date=September 3, 2006 |title=Roethlisberger to miss opener after appendectomy |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2572171 |access-date=December 6, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=February 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215215416/https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2572171 |url-status=live }}</ref> Backup Charlie Batch started and led the Steelers to a victory over the [[2006 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. Roethlisberger played the following game against the [[2006 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]]. His return resulted in a sub-par performance as he threw two interceptions with no touchdowns in a 9–0 loss.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Jacksonville Jaguars – September 18th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200609180jax.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001602/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200609180jax.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 3, Roethlisberger completed fewer than half of his passes for three interceptions and no touchdowns in a 28–20 loss to the [[2006 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]]. The final interception came in the final seconds of the game, in the end zone, ending Pittsburgh's comeback attempt.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers – September 24th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200609240pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001514/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200609240pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Ben Roethlisberger Steelers cropped.jpg|thumb|left|Roethlisberger drops back against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in 2006]]
In Week 5 against the [[2006 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]], Roethlisberger looked sharp throughout the first half, leading three scoring drives. However, in the second half, he threw two interceptions, both of which shifted momentum away from the Steelers and led to the Chargers' 23–13 win.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at San Diego Chargers – October 8th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610080sdg.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412094908/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610080sdg.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 6 against the [[2006 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]], Roethlisberger had his first big game of the season, completing 16 of 19 passes for 238 yards with two touchdowns (his first of the year) and no interceptions during a 45–7 rout of the Chiefs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Pittsburgh Steelers – October 15th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610150pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001535/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610150pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> During Week 7 in [[2006 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta]], Roethlisberger continued his success, going 16 of 22 for 237 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Atlanta Falcons – October 22nd, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610220atl.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184457/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610220atl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> However, during the third quarter, Roethlisberger was helped off the field after sustaining a concussion following a controversial hit by Falcons defensive end [[Patrick Kerney]]. Roethlisberger was replaced by Charlie Batch, and the Steelers went on to lose 41–38 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bouchette |first=Ed |date=October 22, 2006 |title=Falcons beat Steelers in overtime, 41–38 |work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/sports/steelers/2006/10/22/Falcons-beat-Steelers-in-overtime-41-38/stories/200610220212 |access-date=November 2, 2018 |archive-date=January 2, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190102143205/https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/steelers/2006/10/22/Falcons-beat-Steelers-in-overtime-41-38/stories/200610220212 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 29 against the [[2006 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]], Roethlisberger threw four interceptions in a 20–13 upset loss.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Oakland Raiders – October 29th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610290rai.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001610/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610290rai.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The loss was his fifth of the season—two more than he had in his first two seasons combined as a starter—and gave him a total of 11 interceptions, versus just six touchdowns, on the season. In a Week 9 rematch of the 2005 AFC Championship against the [[2006 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]], Roethlisberger threw for a career-high 433 yards, but had three of the six Steelers turnovers in a 31–20 loss.<ref>{{cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers – November 5th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611050pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001619/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611050pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger and the Steelers got back on a winning track in a home game a week later against the [[2006 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. He passed for 265 yards and three touchdowns in a 38–31 win.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Pittsburgh Steelers – November 12th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611120pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627224256/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611120pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 11, Roethlisberger overcame three first-half interceptions by throwing for 224 yards and two touchdowns in the fourth quarter, leading the Steelers to score 21 points and come back to beat the [[2006 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], 24–20.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns – November 19th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611190cle.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184424/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611190cle.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The following week, Roethlisberger and the Steelers were held scoreless in a 27–0 loss to the [[2006 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]]. Roethlisberger finished 21 of 41 for 214 yards and two interceptions. He was sacked nine times, including once by Ravens linebacker [[Bart Scott]], which sent him to the sidelines briefly. He also fumbled once, which the Ravens returned for a touchdown in the second half.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Baltimore Ravens – November 26th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611260rav.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001510/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611260rav.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger bounced back the following game, throwing for 198 yards and two touchdowns in a 20–3 victory over the [[2006 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 3rd, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612030pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001624/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612030pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Pittsburgh kept their playoff hopes alive in Week 14 with a 27–7 victory against the Browns. Roethlisberger went 11 of 21 for 225 yards with one touchdown, and rushed for one more.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 7th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612070pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001557/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612070pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 15, Roethlisberger threw for 140 yards and a touchdown in a 37–3 rout of the [[2006 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Carolina Panthers – December 17th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612170car.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184501/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612170car.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The following week, Baltimore eliminated Pittsburgh from the playoffs. In the 31–7 defeat, Roethlisberger was intercepted twice and threw for 156 yards.<ref>{{cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 24th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612240pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001433/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612240pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Roethlisberger ended the season on a good note by defeating the Cincinnati Bengals by a score of 23–17 in overtime and eliminating them from playoff contention in what was Bill Cowher's final game as the Steelers' head coach. He was 19 for 28 passing with 280 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. In overtime, Roethlisberger completed a slant pass to rookie Santonio Holmes, who went 67 yards for the game-winning touchdown.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kay |first=Joe |date=December 31, 2006 |title=Steelers Shatter Bengals' Playoff Hopes |url=https://www.foxnews.com/printer_friendly_wires/2006Dec31/0,4675,FBNSteelersBengals,00.html |access-date=December 7, 2019 |website=FOXNews.com |archive-date=December 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207195355/https://www.foxnews.com/printer_friendly_wires/2006Dec31/0,4675,FBNSteelersBengals,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2007===
{{See also|2007 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
In Week 1 against the [[2007 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], Roethlisberger threw four touchdown passes in a game for the first time in his NFL career as he led the Steelers to a win in the debut of new Steelers head coach [[Mike Tomlin]].<ref>{{cite web |date=September 10, 2007 |title=Roethlisberger throws 4 TDs |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/os-xpm-2007-09-10-nflcle10-story.html |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=OrlandoSentinel.com |archive-date=January 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116221546/https://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/os-xpm-2007-09-10-nflcle10-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Against the [[2007 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]] in Week 4, Roethlisberger looked to get a win over his former offensive coordinator [[Ken Whisenhunt]], who was then the head coach of the Cardinals. However, Roethlisberger had his first loss of the season as he was intercepted twice; once in the red zone, and then on a desperation pass with six seconds left in the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Arizona Cardinals – September 30th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200709300crd.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=June 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606011312/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200709300crd.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Ben Roethlisberger throwback.jpg|thumb|left|Roethlisberger in a Steelers' throwback jersey during 500th franchise win]]
In Week 9 against the [[2007 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], Roethlisberger passed for a career-high five touchdown passes, which tied the team record held by [[Terry Bradshaw]] and [[Mark Malone]]. All five touchdowns were thrown in the first half, making Roethlisberger one of two quarterbacks in the [[2007 NFL season|2007 season]] (the other being Tom Brady), and only the fifth quarterback since the [[NFL-AFL merger|1970 merger]], to accomplish such a feat. He also posted a perfect 158.3 [[passer rating]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers – November 5th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711050pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703145913/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711050pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Against the Browns in Week 10, Roethlisberger helped the Steelers erase a 15-point deficit against the rival Browns in a 31–28 victory. He passed for 278 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception to earn AFC Offensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers – November 11th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711110pit.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328201229/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711110pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2007 NFL Week 10 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/week_10.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328201236/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/week_10.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 12 against the [[2007 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]], Roethlisberger set a Steelers record, completing 85.7% of his passes (18 of 21) as the Steelers beat the Miami Dolphins, 3–0—a feat made all the more remarkable given the weather conditions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at Pittsburgh Steelers – November 26th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711260pit.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184459/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711260pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Pittsburgh]] was hit with a torrential storm, delaying the Monday night game 30 minutes due to lightning, while turning the new sod on the field, laid earlier that week, into a soggy mess. In many parts of the field, players sunk several inches with each step. After one of the game's punts, the ball infamously stood straight up, stuck in the ground upon impact. With the game scoreless in the fourth quarter, Roethlisberger led a game-winning field goal drive for the only points of the night.<ref>{{cite news |date=November 27, 2007 |title=Steelers win mud wrestling battle, 3–0 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/27/sports/27iht-NFL.1.8493504.html |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=The New York Times |archive-date=September 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190922234347/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/27/sports/27iht-NFL.1.8493504.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Roethlisberger threw his 29th touchdown pass of the season in Week 15 against the [[2007 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]], breaking the team single-season touchdown pass record previously held by Bradshaw.<ref>{{cite news |date=December 16, 2007 |title=Garrard's 3 TD passes, Taylor's running lead weatherproof Jaguars past Steelers 29–22 |url=http://www.espn.com/espn/wire/_/section/nfl/id/3157367 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021141101/http://www.espn.com/espn/wire/_/section/nfl/id/3157367 |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 16 against the [[2007 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]], Roethlisberger became the first quarterback in NFL history to have two perfect passer rating (158.3) games in the same regular season, completing 16 of 20 passes for 261 yards and three touchdowns. It was his third career-perfect passer rating game, tying Peyton Manning for the most such regular-season games in NFL history.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dulac |first=Gerry |date=December 27, 2007 |title=Steelers' Roethlisberger named player of the week |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/steelers/2007/12/27/Steelers-Roethlisberger-named-player-of-the-week/stories/200712270270 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |archive-date=October 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031163227/https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/steelers/2007/12/27/Steelers-Roethlisberger-named-player-of-the-week/stories/200712270270 |url-status=live }}</ref> He earned his second AFC Offensive Player of the Week nod for the 2007 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=2007 NFL Week 16 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/week_16.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328201227/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/week_16.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

To cap his comeback season, Roethlisberger was selected to his first Pro Bowl, joining five other Steelers teammates on the AFC squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=2007 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/probowl.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316023313/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/probowl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger's 32 touchdown passes ranked third in the NFL, behind [[Tony Romo]] and Tom Brady, while his 104.1 passer rating was second only to Brady.<ref>{{cite web |title=2007 NFL Passing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/passing.htm |access-date=December 6, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200420205126/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/passing.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger also set a new Steelers single-season record with 32 touchdown passes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers Single-Season Passing Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/single-season-passing.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184421/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/single-season-passing.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In a rematch of the Week 15 game, the Steelers were defeated by the Jaguars in the AFC [[2007–08 NFL playoffs#AFC: Jacksonville Jaguars 31, Pittsburgh Steelers 29|Wild Card Round]], 31–29. In the loss, Roethlisberger passed for 337 yards, two touchdowns, and three interceptions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wild Card – Jacksonville Jaguars at Pittsburgh Steelers – January 5th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801050pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412065305/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801050pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger finished third in Comeback Player of the Year voting, behind the Patriots' [[Randy Moss]] and the Dallas Cowboys' [[Greg Ellis (American football)|Greg Ellis]], who won the award.<ref>{{cite news |date=January 12, 2008 |title=Ellis makes impact even after Achilles tendon tear, position change |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3193239 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=April 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190428122209/http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3193239 |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger played in his first [[Pro Bowl]] in Hawaii.<ref>{{cite web |title=2008 Pro Bowl Game Summary |url=http://www.nfl.com/liveupdate/gamecenter/29527/NFC_Gamebook.pdf |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=October 31, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081031031012/http://www.nfl.com/liveupdate/gamecenter/29527/NFC_Gamebook.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===2008: Second Super Bowl championship===
{{See also|2008 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
[[File:Roethlisberger warm-up 2008.jpg|thumb|Roethlisberger in 2008 prior to a game against the [[Tennessee Titans]]]]
On March 4, 2008, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Roethlisberger agreed to an eight-year, $102 million contract.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bouchette |first=Ed |date=March 4, 2008 |title=Steelers break bank for Big Ben |work=Pittsburgh Post Gazette |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/2008/03/04/Steelers-break-bank-for-Big-Ben/stories/200803040247 |access-date=December 11, 2011 |archive-date=November 6, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131106024103/http://www.post-gazette.com/sports/2008/03/04/Steelers-break-bank-for-Big-Ben/stories/200803040247 |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger had two years left on his original that he signed after the draft. He stated at the time that he wanted to retire as a Steeler.<ref>{{cite web |last=Prisuta |first=Mike |date=January 16, 2008 |title=Roethlisberger wants to stick with Steelers |url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/s_547648.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081005184743/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/s_547648.html |archive-date=October 5, 2008 |access-date=December 11, 2011 |publisher=Pittsburghlive.com}}</ref>

In Week 1 against the [[2008 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]], Roethlisberger completed 13 of 14 passes for a career-high 92.9 completion percentage (minimum 10 attempts), and finished with 137 yards passing and two touchdown passes in the 38–17 win. [[Byron Leftwich]] took over in the fourth quarter when Roethlisberger was on the sideline with a shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Scott |date=September 8, 2008 |title=Steelers pummel Texans, 38–17 |url=https://archive.triblive.com/news/steelers-pummel-texans-38-17/ |access-date=December 7, 2019 |website=TribLIVE.com |archive-date=December 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207195424/https://archive.triblive.com/news/steelers-pummel-texans-38-17/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The next week against the [[2008 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], he had the first pass reception of his career: a negative-seven-yard completion to himself after a deflected pass in the second quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns – September 14th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809140cle.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301074429/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809140cle.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In a 15–6 loss to the [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 3, Roethlisberger was sacked eight times, fumbled twice, threw one interception, and was called for a safety in the fourth quarter. He did not finish the game, as his throwing hand was injured.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles – September 21st, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809210phi.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021120003/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809210phi.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Bouchette |first=Ed |date=September 22, 2008 |title=Roethlisberger is blitzed, bothered and battered by Philadelphia's hungry defense |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/2008/09/22/Roethlisberger-is-blitzed-bothered-and-battered-by-Philadelphia-s-hungry-defense/stories/200809220164 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |archive-date=October 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031230949/https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/2008/09/22/Roethlisberger-is-blitzed-bothered-and-battered-by-Philadelphia-s-hungry-defense/stories/200809220164 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 4 against the [[2008 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], the Steelers trailed 13–3 at halftime. Roethlisberger threw a touchdown pass to [[Santonio Holmes]] in the third quarter to start a comeback. He completed two passes to [[Mewelde Moore]] for 31 yards in overtime, setting up Jeff Reed for the winning 46-yard field goal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers – September 29th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809290pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703150552/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809290pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The next week, Roethlisberger threw for 239 yards in the first half—a career-high for one half—and directed the game-winning drive, passing for an eight-yard touchdown to Hines Ward to defeat the [[2008 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] by a score of 26–21.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 6, 2008 |title=Big Ben leads Steelers past Jags |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d80b64ac2/printable/quick-take-big-ben-leads-steelers-past-jags |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207195441/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d80b64ac2/printable/quick-take-big-ben-leads-steelers-past-jags |archive-date=December 7, 2019 |access-date=December 7, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week and the [[FedEx Air & Ground NFL Players of the Week|FedEx Air Player of the Week]] for his performance.<ref>{{cite web |title=2008 NFL Week 5 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/week_5.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190326222413/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/week_5.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>
[[File:Ben Roethlisberger MNF 2008.jpg|thumb|left|Roethlisberger during a 2008 game]]

Roethlisberger had one of the worst performances of his career in a Week 9 23–6 win over the [[2008 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]], posting career lows in passer rating (15.1), completions (5), passing yards (50), yards per attempt (2.94) and completion percentage (29.4%).<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Washington Redskins – November 3rd, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200811030was.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703150418/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200811030was.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 13 at [[2008 New England Patriots season|New England]], in consistent rain, Roethlisberger completed 17 of 33 passes for 179 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. After falling behind, 10–3, in the second quarter, Roethlisberger led the Steelers to 30 unanswered points in a 33–10 victory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at New England Patriots – November 30th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200811300nwe.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703151241/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200811300nwe.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Against the [[2008 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] in Week 14, Roethlisberger had his 49th victory as a starting quarterback, breaking the record for the most wins by a quarterback in their first five NFL seasons.<ref name="dallasnews.com">{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=David |date=December 7, 2008 |title=It's sweet 16 comebacks for Pittsburgh's Roethlisberger |url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/football/cowboys/stories/120808dnspomoore.3dea36e.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100908115817/http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/football/cowboys/stories/120808dnspomoore.3dea36e.html |archive-date=September 8, 2010 |website=The Dallas Morning News}}</ref> The Steelers clinched the AFC North in Week 15 with a win over the Baltimore Ravens,<ref>{{cite web |date=December 14, 2008 |title=Steelers clinch AFC North, secure first-round bye |url=https://www.tribdem.com/sports/national_sports/steelers-clinch-afc-north-secure-first-round-bye/article_2f18b07c-7cde-5ab7-8a78-8f523040b4d7.html |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=The Tribune-Democrat |archive-date=September 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924092904/https://www.tribdem.com/sports/national_sports/steelers-clinch-afc-north-secure-first-round-bye/article_2f18b07c-7cde-5ab7-8a78-8f523040b4d7.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and with a loss to the [[2008 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] the following week clinched the No. 2 seed in the playoffs. The Steelers defeated the [[2008 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] in the [[2008–09 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 35, San Diego Chargers 24|Divisional Round]] and the Baltimore Ravens in the [[2008–09 NFL playoffs#AFC Championship: Pittsburgh Steelers 23, Baltimore Ravens 14|AFC Championship]] en route to the Super Bowl.<ref>{{cite web |title=Divisional Round – San Diego Chargers at Pittsburgh Steelers – January 11th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200901110pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=September 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921064557/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200901110pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=AFC Championship – Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers – January 18th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200901180pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703140608/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200901180pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Steelers last play 2008.jpg|thumb|Roethlisberger (7) kneeling out the win for the Steelers in Super Bowl XLIII]]
In [[Super Bowl XLIII]] against the [[2008 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], Roethlisberger led the Steelers to one of the most dramatic victories in Super Bowl history. On the first two offensive drives, Roethlisberger passed for 122 yards on seven of eight passing attempts, which was one yard shy of his total amount from his first Super Bowl start. The Steelers led, 10–0, and went into halftime up, 17–7. The lead grew to 20–7 before Arizona mounted a comeback. Trailing for the first time in the game, 23–20, with 2:30 remaining in the game, Roethlisberger took the field to start the winning drive. After a holding penalty on the first play, Roethlisberger marched the Steelers 88 yards in eight plays, connecting with the game's MVP, Santonio Holmes, four times for 73 yards on the drive, including the six-yard touchdown pass that put the Steelers ahead with 0:35 remaining.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=The 100 Greatest Moments in Sports History – The Steelers Are Super! |url=http://www.si.com/specials/100-greatest/?q=28-the-steelers-are-super |access-date=September 17, 2019 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |archive-date=June 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190618085443/https://www.si.com/specials/100-greatest/?q=28-the-steelers-are-super |url-status=dead }}</ref> After a [[LaMarr Woodley]] strip sack and a fumble recovery by [[Brett Keisel]], Roethlisberger and the Steelers offense went back on the field to kneel the ball and run the clock out, ensuring Pittsburgh's victory. Overall, Roethlisberger finished 21 of 30 for 256 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. He had a passer rating of 93.2.<ref>{{cite web |title=Super Bowl XLIII – Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Arizona Cardinals – February 1st, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200902010crd.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=September 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921064548/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200902010crd.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2009===
{{See also|2009 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
In Week 3 against the [[2009 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]], the Steelers were dominant in the first half and led, 20–9, in the fourth quarter, but the defense surrendered the lead with 14 seconds left. Roethlisberger got the ball back with two seconds remaining and his Hail Mary attempt was incomplete. It was his first NFL loss in the state of Ohio, snapping an 11–0 record.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals – September 27th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200909270cin.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 2, 2019 season|Kansas City Chiefs]], he had thrown for 398 yards and three touchdowns before leaving the game in overtime after taking a knee to the helmet on a scramble attempt.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 23, 2009 |title=Roethlisberger hurt as Steelers stunned by Chiefs |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2009/nov/23/roethlisberger-hurt-as-steelers-stunned-by-chiefs/ |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=The Washington Times |archive-date=October 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024190710/https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2009/nov/23/roethlisberger-hurt-as-steelers-stunned-by-chiefs/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Kansas City Chiefs – November 22nd, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200911220kan.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football suffered the fourth concussion of his NFL career.<ref>{{cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=June 9, 2013 |title=Was Big Ben's benching after '09 concussion right call? |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/was-big-ben-s-benching-after-09-concussion-right-call-0ap1000000210371 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=January 10, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110031932/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000210371/article/was-big-bens-benching-after-09-concussion-right-call |url-status=live }}</ref> After sitting out the overtime loss in Week 12 at [[2009 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore]], Roethlisberger started against the [[2009 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] in Week 13 and passed for 278 yards and two touchdown passes. He threw a go-ahead touchdown pass to Hines Ward with 1:56 remaining, only to have the Raiders answer back with a winning touchdown with nine seconds left. The Steelers could not hold three leads in the fourth quarter. They led 10–6, 17–13 and 24–20. It was the fifth loss of the season in which they surrendered the lead in the final quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 6th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912060pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=June 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200602095545/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912060pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On a frigid Thursday night in Cleveland in Week 14, Roethlisberger was sacked 8 times and did not lead a touchdown drive in his first career loss to Cleveland, ending a perfect 10–0 record against the rival Browns. It is the first time he lost four straight starts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns – December 10th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912100cle.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703145937/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912100cle.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 15 against the [[2009 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], Roethlisberger broke several franchise passing records in ending the five-game losing streak for the Steelers with the biggest passing day in franchise history. His first pass of the day was a 60-yard touchdown to Mike Wallace, and his last pass was a game-winning 19-yard touchdown to Wallace on the final play of the game. He passed for 503 yards, three touchdowns, and had no turnovers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Alan |date=December 21, 2009 |title=Steelers' Roethlisberger throws for team record 503 yards |url=https://helenair.com/sports/steelers-roethlisberger-throws-for-team-record-503-yards/article_4ee44ab8-ee64-11de-b993-001cc4c03286.html |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=Helena Independent Record |language=en |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=May 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220502161027/https://helenair.com/sports/steelers-roethlisberger-throws-for-team-record-503-yards/article_4ee44ab8-ee64-11de-b993-001cc4c03286.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He broke Terry Bradshaw's single-season record of 3,724 passing yards, and set a new mark for single-season completions (302). After leading a FG drive to take a 30–28 lead, the defense again surrendered the lead and the Steelers trailed, 36–30. Roethlisberger used all 2:01 he had left to drive the team 86 yards for the winning touchdown with no time remaining.<ref>{{cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 20th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912200pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=August 29, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829075324/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912200pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger was named AFC Player of the Week for his effort; the fifth time he has won that award in his career.<ref>{{cite web |title=2009 NFL Week 15 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/week_15.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327184552/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/week_15.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 16 against the Baltimore Ravens, Roethlisberger's 259-yard effort helped him become the first quarterback in franchise history to pass for over 4,000 yards in a single season. With the game tied at 20 in the final quarter, he led the Steelers on the game-winning field goal drive as they improved to 8–7.<ref>{{cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 27th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912270pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703153430/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912270pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Roethlisberger finished the season with 4,328 yards and 26 touchdown passes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Roethlisberger 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2009 |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184508/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was 9–6 as a starter and his 100.5 passer rating was the second time in his career he had a season with a rating over 100. He was sacked 50 times in 2009. Despite the three game win streak to end the season, the Steelers did not make the playoffs after tie-breakers eliminated them. Roethlisberger was voted as team MVP by the Steelers for the first time in his career.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Miami Dolphins – January 3rd, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001030mia.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=April 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420085407/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001030mia.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He was selected as the first alternate to the Pro Bowl, but declined the invitation to rest his right shoulder which was injured in the Miami game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Walker |first=James |date=January 20, 2010 |title='Big Ben' declined Pro Bowl invite |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/afcnorth/post/_/id/8767/big-ben-declined-pro-bowl-invite |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412095034/http://www.espn.com/blog/afcnorth/post/_/id/8767/big-ben-declined-pro-bowl-invite |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2010: Third Super Bowl appearance===
{{See also|2010 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
In Week 6 against the [[2010 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], after being suspended for the first four games of the season under the NFL player conduct policy, Roethlisberger returned to the Steelers. In his first game of the season he completed 16 of 27 passes for 258 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers – October 17th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010170pit.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703150004/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010170pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 7 against the [[2010 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]], with the Steelers trailing, 22–20, with 2:37 remaining in the game, Roethlisberger was at the center of controversy when he ran a QB draw and dove for the end zone, appearing to score a touchdown in the process. The play was ruled a touchdown on the field, but reviews showed Roethlisberger had fumbled short of the end zone. However, the review failed to provide conclusive evidence as to who recovered the ball after the fumble. By rule, possession was given to Pittsburgh, resulting in the game-winning field goal. Roethlisberger passed for 302 yards and 2 touchdowns in the game. "Just a bizarre kind of play. You hate to win it that way, but you'll take a win," Roethlisberger said.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Miami Dolphins – October 24th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010240mia.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327011149/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010240mia.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 25, 2010 |title=Roethlisberger fumble ends up not costing Steelers in win |url=https://www.pennlive.com/patriotnewssports/2010/10/roethlisberger_fumble_ends_up.html |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=pennlive.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=May 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220501212449/https://www.pennlive.com/patriotnewssports/2010/10/roethlisberger_fumble_ends_up.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
