In his first win over the [[2010 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] in Week 11, Roethlisberger passed for 275 yards and three touchdowns, and rushed for a career-high 55 yards and a<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2010 |title=Steelers QB Roethlisberger recovering from broken nose |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d81cbe75a/article/steelers-qb-roethlisberger-recovering-from-broken-nose |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322155039/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d81cbe75a/article/steelers-qb-roethlisberger-recovering-from-broken-nose |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |access-date=March 22, 2019 |website=NFL.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> touchdown. Celebrating a second-quarter touchdown pass, Roethlisberger was punched in the face by Raiders' defensive lineman [[Richard Seymour]], who was then ejected.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2010 |title=Ben Roethlisberger Punched in the Face in Game |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ben-roethlisberger-punched-in-the-face-in-game/ |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=CBS News |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023063534/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ben-roethlisberger-punched-in-the-face-in-game/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger was questionable to start the Week 13 game against the [[2010 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] with a foot injury, but did start the game and suffered a broken nose on the first series after a hit to the face from [[Haloti Ngata]]. Trailing 10–6 in the fourth quarter, Roethlisberger threw a go-ahead touchdown pass to [[Isaac Redman]] with 2:51 remaining and the Steelers held on for the 13–10 win as he finished with 253 yards passing.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Baltimore Ravens – December 5th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201012050rav.htm |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322231907/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201012050rav.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 17 against the Cleveland Browns, the Steelers clinched the AFC North and the #2 seed in the AFC playoffs. In the 41–9 victory, he finished with 280 passing yards and two touchdowns to earn AFC Offensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns – January 2nd, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201101020cle.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=November 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110080401/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201101020cle.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2010 NFL Week 17 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/week_17.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328201240/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/week_17.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the season with a 9–3 record in 12 starts, passing for 3,200 yards, 17 touchdowns and a career-low five interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bruno |first=Joseph |date=January 4, 2011 |title=Pittsburgh Steelers 2010: A Look Back At Their 12–4 Season |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/561575-pittsburgh-steelers-a-look-back-at-their-12-4-season |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en |archive-date=October 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020005147/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/561575-pittsburgh-steelers-a-look-back-at-their-12-4-season |url-status=live }}</ref>

Late in the first quarter of the AFC [[2010–11 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 31, Baltimore Ravens 24|Divisional Round]] against the Baltimore Ravens, Roethlisberger was sacked and fumbled the ball, and after both teams thought the pass was incomplete, it was eventually picked up by [[Cory Redding]] for a Baltimore touchdown. The Steelers trailed, 21–7, in the third quarter before Roethlisberger completed touchdown passes to Heath Miller and Hines Ward to tie the game at 21. With just over two minutes left, the game was tied, 24–24, and the Steelers faced a 3rd and 19. Roethlisberger completed a deep pass to rookie wide receiver [[Antonio Brown]] for 58 yards and Rashard Mendenhall's rushing touchdown put the Steelers ahead for good, 31–24, with 1:33 left. It was Roethlisberger's third game-winning drive in a playoff game. He finished with 19 completions on 32 attempts for 226 yards and 2 touchdown passes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 15, 2011 |title=Steelers Beat Ravens 31–24 in AFC Playoffs |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/steelers-beat-ravens-31-24-in-afc-playoffs/ |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=CBS News |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025094624/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/steelers-beat-ravens-31-24-in-afc-playoffs/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the [[2010–11 NFL playoffs#AFC: New York Jets 28, New England Patriots 21|AFC Championship]] against the [[2010 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], Roethlisberger rushed for a touchdown in the first half as the Steelers built a 24–0 lead, before the Jets scored 19 unanswered points. With two minutes remaining in the game, Roethlsiberger faced a 3rd and 6. He scrambled right and completed a 14-yard pass to Antonio Brown to seal the victory for Pittsburgh, sending them to their third Super Bowl appearance in the last six seasons. Roethlisberger completed 10 of 19 passes for a season-low 133 yards and two interceptions in the 28–21 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 23, 2011 |title=Steelers 24, Jets 19: Pittsburgh to face Packers in Super Bowl |url=https://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=51106291&itype=CMSID |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=The Salt Lake Tribune |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025225231/https://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=51106291&itype=CMSID |url-status=live }}</ref>

In [[Super Bowl XLV]] against the [[2010 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], Roethlisberger was hit as he attempted a pass to Mike Wallace in the first quarter, and it was intercepted for a touchdown by [[Nick Collins]]. The Steelers trailed, 21–3, in the second quarter before Roethlisberger completed a touchdown pass to Hines Ward to make it 21–10 at halftime. The Steelers closed to within 21–17 in the third quarter, but were unable to score on their next three drives. After falling behind, 28–17, in the fourth quarter, Roethlisberger threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Mike Wallace, and then pitched the ball to Antwaan Randle El on an [[option run]] for the two-point conversion to make it 28–25. Taking over at his own 13 with 1:59 left and down 31–25, Roethlisberger was unable to lead the game-winning drive against Green Bay this time after his pass fell incomplete to Wallace on 4th and 5 at his own 33-yard line, ensuring the only Super Bowl loss of his career. Roethlisberger finished the 31–25 loss 25 of 40 for 263 yards, 2 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. "I feel like I let the city of Pittsburgh down, the fans, my coaches and my teammates," Roethlisberger said, "and it's not a good feeling."<ref>{{cite web |last=Cimini |first=Rich |date=February 6, 2011 |title=Super Bowl XLV: Clock strikes midnight for Pittsburgh Steelers |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/playoffs/2010/columns/story?columnist=cimini_rich&id=6097547 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=October 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211006080338/https://www.espn.com/nfl/playoffs/2010/columns/story?columnist=cimini_rich&id=6097547 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the off-season, he was ranked 41st by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2011]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2011 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2011-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308170627/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2011-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2011===
{{See also|2011 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
[[File:Pro Bowl 2012 120129-M-DX861-089 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Roethlisberger at his second [[Pro Bowl]] in 2011]]
In Week 1 against the [[2011 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], Roethlisberger set career-worsts for turnovers (5) and largest margin of defeat (28) in his first loss against the Ravens since 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2011 |title=Flacco, Rice, Ravens D lead easy win over Steelers |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/recap/NFL_20110911_PIT@BAL |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111018050956/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/recap/NFL_20110911_PIT@BAL |archive-date=October 18, 2011 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> In Week 2 against the [[2011 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], he became the fourth quarterback to reach 70 wins in his first 100 starts, as he threw for 298 yards and did not turn the ball over. He took a shot to his right knee in the second quarter, but returned after missing two plays to finish the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Today, Week 2 – NFL |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/15602868/nfl-today-week-2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306132929/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/15602868/nfl-today-week-2 |archive-date=March 6, 2012 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

In a 23–20 Week 3 win against the [[2011 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], Roethlisberger threw for a career-high 171 yards in the first quarter, turned the ball over three times in the second quarter, then led the Steelers to the 20th fourth quarter comeback of his career, passing Terry Bradshaw for the most in Steelers' history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2011 |title=Steelers overcome turnovers, edge Colts on late FG |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/recap/NFL_20110925_PIT@IND |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111018051405/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/recap/NFL_20110925_PIT@IND |archive-date=October 18, 2011 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> In Week 5 against the [[2011 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]], Roethlisberger threw five touchdown passes for the second time in his career. He earned AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors for the seventh time in his career.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hensley |first=Jamison |date=October 12, 2011 |title=Roethlisberger named AFC Player of Week |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/afcnorth/post/_/id/33254 |access-date=July 1, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=July 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190701224740/https://www.espn.com/blog/afcnorth/post/_/id/33254 |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 7 against the [[2011 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], Roethlisberger set the franchise record for longest pass with a 95-yard touchdown pass to Mike Wallace. He finished with 361 yards and 3 touchdowns in his first regular season win over the Cardinals.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 23, 2011 |title=Big Ben throws longest pass in Steelers history in win |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/recap/NFL_20111023_PIT@ARI |url-status=dead 2019 |website=CBSSports.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

In the second quarter of the Week 14 game against the [[2011 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], Roethlisberger's leg was injured on a sack and he left the game. He returned for the second half and played the rest of the game, despite limping on his high-ankle sprain. He threw a game-clinching 79-yard touchdown pass to Antonio Brown late in the fourth quarter as the Steelers won 14–3. Roethlisberger finished with 280 yards passing on just 21 attempts for a career-high 13.33 YPA (min. 15 attempts).<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2011 |title=Roethlisberger Leads Steelers Over Browns, 14–3 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/12/09/sports/football/nfl-football-roundup.html |access-date=December 17, 2019 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217214628/https://www.nytimes.com/2011/12/09/sports/football/nfl-football-roundup.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On the injury, Roethlisberger said, "It was one of the most painful things I ever felt. It felt like the middle of my leg was just, cracked ... it felt like my foot was outside of my leg."<ref>{{cite web |last=Graves |first=Will |date=December 9, 2011 |title=Roethlisberger hurt, Steelers hold off Browns 14–3 |url=http://www.newstribune.com/news/news/story/2011/dec/09/roethlisberger-hurt-steelers-hold-browns-14-3/560725/ |access-date=December 17, 2019 |website=Tucson.com |language=en |archive-date=December 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218045034/https://www.newstribune.com/news/news/story/2011/dec/09/roethlisberger-hurt-steelers-hold-browns-14-3/560725/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 15 against the San Francisco 49ers, Roethlisberger started the game while suffering through a high-ankle sprain. During the game, it was clear that Roethlisberger was still showing signs of the injury due to him limping between plays. He finished the game without any touchdowns, but had 330 yards passing while throwing three interceptions.<ref>{{cite web |last=McCauley |first=Jamie |date=December 20, 2011 |title=49ers beat Big Ben, Steelers 20–3 |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-49ers-beat-big-ben-steelers-20-3-2011dec19-story.html |access-date=December 17, 2019 |website=San Diego Union-Tribune |language=en-US |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217214628/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-49ers-beat-big-ben-steelers-20-3-2011dec19-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Due to Roethlisberger's leg injury from Week 14, the team opted to sit him and start Charlie Batch in the Week 16 game against the [[2011 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]], giving Roethlisberger more time to recover.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 24, 2011 |title=Rashard Mendenhall, Charlie Batch lead Steelers past hapless Rams |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=311224023 |access-date=November 22, 2012 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=November 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116062634/http://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=311224023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Week 17 against the Cleveland Browns, just three weeks after the Browns injured Roethlisberger in Pittsburgh, Roethlisberger once again took the field to face the same opponents in their home stadium. The Steelers opted to start Roethlisberger over Batch because of the possibility that Baltimore could drop its final game, and a win by the Steelers would take back the division title. Despite his injury, Mike Tomlin and the coaching staff believed Roethlisberger gave them their best chance at victory. Big Ben completed 23 of 40 passes for 221 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. Baltimore went on to win their final game and secured the division title, leaving Steelers with the number 5 seed to face Denver in the Wild Card round of the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schefter |first=Adam |date=January 1, 2012 |title=Isaac Redman steps in, rushes for TD as Steelers get past Browns |url=http://espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320101005 |access-date=November 22, 2012 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=November 1, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121101065628/http://espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320101005 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the [[2011–12 NFL playoffs#AFC: Denver Broncos 29, Pittsburgh Steelers 23 (OT)|Wild Card Round]] against the [[2011 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]], Roethlisberger and the Steelers offense battled a tough Denver defense, trailing 20–6 at the half, but tying it at 23–23 before the end of regulation. The game-tying touchdown came on a 2nd and 10 with 3:47 remaining in regulation, where Big Ben made a vintage play eluding pass rushers before connecting with Jerricho Cotchery on a 31-yard pass. Despite the heroic efforts of Roethlisberger and company, [[Tim Tebow]]'s magical season continued with his best single-game performance to date, capped off with an 80-yard completion to [[Demaryius Thomas]] to end overtime after one play. Roethlisberger completed 22 of 40 passes for 289 yards, with 1 touchdown and 1 interception in the 29–23 overtime loss to end the 2011 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 8, 2012 |title=Tim Tebow rediscovers magic as Broncos oust stunned Steelers in OT |url=http://espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320108007 |access-date=November 22, 2012 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=August 9, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120809184605/http://espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320108007 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was named to the Pro Bowl for the 2011 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=2011 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/probowl.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=August 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180830174119/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/probowl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished ranked 30th by his peers on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2012]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2012-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211112163739/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2012-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2012===
{{See also|2012 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
[[File:Ben Roethlisberger 2012 September.JPG|thumb|upright|left|Roethlisberger in [[Empower Field at Mile High|Denver]] for the season opener in September 2012]]
Roethlisberger threw for 3,265 yards, 26 touchdowns, and 8 interceptions in thirteen games as the Steelers finished the 2012 season with an 8–8 record.<ref>{{cite web |last=Crabtree |first=Curtis |date=May 30, 2013 |title=Ben Roethlisberger had input in Steelers' offensive changes |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/05/30/ben-roethlisberger-had-input-in-steelers-offensive-changes/ |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=ProFootballTalk |archive-date=October 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027215302/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/05/30/ben-roethlisberger-had-input-in-steelers-offensive-changes/ |url-status=live }}</ref> One of his best individual games in the 2012 season came against the [[2012 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] in Week 3. He had 384 passing yards and four touchdowns in the 34–31 loss.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=September 23, 2012 |title=Pittsburgh Steelers' defense on alert after latest loss |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/pittsburgh-steelers-defense-on-alert-after-latest-loss-0ap1000000065252 |access-date=December 7, 2019 |website=NFL.com |language=en |archive-date=December 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207195430/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000065252/article/pittsburgh-steelers-defense-on-alert-after-latest-loss |url-status=live }}</ref> He missed three games due to injury, being replaced by Byron Leftwich, who went 0–1, and Charlie Batch, who went 1–1. It was the Steelers first season missing the playoffs since 2009 and their first with a non-winning record since 2006.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Roethlisberger 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=December 16, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=December 17, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171217014911/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2012/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished ranked 61st by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2013]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2013-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220409042306/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2013-nfl-top-100.htm |archive-date=April 9, 2022 |access-date=May 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2012, Roethlisberger returned to Miami University to complete his college degree, graduating with a [[Bachelor of Science in Education]] on May 6, 2012. Roethlisberger walked with the other graduates at the commencement ceremony, with his parents, grandmother, and wife Ashley in attendance.<ref name="Graduation">{{Cite web |last=Lopresti |first=Mike |date=May 7, 2012 |title=Steelers QB Ben Roethlisberger graduates at 30, wins 'Super Bowl in life' |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/football/nfl/article/1173956--steelers-quarterback-ben-roethlisberger-graduates-at-30-wins-super-bowl-in-life |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801060649/http://www.thestar.com/sports/football/nfl/article/1173956--steelers-quarterback-ben-roethlisberger-graduates-at-30-wins-super-bowl-in-life |archive-date=August 1, 2012 |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=The Star |location=Toronto}}</ref> He had planned on finishing his degree sooner, but the Steelers having deep playoff runs earlier in his career prevented him from registering for classes in time for the winter term, only being able to do it after the Steelers were eliminated in the Wild Card round against the [[Denver Broncos]] the previous season.<ref name="Graduation" /> Roethlisberger became the second member of the Steelers in less than a year to return to college and complete his degree, with teammate Polamalu doing the same thing the previous off-season during the [[2011 NFL lockout]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Moura |first=Pedro |date=May 14, 2011 |title=Troy Polamalu graduates from USC |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=6547248 |access-date=May 14, 2011 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=May 16, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516160753/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=6547248 |url-status=live }}</ref>

This season was particularly notable for Roethlisberger as it marked the beginning of the [[Killer B's (Pittsburgh)|Killer B's]] era. Roethlisberger, along with wide receiver [[Antonio Brown]], running back [[Le'Veon Bell]] and, later, kicker [[Chris Boswell]] all entered their primes.<ref name="d219">{{cite web | title=The Killer B's | website=Steelers.com | date=2017-11-27 | url=https://www.steelers.com/news/the-killer-b-s-19852434 | access-date=2025-01-10}}</ref> Roethlisberger finished the season seventh in passing yards, eighth in touchdowns, 10th in completion percentage and his 92.0 passer rating ranked 12th in the league for the 2013 season.<ref>{{cite web | title=2013 NFL passing statistics | website=NFL.com | url=https://www.nfl.com/stats/player-stats/category/passing/2013/reg/all/passingyards/desc | access-date=2026-01-02}}</ref> Roethlisberger targeted Brown in particular 165 times, resulting in 110 receptions for 1,499 yards and 8 touchdowns. This accounted for approximately 28% of Roethlisberger's 584 pass attempts that season.<ref name="x395">{{cite web | last=Fantasy | first=SB Nation | title=Antonio Brown Week 4 fantasy football recap | website=SBNation.com | date=2013-09-30 | url=https://www.sbnation.com/fantasy/2013/9/30/4784300/antonio-brown-fantasy-football-ben-roethlisberger-steelers-vs-vikings | access-date=2025-01-10}}</ref> Even though he was not a receiver and mainly fulfilled the role of being a "power back" in the Steelers' offense, Roethlisberger targeted Bell 66 times, resulting in 45 receptions for 399 yards, but recording no receiving touchdowns.<ref name="g429">{{cite web | title=Le'Veon Bell Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College | website=Pro-Football-Reference.com | date=1992-02-18 | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellLe00.htm | access-date=2025-01-10}}</ref>

===2014===
{{See also|2014 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
Roesthilsberger started the 2014 season with a 4–3 record in the first seven games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Roethlisberger 2014 Game Log (Games 1–7) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2014/#144-150-sum:stats |access-date=December 7, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218142050/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2014#144-150-sum:stats |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 26, 2014, against the [[2014 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], Roethlisberger completed 40 of 49 passes for a career-high 522 yards and six touchdowns as the Steelers defeated the [[Indianapolis Colts]] 51–34.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2014 |title=Roethlisberger throws 6 TDs as Steelers top Colts |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=400554310 |access-date=October 26, 2014 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 27, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141027052941/http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=400554310 |url-status=live }}</ref> With the win, Roethlisberger became just the fourth quarterback in NFL history to get 100 wins in his first 150 starts.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brady |first=James |date=October 26, 2014 |title=Ben Roethlisberger becomes 4th quarterback to get 100 wins in first 150 games |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2014/10/26/7070697/ben-roethlisberger-record-milestone-steelers |access-date=October 26, 2014 |website=SB Nation |archive-date=October 27, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141027192233/http://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2014/10/26/7070697/ben-roethlisberger-record-milestone-steelers |url-status=live }}</ref> He also became the first NFL quarterback to pass for over 500 yards twice in a career. He earned AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his effort against the Colts.<ref>{{cite web |title=2014 NFL Week 8 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/week_8.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317164720/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/week_8.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In the next game, a 43–23 victory over the [[2014 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], he had 340 passing yards and six passing touchdowns to earn AFC Offensive Player of the Week for the second consecutive week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2014 |title=Ben Roethlisberger's six TD passes lift Steelers over Ravens, 43–23 |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/nfl/la-sp-ravens-steelers-20141103-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111140740/https://www.latimes.com/sports/nfl/la-sp-ravens-steelers-20141103-story.html#:~:text=Ben%20Roethlisberger%20threw%20for%20340,Baltimore%20Ravens%20on%20Sunday%20night. |archive-date=November 11, 2017 |access-date=May 1, 2022 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2014 NFL Week 9 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/week_9.htm |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328201232/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/week_9.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the Steelers Week 15 matchup against the [[2014 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]], Roethlisberger completed 27 of 35 passes for 360 yards in a 27–20 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bryan |first=Dave |date=December 14, 2014 |title=Roethlisberger Sets New Franchise Passing Yardage Record, Joins 31-Club With Sunday Win |url=https://steelersdepot.com/2014/12/roethlisberger-sets-new-franchise-passing-yardage-record-joins-31-club-sunday-win/ |access-date=May 1, 2022 |website=Steelers Depot |language=en-US }}</ref> The victory made Roethlisberger only the sixth quarterback in NFL history to have defeated at least 31 different teams, joining Tom Brady, [[Drew Brees]], [[Kerry Collins]], [[Brett Favre]], and [[Peyton Manning]]; Roethlisberger has only played with one team and thus has not played against the Steelers. The Steelers lost 41–38 in Roethlisberger's only other matchup against Atlanta in 2006, and he was suspended for the Steelers 15–9 overtime victory against the Falcons in 2010.<ref name="31 teams" />

During 2014, Roethlisberger passed for career highs in yards with 4,952, completion percentage with 67.1, completions with 408, and attempts with 608. Roethlisberger also matched his career high in passing touchdowns with 32, as well as posting a passer rating of 103.3, the second highest of his career. His 4,952 yards were tied for most on the season with Drew Brees, but Roethlisberger reached the mark with fewer completions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Roethlisberger 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2014 |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001429/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2014 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2014 NFL Passing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/passing.htm |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115214627/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/passing.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Steelers had an 11–5 record and finished first in the AFC North.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 29, 2014 |title=Steelers clinch AFC North with win over Bengals ===2021===
{{See also|2021 Pittsburgh Steelers season}}
[[File:Ben Roethlisberger (51654815739) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Roethlisberger during his final season with the Steelers]]
Roethlisberger signed a renegotiated contract with the Steelers on March 4, 2021, that saw him take a $5 million pay cut.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=March 4, 2021 |title=Steelers sign new contract with Roethlisberger for 2021 season |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-new-contract-with-ben-roethlisberger-for-2021-season |access-date=March 8, 2021 |website=Steelers.com |archive-date=March 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310055957/https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-new-contract-with-ben-roethlisberger-for-2021-season |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 5, 2021 |title=Unlike Peyton Manning, Ben Roethlisberger's pay cut includes no ability to earn it back |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/03/05/unlike-peyton-manning-ben-roethlisbergers-pay-cut-includes-no-ability-to-earn-it-back/ |access-date=July 9, 2022 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref> Roethlisberger began his final season with a Week 1 victory over the [[2021 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. He scored his first touchdown of the season with a five yard pass to [[Diontae Johnson]]. It would be his only score of the game as he completed 18-of-32 passes for 188 yards and not committing any turnovers.<ref name="w425">{{cite web | title=Steelers 23-16 Bills (Sep 12, 2021) | website=StatMuse | date=2021-09-12 | url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/game/9-12-2021-pit-at-buf-16816 | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref> Despite losing 24–10 to division rivals, the [[2021 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]], Roethlisberger threw for a season high 318 yards, completed 38 out of 58 pass attempts and threw one touchdown pass against two interceptions. During October 10's 27–19 win over the [[2021 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]], Roethlisberger had his first multiple touchdown game of the year, opening the game with a 50 yard touchdown pass to Johnson and an 18 yard pass to [[Chase Claypool]].<ref name="a608">{{cite web | title=Broncos 19-27 Steelers (Oct 10, 2021) | website=StatMuse | date=2021-10-10 | url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/game/10-10-2021-den-at-pit-16882 | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref> This kickstarted a four game win streak for the Steelers. Across those four games, Roethlisberger threw for six touchdowns, committed no turnovers and completed 67%, (87 out of 129) pass attempts for 953 yards.<ref name="p331">{{cite web | title=Ben Roethlisberger 2021 Season | website=StatMuse | date=2022-01-09 | url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/ben-roethlisberger-2021-season | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref> The Steelers' streak was halted when, a day before the Week 10 game against the [[2021 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]], the Steelers placed Roethlisberger on Reserve/COVID-19 list after testing positive for the virus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lev |first=Jacob |date=November 13, 2021 |title=Pittsburgh Steelers QB Ben Roethlisberger placed on the reserve/Covid-19 list, ruled out for Sunday's game |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/11/13/sport/pittsburgh-steelers-ben-roethlisberger-reserve-list/index.html |access-date=November 15, 2021 |website=CNN.com |archive-date=November 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211114213327/https://www.cnn.com/2021/11/13/sport/pittsburgh-steelers-ben-roethlisberger-reserve-list/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=November 13, 2021 |title=Roethlisberger out for Sunday's game vs. Lions |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/roethlisberger-out-for-sunday-s-game-vs-lions |access-date=November 15, 2021 |website=Steelers.com |archive-date=November 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211115014922/https://www.steelers.com/news/roethlisberger-out-for-sunday-s-game-vs-lions |url-status=live }}</ref> He returned for November 21's 41–37 loss to the [[2021 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]] in which he threw for 273 yards and three touchdowns.

Roethlisberger played his final game at [[Heinz Field]] on January 3, 2022. Leading up to his final game, Roethlisberger's career was memorialized with [[ESPN]] hosting a countdown tribute.<ref name="k774">{{cite web | title=Tribute to Ben Rothlisberger before his last home game ever! | website=YouTube | date=2024-03-06 | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4BbO2qKAsME | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref> In his final home game, Roethlisberger threw for 123 yards, a touchdown and an interception, leading the team to a 26–14 victory over the [[2021 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] and eliminating them from playoff contention.<ref name="f705">{{cite web | title=Browns 14-26 Steelers (Jan 3, 2022) | website=StatMuse | date=2022-01-03 | url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/game/1-3-2022-cle-at-pit-17068 | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref> With his helmet still on, in full uniform, Roethlisberger gave an emotional interview after the game and was the last player to leave the field. This win officially cemented Roethlisberger with 164 career wins as a starter, which was the fifth-most in NFL history at the time and ending his record at Heinz Field with a win-loss record of 92–31, the fourth most home victories a quarterback has ever had with a single team in NFL history.<ref name="d016">{{cite web | last=Gordon | first=Grant | title=Steelers QB Ben Roethlisberger goes out a winner at Heinz Field: 'This is the best place to play' | website=NFL.com | date=2022-01-04 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-qb-ben-roethlisberger-goes-out-a-winner-at-heinz-field-this-is-the-best | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref>

Roethlisberger finished the 2021 regular season with 3,740 passing yards, 22 touchdowns, and ten interceptions, and also had an additional rushing touchdown as the Steelers finished with a 9–7–1 record, earning a spot in the [[2021-22 NFL playoffs|Wild card round]] as the seven seed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Roethlisberger 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=January 28, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128031127/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RoetBe00/gamelog/2021/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#AFC: Kansas City Chiefs 42, Pittsburgh Steelers 21|Wild Card Round]] against the [[2021 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]], Roethlisberger threw for 215 yards and two touchdowns in the 42–21 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=January 17, 2022 |title=Big Ben looks back after playoff loss to Chiefs: 'It was meant to be that I was going to wear black and gold' |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-qb-ben-roethlisberger-looks-back-after-playoff-loss-to-chiefs-it-was-me |access-date=January 17, 2022 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=January 17, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117060113/https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-qb-ben-roethlisberger-looks-back-after-playoff-loss-to-chiefs-it-was-me |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Retirement==

[[File:Hall of Honor inductees.jpg|thumb|Roethlisberger (far right) being inducted into the Steelers’ Hall of Honor during halftime on Monday Night Football in 2025]]

On January 27, 2022, Roethlisberger announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gordon|first=Grant|title=Steelers QB Ben Roethlisberger officially announces retirement after 18 seasons|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-qb-ben-roethlisberger-officially-announces-retirement-after-18-seasons|work=NFL.com|date=January 27, 2022|access-date=January 27, 2022|archive-date=January 27, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220127164453/https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-qb-ben-roethlisberger-officially-announces-retirement-after-18-seasons|url-status=live}}</ref>

After [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] quarterback [[Tom Brady]] unretired in March of that year, some wondered if Roethlisberger would also come back for another season. Roethlisberger was quick to silence those questions when he told [[WDVE]] in Pittsburgh, "First off, my coach and GM don't want me back. Second off, I'm pretty content with where I'm at."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ragan |first=Zach |date=April 28, 2022 |title=Ben Roethlisberger gives hilarious response to question about un-retiring |url=https://atozsports.com/pittsburgh/ben-roethlisberger-steelers-draft-news-return/ |access-date=January 20, 2024 |website=A to Z Sports |language=en}}</ref> In March 2023, Roethlisberger revealed to [[Mark Madden]] however that the [[San Francisco 49ers]] did show some interest after suffering injuries with [[Trey Lance]] and [[Jimmy Garoppolo]] left [[Brock Purdy]] as the starting quarterback, but Roethlisberger declined.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeArdo |first=Bryan |date=April 15, 2023 |title=Ben Roethlisberger clarifies what happened between him and the 49ers during the 2022 season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/ben-roethlisberger-clarifies-what-happened-between-him-and-the-49ers-during-the-2022-season/ |access-date=January 20, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> In February 2025, Roethlisberger mentioned on the [[Nate Bargatze]] podcast that the [[New York Jets]] reached out to him in 2023 after [[Aaron Rodgers]] tore his [[Achilles tendon]], which he promptly declined.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/steelers/news/afc-team-tried-unretire-pittsburgh-steelers-ben-roethlisberger |title=AFC Team Tried to Unretire Steelers' Ben Roethlisberger |magazine=Sports Illustrated |last=Strackbein |first=Noah |date=March 2, 2025 |access-date=March 20, 2025}}</ref>

Although the Steelers generally do not retire jersey numbers, having only retired the numbers of [[Joe Greene]] and [[Franco Harris]] (both from the Steelers dynasty years of the 1970s) since the team lifted its decades-long ban on retiring numbers in 2014 (with [[Ernie Stautner]] being the only other player with his number retired), the team has not reissued Roethlisberger's number 7 since his retirement.<ref name="z051">{{cite web | title=All Players To Wear Number 7 For Pittsburgh Steelers | website=Pro-Football-Reference.com | date=December 16, 2024 | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com:443/players/uniform.cgi?team=pit&number=7 | access-date=July 11, 2025}}</ref> It is generally understood that no Steeler will ever wear number 7 again.

===''Footbahlin with Ben Roethlisberger''===

The show eventually evolved into having guest interviews with current and former players and coaches such as [[Kenny Pickett]], [[Jerome Bettis]], [[Bill Cowher]] and [[Mike Tomlin]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2_g4Xowe1r8 | title=Big Ben & Kenny Pickett talk going into second year, ushering in a new era and so much more! Ep. 28 | website=[[YouTube]] | date=May 21, 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7VZOm3Z_gac | title=Big Ben and Jerome Bettis share SBXL stories, talk Notre Dame, infamous Indy fumble and more! EP. 36 | website=[[YouTube]] | date=September 24, 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pNOkc67Jqlg | title=Big Ben & Coach Cowher talk 2004 draft, SB XL, getting Jerome Bettis to return and more! Ep. 27 | website=[[YouTube]] | date=May 8, 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WNuxwK5-HTM | title=Big Ben & Mike Tomlin share SBXLIII stories, talk best defense Tomlin has coached, and more! Ep. 23 | website=[[YouTube]] | date=March 13, 2023 }}</ref> During the 2023 season, the show began to incorporate Roethlisberger and Te'o watching various Steeler games and providing commentary.

The final episode was uploaded on December 25, 2023, with an episode about the Steelers' victory over the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on [[Christmas Eve]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T-3Uyaxt-M8 | title=Big Ben recaps Steelers vs Bengals, talks Mason Rudolph & Christmas traditions Ep. 47 | website=[[YouTube]] | date=December 25, 2023 }}</ref> In an interview with WDVE in 2024, Roethlisberger claimed that the podcast would not continue. Despite this announcement, Roethlisberger uploaded a surprise teaser for another season of the podcast on August 29, 2024, to begin the following week. ===Motorcycle accident===
On June 12, 2006, Roethlisberger was involved in a motorcycle accident near downtown Pittsburgh. He was not wearing a helmet and did not have a valid Pennsylvania motorcycle license at the time, only a temporary permit that had expired in March.<ref name="NoLicense">{{cite web |last=Parsons |first=Jim |date=June 13, 2006 |title=Team 4: Questions Surround Roethlisberger's Motorcycle License – Pittsburgh News Story – WTAE Pittsburgh |url=http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/9364467/detail.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100901202533/http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/9364467/detail.html |archive-date=September 1, 2010 |access-date=December 11, 2011 |publisher=The Pittsburgh Channel}}</ref> Roethlisberger was traveling east on Second Avenue when a car turned in front of him at the [[South Tenth Street Bridge]], causing a collision.<ref name="benbridge">{{cite web |date=June 12, 2006 |title=Roethlisberger Undergoes Surgery After Bike Crash |url=http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/9356067/detail.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090603142732/http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/9356067/detail.html |archive-date=June 3, 2009 |access-date=December 11, 2011 |website=The Pittsburgh Channel}}</ref> According to eyewitnesses, Roethlisberger went over the handlebars of his bike, shattering the windshield of the car with his head.<ref name="benbike">{{cite web |last=Greenwood |first=Jill King |date=June 15, 2006 |title=Roethlisberger surgery called success |url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/steelers/s_457685.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060615005002/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/steelers/s_457685.html |archive-date=June 15, 2006 |access-date=May 22, 2020 |website=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review}}</ref><ref name="ESPNinjury">{{Cite web |last1=Pasquarelli |first1=Len |author-link=Len Pasquarelli |last2=Clayton |first2=John |author-link2=John Clayton (sportswriter) |date=June 12, 2006 |title=Big Ben in serious condition after motorcycle accident |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2480830 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160124123609/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=2480830 |archive-date=January 24, 2016 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Though initial reports described the injuries as non-life-threatening, Roethlisberger later said paramedics had to stop bleeding in his throat to save his life.<ref name="bencrash">{{cite web |title=Big Ben could be out of hospital by Thursday |url=http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/13279232 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060615011826/http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/13279232 |archive-date=June 15, 2006 |access-date=May 22, 2020 |website=MSNBC.com}}</ref> He was taken to [[Mercy Hospital (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania)|Mercy Hospital]] in "serious but stable" condition.<ref>{{cite news |date=June 13, 2006 |title=Steelers QB is 'serious but stable' |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/steelers-qb-is-serious-but-stable/article_26643252-3c2d-52f9-ac6c-fe9e1ff6f5eb.html |access-date=May 22, 2020 |website=The Quad-City Times |language=en |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=April 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220422180129/https://qctimes.com/sports/steelers-qb-is-serious-but-stable/article_26643252-3c2d-52f9-ac6c-fe9e1ff6f5eb.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Roethlisberger suffered significant facial injuries, including fractures to his jaw and [[sinus cavity]], a broken nose, a nine-inch head laceration, the loss of two teeth, and several chipped teeth.<ref name="bensurgery">{{cite web |title=Roethlisberger Undergoes Surgery, Still Hospitalized |url=http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/9356067/detail.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090603142732/http://www.thepittsburghchannel.com/news/9356067/detail.html |archive-date=June 3, 2009 |access-date=May 22, 2020 |website=The Pittsburgh Channel}}</ref> He underwent immediate surgery to repair the damage and was upgraded to fair condition the following day.<ref name=bencrash/><ref name="espn">{{cite news |date=June 14, 2006 |title=Roethlisberger likely to be able to play this season |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2482701 |access-date=December 11, 2011 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 20, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111020224659/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=2482701 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Branch |first=John |date=June 13, 2006 |title=Roethlisberger Is Seriously Injured in Motorcycle Wreck |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/06/13/sports/football/13steelers.html |access-date=May 22, 2020 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US |archive-date=January 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130124930/http://www.nytimes.com/2006/06/13/sports/football/13steelers.html |url-status=live }}</ref> A subsequent news conference with hospital staff was brief, but confirmed early reports that the most serious injuries were to the head and face. He was released from the hospital on June 14 and issued a public apology the next day, in which he also stated, "If I ever ride again, it certainly will be with a helmet."<ref>{{cite web |date=June 15, 2006 |title=Big Ben speaks out on accident, says he'll start wearing a helmet |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/06166/698658-100.stm |access-date=May 22, 2020 |website=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |archive-date=March 5, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090305150756/http://post-gazette.com/pg/06166/698658-100.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger was allegedly videotaped by [[KDKA-TV]] staff riding without a helmet a few months later, but the existence of said tape is disputed.<ref name="hangover">{{Cite magazine |last=McCallum |first=Jack |date=May 10, 2010 |title=The Hangover: Roethlisberger |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/vault/2010/05/10/105935652/the-hangover-roethlisberger |access-date=April 19, 2019 |archive-date=April 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420024228/https://www.si.com/vault/2010/05/10/105935652/the-hangover-roethlisberger |url-status=live }}</ref>

The driver of the other vehicle was cited for failure to yield the right of way.<ref name="benhelmet">{{cite web |last=Weisman |first=Larry |date=June 19, 2006 |title=Steelers' Roethlisberger to be cited for lack of license, helmet |url=https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/steelers/2006-06-19-roethlisberger-accident_x.htm |access-date=May 22, 2020 |website=USA TODAY |archive-date=April 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220422170909/https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/steelers/2006-06-19-roethlisberger-accident_x.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Sexual assault allegations===

====Lake Tahoe====
In July 2009, Andrea McNulty, 31, filed a civil lawsuit in the [[Washoe County, Nevada]] District Court, accusing  Roethlisberger of sexually assaulting her in June 2008 at his hotel room in [[Stateline, Nevada]], during a celebrity golf tournament.<ref name="ESPN">{{Cite web |date=March 8, 2010 |title=Woman in Georgia alleges assault |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4970050 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160123210926/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4970050 |archive-date=January 23, 2016 |access-date=November 12, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Roethlisberger was one of nine defendants named in the case, and his attorney denied the allegations.<ref name="SIdefendant">{{Cite magazine |date=July 21, 2009 |title=Roethlisberger listed as defendant in sexual assault lawsuit |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/football/nfl/07/21/roethlisberger.ap/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090723022812/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/football/nfl/07/21/roethlisberger.ap/index.html |archive-date=July 23, 2009 |access-date=July 21, 2009 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> The lawsuit sought damages from Roethlisberger and additional damages from officials at [[Harrah's Lake Tahoe]], alleging they helped cover up the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-01-21 |title=Settlement reached in Roethlisberger civil suit |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7485346/settlement-reached-ben-roethlisberger-civil-lawsuit |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> The case was settled in December 2011.<ref>{{cite web |last=Newell |first=Sean |date=January 21, 2012 |title=Ben Roethlisberger Settles Lake Tahoe Rape Suit |url=http://deadspin.com/5878113/ben-roethlisberger-settles-lake-tahoe-rape-suit |access-date=January 10, 2016 |website=[[Deadspin]] |publisher=[[Gawker Media]] |archive-date=January 28, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160128130914/http://deadspin.com/5878113/ben-roethlisberger-settles-lake-tahoe-rape-suit |url-status=live }}</ref>

According to McNulty, she was working as an executive casino host at the time when Roethlisberger struck up a friendly conversation with her during the tournament. The following night, she claimed he called her to report a problem with his television's sound system and asked her to check it. McNulty said she found the TV working properly, but as she turned to leave, Roethlisberger allegedly blocked the door, grabbed her, and began kissing her.<ref name="NFLcancel">{{cite web |date=July 21, 2009 |title=Steelers QB Roethlisberger cancels press conference amid civil lawsuit |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-qb-roethlisberger-cancels-press-conference-amid-civil--09000d5d8116680b |access-date=December 11, 2011 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=November 6, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131106020533/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d8116680b/article/steelers-qb-roethlisberger-cancels-press-conference-amid-civil-lawsuit |url-status=live }}</ref> The lawsuit states that she sought hospital treatment after the incident. A second lawsuit filed by another Harrah's employee claimed that the quarterback was friends with a Harrah's executive overseeing operations in northern Nevada.<ref name=hangover /> McNulty's suit alleged that her boss told her, "That guy [Roethlisberger] can have anyone he wants."<ref name=hangover />

In August 2009, the ''[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]'' published an affidavit from Angela Antonetti, McNulty's former co-worker, submitted as part of a motion to move the case to [[Douglas County, Nevada]].<ref name="Antonetti-Post-Gazette">{{Cite web |last=Fuoco |first=Michael A. |date=August 8, 2009 |title=Woman's affidavit supports Roethlisberger's denial of sexual assault |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/09220/989640-66.stm#ixzz0Nq1oEgKL |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090811042134/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/09220/989640-66.stm#ixzz0Nq1oEgKL |archive-date=August 11, 2009 |access-date=August 10, 2009 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}</ref> Antonetti stated that McNulty had previously bragged about having consensual sex with Roethlisberger, expressed hope of becoming pregnant with a "little Roethlisberger", and had asked her to travel to Pittsburgh in an attempt to "run into" him.<ref name=hangover /><ref name="Antonetti-Post-Gazette" /> Antonetti said she was "absolutely shocked" to hear about the lawsuit and believed the allegations were false.<ref name="Antonetti-Post-Gazette" />

====Milledgeville, Georgia====
On March 5, 2010, it was revealed that police in [[Milledgeville, Georgia]], investigated Roethlisberger for an alleged sexual assault which occurred inside the women's restroom at the Capital City nightclub. The accuser, a 20-year-old student at nearby [[Georgia College & State University]], had been seen earlier in the evening at several establishments with Roethlisberger, including posing for a photograph with him.<ref>{{cite web |last=Walker |first=Hunter |date=March 7, 2010 |title=Big Ben's Night Out In "Millyvegas": What The Bartenders Saw |url=https://deadspin.com/5487565/big-bens-night-out-in-millyvegas-what-the-bartenders-saw |access-date=July 18, 2018 |website=Deadspin |publisher=Gizmodo Media Group |archive-date=July 18, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180718114444/https://deadspin.com/5487565/big-bens-night-out-in-millyvegas-what-the-bartenders-saw |url-status=live }}</ref> Roethlisberger spoke with police the same night, admitting he had contact with the woman, but claimed it was not "consummated", and that she later slipped and injured herself.

Roethlisberger hired lawyer Ed Garland, who previously defended [[Baltimore Ravens]] linebacker [[Ray Lewis]] in his murder trial. The accuser was treated at [[Oconee Regional Medical Center]], where an emergency-room doctor and two nurses reported a "superficial laceration and bruising and slight bleeding in the genital area", though they could not determine whether the injuries were caused by trauma or assault. A rape kit was collected, but no semen was found. The woman reportedly told medical staff, "A boy kind of raped me."<ref name="DAtranscript">{{cite web |title=Baldwin County DA Fred Bright's transcript |url=http://www.ourgeorgiahistory.com/ogh/Baldwin_County_DA_Fred_Bright%27s_transcript |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191115024817/http://www.ourgeorgiahistory.com/ogh/Baldwin_County_DA_Fred_Bright%27s_transcript |archive-date=November 15, 2019 |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=Our Georgia History }}</ref>

According to the accuser, Roethlisberger invited her and her friends to the VIP area and encouraged them to take multiple shots of alcohol. ===2010 suspension===
Roethlisberger was suspended for six games during the [[2010 NFL season]] for violating the league's [[National Football League player conduct controversy|personal conduct policy]], and was ordered to undergo a league-mandated "professional behavior evaluation" and "must adhere to any counseling or treatment that is recommended by the professional evaluators."<ref name="APBW">{{Cite web |last=Wilner |first=Barry |date=April 21, 2010 |title=Roethlisberger banned 6 games |url=https://www.salon.com/2010/04/21/fbn_roethlisberger_suspension/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210411225750/https://www.salon.com/2010/04/21/fbn_roethlisberger_suspension/ |archive-date=April 11, 2021 |access-date=April 21, 2010 |website=Salon.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> The suspension was subsequently reduced to four games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2010 |title=Goodell reduces Roethlisberger's suspension to four games |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/goodell-reduces-roethlisberger-s-suspension-to-four-games-09000d5d81a3eb23 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017043610/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d81a3eb23/article/goodell-reduces-roethlisbergers-suspension-to-four-games |archive-date=October 17, 2017 |access-date=April 23, 2017 |website=NFL.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="SuspensionCut">{{Cite web |last=Paolantonio |first=Sal |author-link=Sal Paolantonio |date=September 4, 2010 |title=Ben Roethlisberger's ban at 4 games |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=5527564 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324224055/https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=5527564 |archive-date=March 24, 2022 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name=hangover />

'''Benjamin Richard Hartsock''' (born July 5, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the third round of the [[2004 NFL draft]].

Hartsock also played in the NFL for the [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[New York Jets]], and [[Carolina Panthers]] during his NFL career. Since retiring he has worked as a [[color analyst]] for pro and college football on [[Fox Sports Radio]] and [[ESPN Radio]].

==Early life==
Hartsock attended [[Unioto High School]] in [[Chillicothe, Ohio]], where he caught 86 passes for 1562 yards (18.16 yards reception). He also played [[running back]], [[placekicker]], and [[linebacker]]. Hartsock recorded 61 [[Tackle (football move)|tackle]]s, and 19 [[quarterback sack]]s during his senior season, after switching from linebacker to defensive end. Hartsock was a three-year captain and four-year letter winner. Hartsock committed to play at [[Ohio State University]] during his senior year of high school.

==College career==
Hartsock attended the Ohio State University, where he played tight end. He was a three-time Academic All-Big Ten Conference honoree and won CoSIDA Academic All-American honors as a junior.

During his college career, Hartsock started 31 of 51 games played and had 58 receptions for 519 yards (8.9 yards per reception). Hartsock recorded 33 catches for 290 yards and 2 touchdowns) in his senior year. As a junior, he was a contributor for the [[2002 Ohio State Buckeyes football team]], which that defeated the [[2002 Miami Hurricanes football team|Miami Hurricanes]] in the [[2003 Fiesta Bowl|Fiesta Bowl]], winning the [[BCS National Championship Game|BCS National Championship]].

==Professional career==

===Indianapolis Colts===
Hartsock  was selected in the third round with the 68th overall pick of the [[2004 NFL draft]] by the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |title=2004 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref> He was a reserve tight end in his time with the Colts, playing behind [[Marcus Pollard]] and [[Dallas Clark]].

===Tennessee Titans===
In 2006, Hartsock signed with the Colts' division rival, the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He started 12 games, compiling 206 yards receiving in two years at tight end for Tennessee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Hartsock 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HartBe00/gamelog/2006/ |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The Titans lost Hartsock to unrestricted free agency in March 2008.<ref>{{cite news |title=Titans agree to terms with Blakley |url=http://nashvillecitypaper.com/content/sports/titans-agree-terms-blakley |work=The City Paper |publisher=SouthComm Inc. |date=March 18, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929062030/http://nashvillecitypaper.com/content/sports/titans-agree-terms-blakley |archive-date=September 29, 2011 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On March 2, 2008, the [[Atlanta Falcons]] came to an agreement with Hartsock.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 3, 2008 |title=Atlanta Falcons Reach Contract Agreement With Ben Hartsock |url=http://www2.wjbf.com/sports/2008/mar/03/-jbf_2008_03_03_0026-ar-229543/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728065631/http://www2.wjbf.com/sports/2008/mar/03/-jbf_2008_03_03_0026-ar-229543/ |archive-date=July 28, 2011 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |website=WJBF-TV}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 3, 2008 |title=Source: Turner to get approximately $15M guaranteed from Falcons |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3273710 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090718175206/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3273710 |archive-date=July 18, 2009 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He was released on September 1, 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=Falcons release three players |url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-falcons/falcons-release-three-players-128749.html?cxtype=rss_sports_82014 |work=AJC.com |publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |author=Ledbetter, D. Orlando |date=September 1, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629134801/http://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-falcons/falcons-release-three-players-128749.html?cxtype=rss_sports_82014 |archive-date=June 29, 2011 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===New York Jets===
Hartsock was signed by the [[New York Jets]] on September 2, 2009, to a one-year $1.2 million contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=NY Jets sign tight end Ben Hartsock |url=http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2009/09/ny_jets_sign_te_ben_hartsock.html |work=The Star-Ledger |publisher=Advance Publications |author=Hutchinson, Dave |date=September 2, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121013133703/http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2009/09/ny_jets_sign_te_ben_hartsock.html |archive-date=October 13, 2012 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Hartsock recorded his first career touchdown on a two-yard pass from Jets quarterback [[Mark Sanchez]] against his former team, the Tennessee Titans, in September 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=For NY Jets blocking tight end Ben Hartsock, a long awaited trip to the end zone |url=http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2009/09/ny_jets_veteran_te_ben_hartsoc.html |work=The Star-Ledger |publisher=Advance Publications |author=Hutchinson, Dave |date=September 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003104512/http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2009/09/ny_jets_veteran_te_ben_hartsoc.html |archive-date=October 3, 2009 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Hartsock was re-signed by the team to a two-year contract in March 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=Source: Ben Hartsock re-signs with Jets |url=http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Source-Ben-Hartsock-resigns-with-Jets.html |publisher=National Football Post |author=Wilson, Aaron |date=March 8, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100512072529/http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Source-Ben-Hartsock-resigns-with-Jets.html |archive-date=May 12, 2010 |access-date=October 25, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 2, 2011, Hartsock was released by the Jets after spending the past two seasons with the team primarily as a blocker.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jets cut Vernon Gholston, Ben Hartsock |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/news/story?id=6175578 |publisher=ESPN |author=Cimini, Rich |date=March 2, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110306130616/http://sports.espn.go.com/new-york/nfl/news/story?id=6175578 |archive-date=March 6, 2011 |access-date=March 2, 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
Hartsock signed a two-year contract with the [[Carolina Panthers]] on July 27, 2011.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ben Hartsock signs with Carolina Panthers |url=http://www.chillicothegazette.com/article/20110728/SPORTS/107280316/Ben-Hartsock-signs-Carolina-Panthers |work=Chillicothe Gazette |publisher=Gannett Company |author=Richards, Scott |date=July 28, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110814161537/http://www.chillicothegazette.com/article/20110728/SPORTS/107280316/Ben-Hartsock-signs-Carolina-Panthers |archive-date=August 14, 2011 |access-date=July 29, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On August 10, 2014, Hartsock was signed by the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ben-hartsock-steve-maneri-signed-by-patriots-0ap3000000376543|title=Ben Hartsock, Steve Maneri signed by Patriots|first=Chris|last=Wesseling|date=August 10, 2014|access-date=August 10, 2014}}</ref> He was released just four days later, on August 14.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=August 14, 2014 |title=Ben Hartsock released by New England Patriots |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ben-hartsock-released-by-new-england-patriots-0ap3000000377779 |access-date=August 14, 2014 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hartsock is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Romano |first1=Jason |title=SS PODCAST: Former NFL tight end Ben Hartsock on CFB traditions, identity in Christ |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/podcast/2023/09/01/podcast-ben-hartsock-cfb-traditions-identity-christ/ |website=Sports Spectrum |date=September 2023 |access-date=4 September 2023}}</ref> He married his high school sweetheart, Amy Lykowski, in 2003, and they have two daughters, Whitney and Lindsey.

Graham's 219 game Australian rules career was played exclusively at the [[Geelong Football Club]] in the [[Australian Football League]] (AFL) between 1993 and 2004. As an Aussie rules player, Graham was long noted for his ability to kick extraordinarily long distances with accuracy (in particular his expertise at the [[torpedo punt]]). This is one of the key reasons that he was believed to have potential as a professional NFL punter. The left-footer{{cite news | last = Howard | first = Dylan | title = Ben Graham's amazing punt pays off | publisher=[[Geelong Advertiser]] | date = 26 January 2009 | url = http://www.geelongadvertiser.com.au/article/2009/01/26/46251_geelong_sports.html | access-date = 6 April 2009}} played for the [[New York Jets]], [[New Orleans Saints]], and [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the NFL. He is the only player to be named a captain of both an AFL and NFL side. During his career, he played in the biggest game of both codes, the [[AFL Grand Final]] ([[1995 AFL Grand Final]]) and the [[Super Bowl]] ([[Super Bowl XLIII]]). He was the first Australian to play in a Super Bowl. ==Early life== Graham was born in [[Geelong]] to mother, Helen,{{cite news| url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/ben-graham-loses-his-mother/story-fna7dq6e-1225701578277 | title=Ben Graham loses his mother | date=22 April 2009}} and father, Tony.[http://www.geelongadvertiser.com.au/article/2009/03/17/57191_geelong_sports.html Ben Graham is No.1 at his old club – Local News – Geelong, VIC, Australia]. Geelongadvertiser.com.au (17 March 2009). Retrieved on 2012-01-02. He grew up in [[Leopold, Victoria]], and began playing Aussie rules at a young age for the local Leopold Football Club{{cite web|title=AFL/VFL Players |publisher=Leopold Football Club |url=http://www.leopoldlions.com.au/aflvfl-players.html |access-date=7 April 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101023053915/http://www.leopoldlions.com.au/aflvfl-players.html |archive-date=23 October 2010 }} in the [[Bellarine Football League]], where his father was a former premiership player and coach. Graham's football ability was obvious from an early age, and he was selected by the Geelong U19s (now [[Geelong Falcons]]), where he was first identified by AFL talent scouts. ==Australian rules football career== Graham was recruited by Geelong at pick 40 in the [[1992 AFL Draft|1992]] [[Australian Football League]] (AFL) [[pre-season draft]]. He was Geelong's "Best First-Year Player" in the reserves team of 1992, and made his debut with the Geelong seniors late in 1993. Graham was noted for his long kicking (in particular his expertise at the [[torpedo punt]]),{{cite news | last = Hutchison | first = Craig | title = Benny and the Jets take $7m punt |work=Sydney Morning Herald | date = 21 May 2006 | url = http://www.smh.com.au/news/sport/benny-and-the-jets-take-7m-punt/2006/05/20/1147545567659.html | access-date = 7 April 2009}} and could play at both ends of the ground as a [[key position|key-position]] player. He played at [[centre half-forward]] and could convert goals from distances of 60 metres, as well as playing at [[centre half-back]], where his booming kicks cleared the ball from defence, particularly during [[kickout]]s. Against [[Port Adelaide Football Club|Port Adelaide]] in Round 19, 1999, when Graham was bringing the ball back in from play, he booted the ball just over 85 metres, which was past the centre circle of [[Kardinia Park (stadium)|Simonds Stadium]]. Graham played in Geelong's [[1995 AFL Grand Final]] loss to [[Carlton Football Club|Carlton]]. For the year, he was named most improved player at Geelong. Graham won the club's [[best and fairest]] award (the [[Carji Greeves Medal]]) in 1999. He followed his 1999 season with another solid season in 2000, finishing runner-up in the best & fairest in a year in which he was also bestowed the honour of the club captaincy. In 2001, he was inducted into the Geelong Football Club Hall of Fame and granted life membership. Graham retained the club captaincy until the end of 2002. ==Statistics== {{cite web|url=http://afltables.com/afl/stats/players/B/Ben_Graham.html|title=Ben Graham|work=AFL Tables|access-date=28 May 2016}} {{AFL player statistics legend}} {{AFL player statistics start}} |- style="background-color: #EAEAEA" ! colspan=3| Career ! 219 ! 145 ! 113 ! 1890 ! 803 ! 2693 ! 985 ! 321 ! 0.66 ! 0.52 ! 8.63 ! 3.67 ! 12.30 ! 4.50 ! 1.47 {{AFL player statistics end}} ==Honours and achievements== '''Individual''' * [[List of Geelong Football Club captains|Geelong captain]]: 2000–2002 * [[Carji Greeves Medal]]: 1999 * [[Australian international rules football team|Australian team]] representative honours in the [[1999 International Rules Series]] ==American football career== Graham was first approached by the [[New York Jets]] to try out as a punter in 1997; however, he decided to stay in the AFL.{{cite news | last = Crouse | first = Karen | title = A Star in Australia, Graham Is Seeking a Role With the Jets |work=New York Times | date = 24 June 2005 | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2005/07/24/sports/football/24graham.html | access-date = 5 April 2009}} In 2004, he surprised many in Australia when he quit Australian rules football and left for the United States to pursue a career as a [[Punt (gridiron football)|punter]] in the [[National Football League]], where he would ultimately be paid many times more than he would have earned in Australia and extended his playing career by many years. ===New York Jets=== Graham was signed to a short-term contract by the New York Jets in January 2005. He moved to New York City and attended Jets [[National Football League training camp|training camp]] at [[Hofstra University]], before being confirmed as the team's starting [[Punter (American football)|punter]] for the [[2005 NFL season]] when his predecessor [[Micah Knorr]] was released. When Graham played his first NFL regular season game (against the [[2005 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] at [[Arrowhead Stadium]] on 11 September 2005), he became the second person after [[Darren Bennett (football player)|Darren Bennett]] to play in both the AFL and the NFL ([[Colin Ridgeway]] played at AFL reserves level for [[Carlton Football Club|Carlton]]), and fourth Australian NFL player. He also became the oldest rookie ever to be part of an NFL opening day roster at age 31.{{cite news | last = Waszak Jnr | first = Dennis | title = Jets kick out Aussie Ben Graham | publisher=news.com.au | date = 17 September 2008 | url = http://www.news.com.au/adelaidenow/story/0,22606,24359925-12428,00.html | access-date = 5 April 2009}} On 22 May 2006, the Jets signed Graham to a six-year contract worth US$5.17 million. In late 2006, Graham made history becoming the first Australian to captain an American pro sports team when he joined the leadership group of the New York Jets. He also became the only player to captain a team in two different professional sports leagues."[http://www.worldfootynews.com/article.php?story=20060911135133525 Graham elected a NY Jets Captain]" worldfootynews.com 11 September 2006. URL Accessed 11 September 2006. Graham also used the Australian [[Punt (Australian football)#Drop punt|drop punt]]—a style of kicking prevalent in Australian rules football first introduced in 1997 to the NFL by fellow Australian Darren Bennett—which improves kicking efficiency and is said to be an innovation to the game of American football. The Jets waived Graham on 16 September 2008, but he did not miss a game: they quickly re-signed him on 22 September due to a minor injury to his replacement [[Reggie Hodges]].[http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2008/09/jets_resign_punter_graham.html Jets re-sign punter Graham] Graham was released again on 29 September after Hodges recovered.[http://www.foxsports.com.au/breaking-news/ben-graham-cut-by-jets-again/story-e6frf33c-1111117624549 Ben Graham cut by Jets - again] ===New Orleans Saints=== On 20 October 2008, Graham signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] to play a game in London. The team had released incumbent punter [[Steve Weatherford]] earlier in the week due to travel arrangement issues. He played just the one game, punting three times with an average of 42 yards, before being released on 29 October. He was replaced by [[Glenn Pakulak]].{{cite news | title = Ben Graham sacked again | publisher=Courier Mail | date = 29 October 2008 | url = http://www.news.com.au/couriermail/story/0,20797,24571057-5016169,00.html | access-date = 6 April 2009}} ===Arizona Cardinals=== Graham was signed by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on 1 December 2008 after the team released [[Punter (American football)|punter]] [[Dirk Johnson]]; this was the second time that Johnson had been replaced by an Australian punter. In the NFC Championship game that year, Graham's Cardinals played the [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], whose punter, [[Sav Rocca]], also was an ex-AFL player from [[Collingwood Football Club|Collingwood]] and [[North Melbourne Football Club|North Melbourne]]. This guaranteed that one of the two would be the first Australian to play in a [[Super Bowl]]. The Cardinals' victory presented that honour to Graham.ABC News (2009). [https://web.archive.org/web/20090120050029/http://www.abc.net.au/news/stories/2009/01/19/2468967.htm Graham set to become first Aussie to play in Super Bowl]. Retrieved 19 January 2009. The Cardinals released Graham on 2 September 2011, before the start of the season. But they re-signed him on 5 October;{{cite news |title=Cards re-sign punter Ben Graham |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7063898/arizona-cardinals-re-sign-punter-ben-graham |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=5 October 2011 |access-date=11 October 2011}} he was released again on 11 October, after one game covering for the injured [[Dave Zastudil]]. ===Detroit Lions=== On 15 November 2011, Graham signed with the [[Detroit Lions]], replacing [[Robert Malone (American football)|Robert Malone]]. Malone had played only one game after replacing the injured [[Ryan Donahue]]. During the 2012 preseason, Graham beat out Donahue for the starting job. On 25 September 2012, Graham was placed on the season-ending injured reserve list. [[Nick Harris (punter)|Nick Harris]] was signed to replace Graham for the remainder of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20120925/SPORTS0101/209250436#ixzz27ZvHbsnE |title=Lions put punter Ben Graham on injured reserve, sign Nick Harris | the Detroit News | detroitnews.com |access-date=26 September 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015131107/http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20120925/SPORTS0101/209250436 |archive-date=15 October 2012 }} He was released with an injury settlement later that season. ===International career=== In 2011 with the [[2011 NFL season#Labor dispute|NFL lockout]] looming, Graham announced his intention to play for the [[Australia national American football team|Australian National team]] in the [[2011 IFAF World Cup]], the official international American Football championship tournament. Later, he officially was added to the roster as the country's starting punter.[http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/afl/ben-graham-takes-outback-to-austria/story-e6frexx0-1226054216595 Ben Graham takes Outback to Australia]. Retrieved 12 June 2011. ==Post-playing career== In 2012, Graham joined the [[Western Bulldogs]] as a strategic football operations manager.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/other-sports/news/article/1c608d90vk9j71cmgopttc2o0k|title=Ben Graham joins Western Bulldogs|work=sportingnews.com|date=4 December 2012|access-date=22 July 2024}} ==Personal life== Graham and his wife, Katie, have two daughters, Sophie and Rosie, and one son, Jack.[http://azcardinals.com/team/bio.php?PRKey=219 Arizona Cardinals bio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210080922/http://azcardinals.com/team/bio.php?PRKey=219 |date=10 February 2009 }}. He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]]. He attended [[Clear Brook High School]].
