'''Benjamin Thomas Hamilton''' (born August 18, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[guard (American football)|guard]] and [[center (American football)|center]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[University of Minnesota]], and was a two-time consensus [[All-American]].  The [[Denver Broncos]] picked him in the fourth round of the [[2001 NFL draft]], and he played professionally for the Broncos and [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the NFL.

==Early life==
Hamilton was born in [[Minneapolis, Minnesota]], the son of former [[Minnesota Vikings]] offensive lineman [[Wes Hamilton]]. He attended [[Wayzata High School]] in [[Plymouth, Minnesota]], and was all-state selection in football. He graduated in 1996.

==College career==
He attended the University of Minnesota, where he played for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football]] team from 1996 to 2000.  He was a two-time first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]] selection, and was recognized as a consensus first-team [[All-American]] in 1999 and 2000.<ref>''2011 NCAA Football Records Book'', [http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2011/Awards.pdf  Award Winners], National Collegiate Athletic Association, Indianapolis, Indiana, p. 11 (2011).  Retrieved June 24, 2012.</ref>

==Professional career==
He was selected by the Denver Broncos in the fourth round of the [[2001 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2001/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  After playing his entire career with the Broncos, Hamilton signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on April 20, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ben Hamilton signs with Seahawks|date=20 April 2010|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2010/04/20/hamilton-signs-with-seahawks/|publisher=ProFootballTalk.com}}</ref>

On November 2, 2010, Hamilton was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks place Bryant, Hamilton on season-ending IR|url=http://blog.thenewstribune.com/seahawks/2010/11/02/hawks-place-bryant-hamilton-on-season-ending-ir/|publisher=The News Tribune|access-date=2011-03-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111009024818/http://blog.thenewstribune.com/seahawks/2010/11/02/hawks-place-bryant-hamilton-on-season-ending-ir/|archive-date=2011-10-09|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 22, Hamilton was waived from the injury list.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ben Hamilton waived from injury list|url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/40779581/ns/sports-player_news/|publisher=NBC Sports|access-date=2011-03-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010173518/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/40779581/ns/sports-player_news/|archive-date=2012-10-10|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Post NFL career==
Hamilton is currently a full-time mathematics teacher at [[Valor Christian High School]] in [[Highlands Ranch, CO]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Hamilton' |url=https://govalor.com/about/directory/ben-hamilton/ |website=GoValor.com |publisher=Valor Christian High School |access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref>

'''Ben Leber''' (born December 7, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the third round of the [[2002 NFL draft]] and later played for the [[Minnesota Vikings]].

==Early life==
Lining up primarily at running back, Leber was named to several high school [[All-America]] teams at Vermillion High School in [[Vermillion, South Dakota]]. As a junior, he rushed for 1,404 yards and 18 touchdowns, and notched 1,350 yards in his senior year.  That season, he was declared a ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade Magazine]]'' All-America (the only South Dakotan so honored in 1997), an honorable mention All-USA by ''[[USA Today]]'', and was selected to play in the North-South Dakota All-Star game. An excellent student, he was also an Academic All-State selection.

==College career==
At [[Kansas State University|Kansas State]], Leber made the switch to full-time linebacker.  A two-time All-Big 12 selection, he finished his college career with 216 tackles, 46 tackles for loss, and 13.5 sacks.  His 216 career tackles were the fifth most in Kansas State history.  As a junior, he earned second-team all-conference honors.  The year later, he was an All-America third-team selection by the [[Associated Press]], a consensus [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12 Conference]] first-team choice, and a team captain.  He received a degree in business-general management in 2002.

===San Diego Chargers===
Leber was selected by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the third round of the [[2002 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2002 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2002/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He was an immediate-impact rookie, playing in all 16 games and starting 14 of them.  He was selected to both the ''[[Pro Football Weekly]]'' and ''[[Football Digest]]'' All-Rookie teams, finishing the year with 49 tackles, 5 sacks (third on the team), and 3 forced fumbles (first on the team).

In his second season, Leber started every game at strong side linebacker for the Chargers, notching 75 tackles, 3 sacks, 1 pass defensed, and 1 forced fumble.  In his third year, he was an every-game starter for the Chargers, finishing the season with 58 tackles, 2 sacks, and 1 fumble recovery.  The next season, Leber was injured during training camp and again during the season.  This led to him losing his starting position to future Pro-Bowler [[Shawne Merriman]].  He finished 2005 with 22 tackles, 2 sacks and 1 fumble recovery.

===Minnesota Vikings===
As an unrestricted free agent, Leber was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on March 11, 2006. Playing in 15 games, he finished his first season with the team with 46 tackles, 3 sacks, 1 interception, 3 forced fumbles, 2 fumble recoveries and 1 fumble recovery touchdown. The next year was even better—playing in all 16 games, Leber notched 67 tackles, 5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, and 1 interception. In 2008, Leber again played the full season, recording 64 tackles, a career-low 1.5 sacks, and 2 interceptions.

===St. Louis Rams===
On August 9, 2011, Leber signed with the [[St. Louis Rams]]. On December 3, 2011, Leber was waived by the Rams.

===Retirement===
Despite having worked out for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in March 2012,<ref>{{cite web | url = http://thesidelineview.com/columns/caplans-nfl-corner/eagles-work-out-veteran-lb | title = Eagles Work Out Veteran LB | author = Adam Caplan | date = March 1, 2012| accessdate = June 11, 2012 | publisher = thesidelineview.com | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120629012337/http://thesidelineview.com/columns/caplans-nfl-corner/eagles-work-out-veteran-lb | archive-date = June 29, 2012 | url-status = dead }}</ref> he was unable to find an interested team.

He announced his retirement from professional football on June 18, 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/linebacker-ben-leber-announces-retirement-after-10-seasons-with-chargers-vikings-rams/2012/06/08/gJQAAxorOV_story.html | title = Linebacker Ben Leber announces retirement after 10 seasons with Chargers, Vikings, Rams | agency = Associated Press | date = June 8, 2012 | accessdate = June 11, 2012 | publisher = thesidelineview.com}}{{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Ebenezer Obomanu'''<ref name=ESPN.com>{{cite web|title=Obomanu on ESPN |work=espn.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/9835/ben-obomanu |access-date=2008-01-31}}</ref> (born October 30, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Obomanu played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]],<ref>{{cite web | year=2005 | url=http://graphics.fansonly.com/photos/schools/aub/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/fbmg_players_072805.pdf | title=2005 Tigers (pp. 35-71) | work=2005 Auburn Football Media Guide | publisher=Auburn University | access-date=2006-05-01 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303194437/http://graphics.fansonly.com/photos/schools/aub/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/fbmg_players_072805.pdf | archive-date=2016-03-03 | url-status=dead }}</ref> and he was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the seventh round of the [[2006 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|year=2006 |url=https://nfl.com/draft/drafttracker |title=2006 NFL Draft Tracker |work=NFL.com |access-date=2006-05-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060420203910/http://www.nfl.com/draft/drafttracker |archive-date=2006-04-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Early life==
Obomanu attended [[Selma High School]] in [[Selma, Alabama]], and was a letterman and a starter in football and basketball. He graduated from Selma High School as a [[valedictorian]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Jon |last=Cooper |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/sec-football/ben-obomanu-auburn-alabama/ |title=Former AU player wearing 'State of Auburn' shirt to Alabama law school |website=Saturday Down South |date=August 12, 2015 |access-date=May 12, 2017 }}</ref>

==College career ==
Obomanu played football for Auburn from 2002 to 2005. He had a career game against Ole MIss in 2003 but dropped the game winning touchdown pass in the end zone in a loss.

Obomanu is a member of the Sigma Delta chapter ([[Auburn University]]) of [[Omega Psi Phi]] fraternity. He attended the [[University of Alabama School of Law]] beginning in Fall 2015.

===Seattle Seahawks===
After being drafted by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the seventh round (249th overall) of the [[2006 NFL draft]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=2006 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2006/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Obomanu spent the entire 2006 season on the team's practice squad.

Obomanu made the Seahawks' active roster out of training camp in 2007. His first NFL touchdown came in on October 14 in a [[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]] game against the [[New Orleans Saints]]. Obomanu caught a 17-yard [[Matt Hasselbeck]] pass late in the second quarter.

Obomanu broke his collarbone in a preseason game against the [[Oakland Raiders]] on the 29th of August 2008 and he was placed on Injured Reserve the following day.

Following Week 11 of the 2010 NFL Season, Obomanu was promoted to the #2 receiver, starting alongside Mike Williams.

In a home game against the Carolina Panthers in 2010, Obomanu was injured as a result of a hit by [[Carolina Panthers|Panthers]] safety [[Charles Godfrey (American football)|Charles Godfrey]].

Obomanu finished the 2010 season with 30 receptions for 494 yards, 4 touchdowns, and a 16.5 yard per catch average.
Shortly after the Seahawks' were eliminated from the playoffs against the Bears, Obomanu signed a new 3-year contract with the Seahawks running through 2013.

On March 15, 2013, the Seahawks released Obomanu.

'''Benjamin Frank Davis''' (born October 30, 1945) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] and [[return specialist]] for 10 years in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He is the brother of political activist [[Angela Davis]].

==Early life==
Davis was born in 1945 in [[Birmingham, Alabama]].<ref name=fred>[http://browns.digiknow.com/news_room/history/arts/1182.0.html Where are they now?]{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> His father, a graduate of [[St. Augustine's University (North Carolina)|St. Augustine's College]], a [[Historically black colleges and universities|traditional black college]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]], was briefly a [[high school]] [[history]] [[teacher]], but found it more lucrative to own and operate a [[Filling station|service station]] in the black section of Birmingham.<ref name=nab>[http://www.itsabouttimebpp.com/News_Media/pdf/Angela_Davis.pdf Angela Davis arrested]</ref> His mother, with an [[Master of Arts|MA]] from [[New York University]], was an [[elementary school]] teacher.<ref name=nab /> The family owned a large home in a [[middle class]] mixed neighborhood called "Dynamite Hill"<ref name=nab /> after so-called "night rider" [[terrorist]]s began [[16th Street Baptist Church bombing|bomb attacks]] on [[civil rights]] leaders clustered there.<ref name=nab />

To avoid the racial strife for which Dynamite Hill was named, children in the Davis family spent time with friends and relatives elsewhere. Davis graduated from [[Fair Lawn High School]] in [[Fair Lawn, New Jersey]], at the age of 15,<ref name=fred /><ref>[https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/benjamin-f-davis-jr Benjamin F. Davis Jr.], [[The History Makers]]. Accessed March 24, 2022. "Football player and entrepreneur Ben Davis was born on October 30, 1945 in Birmingham, Alabama to B. Frank and Sallye B. Davis. His sister is activist, author, and professor Angela Davis. He graduated at age fifteen from Fair Lawn High School in Fair Lawn, New Jersey in 1961, and attended Bridgton Academy in North Bridgton, Maine from 1961 to 1963."</ref> then marked time by attending [[Bridgton Academy]], a [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Maine]] until he was old enough to enroll in [[Defiance College]]<ref name=fred /> in rural [[Defiance, Ohio]].

"I went to Defiance because I was looking for the same type of environment as the prep school," Davis told Fred Greetham in 2001.<ref name=fred /> "I was in the band in high school, but I decided to go out for the football team in college. By the time we were seniors, we were undefeated."

==Professional career==
<!-- FAIR USE of IMAGENAME.jpg: see image description page at http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image:IMAGENAME.jpg for rationale 
[[File:BenDavisRookie.gif|left|Rookie card, 1969 (Copyright Topps)]]-->
Davis was [[NFL draft|drafted]] in the 17th (and last) round by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the [[1967 NFL/AFL draft]].<ref name=draft>[http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/history/draft/draft_1960s.php Browns draft history] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060826042032/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/history/draft/draft_1960s.php |date=August 26, 2006 }}</ref> With [[Paul Warfield]], [[Gary Collins (American football)|Gary Collins]] and [[Clifton McNeil]] already established as receivers, Davis was switched to a [[Defense (sports)|defensive]] role. In his [[rookie]] year, he led the league in [[punt return]]s, averaging 12.7 yards per return, and one 52-yard return for a [[touchdown]]. He also led the Browns in [[Kickoff (gridiron football)#Return|returning kickoffs]], with 27 returns totalling 708 yards, including one of 63 yards.<ref name=fred /> Only [[Leroy Kelly]] (15.6), [[Greg Pruitt]] (12.9) and [[Eric Metcalf]] (12.9) ever had better years returning punts for the Browns.<ref name=fred />

In 1968, Davis started at cornerback, and led the team with 8 [[interception]]s. The season's 32 interceptions that year set a Browns record. His individual performance is the 3rd-best in Browns history, and he still holds the record for seven consecutive games with an interception.<ref name=fred />

A torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]] benched Davis during the [[1969 Cleveland Browns season|1969 season]], and half of the [[1970 Cleveland Browns season|1970 season]].<ref name=fred />

He was traded to the [[Detroit Lions]] in 1974 for a 5th-round draft pick.<ref name=draft />

==Post-NFL==
Davis went into [[Photocopier|copier]] sales after his football career ended, then went into [[cable television]] and bought a [[radio station]] in [[Tulsa, Oklahoma]].<ref name=fred /> Since 1995, he has owned and operated Britt Business Systems, a [[Xerox]] dealer, in the [[Cleveland]] suburb of [[Beachwood, Ohio]]. Davis has lived in Cleveland since 1967, even commuting to Detroit when he played for the Lions.

==Personal life==
Davis and his wife Sylvia have two grown children, [https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1141150/ Cecilie] and [https://web.archive.org/web/20161101041441/https://www.phizzle.com/leadership/ Ben III], who both live in [[California]].<ref name=fred /> Davis's sister, [[Angela Davis]], is a prominent [[Activism|political activist]]. A younger brother, Reggie Davis, also attended Defiance College.<ref>[[Defiance College|''Defiance College Defender'']], November 10, 1970</ref>

'''Benjamin Richard Grubbs''' (born March 10, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]], and was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the first round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[New Orleans Saints]] and [[Kansas City Chiefs]].

==Early life==
Grubbs was born in [[Columbus, Georgia]]. He was raised in [[Eclectic, Alabama]] and attended [[Elmore County High School]] where he was the team's star linebacker. Grubbs registered 150 tackles, six sacks, and an interception as a senior. A two-way star, Grubbs also played fullback, rushing for 130 yards on 28 carries, with two touchdowns.  He also caught seven passes for 50 yards. As a junior, Grubbs managed 110 total tackles, and an interception, also lettering as a four-year starter on the basketball team.

As a senior, he was rated one of the top 10 players in Alabama by SuperPrep Magazine. Grubbs was a SuperPrep All-American and an Alabama Sports Writer's Class 4A All-State selection as a linebacker. At 6-4, 250 as a high school senior, he was recruited as a defensive end, though.<ref>{{Citation |work=Rivals.com |title=Ben Grubbs Recruiting Profile |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=145&sport=1 }}</ref> Considered a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Grubbs was listed as the No. 23 strongside defensive end prospect in the nation.<ref>{{Citation |date=February 5, 2002 |title=Rivals100: Strongside defensive ends |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=42 }}</ref> He verbally committed to Auburn on January 23, 2002, picking the Tigers over [[Louisiana State University|LSU]] and [[University of Alabama|Alabama]].

==College career==
Grubbs began attending at [[Auburn University]] in 2002 after being encouraged to attend by his cousin, Alvin Leonard, as an oversized linebacker or undersized defensive end. He was redshirted for the 2002 football season, while he worked with the team's strength and conditioning coach to build muscle. Grubbs was slated to work with as a defensive tackle the following year.

Grubbs moved from defensive tackle to tight end during the 2003 season, playing in a total of nine games, including the last seven.  During spring drills the following year, Grubbs moved from tight end to offensive guard, under the recommendation of his position coach Hugh Nall.

Grubbs started all 13 games during the Auburn Tiger's undefeated 2004 campaign.

In 2005, he started all 12 games for the Auburn Tigers.

During his career at Auburn University, Grubbs never missed a game and started 37 straight contests. During his Auburn career he blocked for future NFL running backs [[Cadillac Williams]], [[Ronnie Brown]], [[Kenny Irons]], and quarterback [[Jason Campbell]]. He also starred alongside future left tackle for the San Diego Chargers, [[Marcus McNeill]].

Grubbs completed his degree from Auburn, graduating with a Bachelor's in Public Administration in May 2006.

At the end of the season, the Chiefs released him.

'''Benjamin Charles Hawkins''' (March 22, 1944 – October 9, 2017), nicknamed "'''the Hawk'''", was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), primarily for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] from 1966 to 1973.<ref name="Hawkins">{{Cite web |title=Former Eagles WR Ben Hawkins dies at 73 |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/20992445/former-philadelphia-eagles-wr-ben-hawkins-dies-73 |access-date=2026-05-25 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref> He later played in the NFL for the [[Cleveland Browns]] and the [[Philadelphia Bell]] of the [[World Football League]] (WFL). Hawkins led the NFL in receiving yards while with the Eagles in 1967. He played [[college football]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]] and was selected in the third round of the [[1966 NFL draft]] by the Eagles.  Hawkins was also selected in the fifth round of the [[1966 American Football League draft|1966 AFL draft]] by the [[New York Jets]] but opted to play in the NFL instead.

Born in [[Newark, New Jersey]], Hawkins attended [[Weequahic High School]] before moving to nearby [[Nutley, New Jersey|Nutley]] and transferring to [[Nutley High School]].<ref>[http://nutleyhalloffame.nutleypubliclibrary.org/2009-hawkins/  2009 Hall of Fame Inductee, Benjamin Charles Hawkins], Nutley Hall of Fame. Accessed November 9, 2019. "Benjamin Charles Hawkins was born in Newark, NJ in 1944. He attended Weequahic High School and Nutley High School."</ref> He had two children.<ref name="Hawkins" />

Hawkins died on October 9, 2017, at age 73.<ref name="Hawkins" />

'''Benjamin Richard Noll''' (born November 14, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[St. Louis Rams]] and [[Detroit Lions]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn Quakers football|Penn Quakers]].

==Early life==
Noll attended [[Saint Louis Priory School]] in St. Louis, where he played [[Guard (American football)|right guard]]. As a junior, he earned All-metro honors. As a senior, he helped his team win the state championship, while earning All-league, All-metro and All-state honors.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.thedp.com/article/2004/09/noll_looks_to_earn_spot_on_nfls_rams | title=Noll looks to earn spot on NFL's Rams | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>
He also practiced [[basketball]] and was a member of the school's [[Rugby football|rugby]] club.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://pennathletics.com/news/2016/6/27/5771aa3ce4b0028e7235daff_131492764751302297.aspx?path=football | title=Ben Noll Makes Dallas Cowboys? Regular Season Roster | date=September 8, 2004 | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
Noll played football scholarship for the [[University of Pennsylvania]] while an undergraduate studying at the [[Wharton School|Wharton School of Business]]. As a true freshman, he appeared in 10 games as a backup. As a sophomore, he appeared in 10 games. As a junior, he started 10 games at [[right tackle]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.thedp.com/article/2002/09/the_quakers_positionbyposition | title=The Quakers, position-by-position | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

As a senior, he played on an [[offensive line]] that featured five seniors (Noll, Chris Clark, Chris Kupchik, Matt Dukes and Michael Powers), helping the team achieve an undefeated season (10-0 overall).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pennathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID%3D1700%26ATCLID%3D51838 |title=The Perfect Team |accessdate=2015-09-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925105615/http://www.pennathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=1700&ATCLID=51838 |archivedate=2015-09-25 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.thedp.com/article/2003/09/growing_together | title=Growing Together | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He finished his college eligibility after playing in 39 out of 40 games (20 starts).

==Professional career==

===St. Louis Rams (first stint)===
Noll was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[St. Louis Rams]] after the [[2004 NFL draft]] on June 18.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://pennathletics.com/news/2016/6/27/5771ab36e4b0028e7235e4fa_131492833244134400.aspx?path=football | title=Ben Noll Signs With the St. Louis Rams | date=June 29, 2004 | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on September 5.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.thedp.com/article/2004/09/noll_signs_with_dallas_after_rams_let_him_go | title=Noll signs with Dallas after Rams let him go | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On September 6, [[2004 NFL season|2004]], he was claimed off waivers by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] to be the backup at [[Guard (American football)|right guard]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/09/07/sports/transactions.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was declared inactive in 11 of the first 14 games of the season. He started in the season finale against the [[New York Giants]], replacing [[Andre Gurode]] at [[Guard (American football)|right guard]]. He played on kickoff returns, field goal, and as a substitute guard played 413 snaps.

In [[2005 NFL season|2005]], he reprised the same role, after being declared inactive during the first 6 games of the season.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2242669 | title=Cowboys release lineman Noll, sign rookie OL Procter | date=November 30, 2005 | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was released on November 30 for medical reasons.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/12/01/sports/transactions.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===St. Louis Rams (second stint)===
On December 2, [[2005 NFL season|2005]], he was claimed off waivers by the [[St. Louis Rams]], and was declared inactive for the final 4 games. He was cut on September 1, [[2006 NFL season|2006]].

===Detroit Lions===
On December 13, [[2006 NFL season|2006]], he was signed by the [[Detroit Lions]] to their [[practice squad]]. He was released on September 1, [[2007 NFL season|2007]] and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2007/09/02/transactions-367/ | title=Transactions | date=September 2, 2007 | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He wasn't re-signed at the end of the season.

==Personal life==
After he retired, Noll moved to Nashville, where he works as a business consultant.{{citation needed|date=February 2020}} He married on October 23, 2010.{{citation needed|date=February 2020}} Ben's wife is an OB/GYN practicing in Nashville.

'''Benjamin James Sobieski''' (born May 3, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player. He attended [[Mahtomedi Senior High School]] and the [[University of Iowa]] before being drafted in the fifth round of the [[2003 NFL draft]] (number 151 overall) by the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2003/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

A ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'' and SuperPrep [[All-American]] who also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[Track and field|track]] and [[Ice hockey|hockey]],<ref>{{Citation |title=ESPN DraftTracker |url=http://www.espn.com/nfldraft/tracker/player?id=7002 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2003-04-26 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref> Sobieski's career was hampered by injuries.<ref>{{Citation |title=Patriots release last player picked in '05 draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2128774 |publisher=ESPN |date=2005-08-09 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=Wright returns after breaking down at Dolphins camp |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2120651 |publisher=ESPN |date=2005-07-31 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=Transactions |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/10/13/sports/transactions.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=2004-10-13 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=Transactions |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/08/09/sports/transactions.html |work=The New York Times |date=2005-08-09 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref> He spent six years at Iowa under two head coaches ([[Hayden Fry]] and [[Kirk Ferentz]]),<ref>{{Citation |last=Maly |first=Ron |title=Tales from the Iowa Sidelines |publisher=Sports Publishing LLC |year=2003 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/talesfromiowasid0000maly/page/50 50–52] |isbn=1-58261-574-8 |url=https://archive.org/details/talesfromiowasid0000maly/page/50 }}</ref> missing both the 1999 and 2000 seasons due to shoulder injuries.<ref>{{Citation |title=Thursday Roundup - Bills sign 5th-round pick Sobieski |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/news/2003/06/19/roundup_thursday/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622094217/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/news/2003/06/19/roundup_thursday/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 22, 2011 |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=2003-06-20 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref>

After being released by Buffalo,<ref>{{Citation |title=Transactions |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/09/06/sports/transactions.html |work=The New York Times |date=2004-09-06 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref> Sobieski was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Citation |title=San Francisco 49ers Transactions - 2005 |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/teams/transactions?team=sfo&year=2005 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120721015953/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/teams/transactions?team=sfo&year=2005 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 21, 2012 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref> He was brought up to the regular team, but never played due to injury.<ref>{{Citation |last=Crumpacker |first=John |title=49ers anticipate fresh start |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/49ers-anticipate-fresh-start-Exhibition-is-1st-2491424.php |publisher=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |date=2006-08-11 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Crumpacker |first=John |title=For one last day, Rice back with red and gold |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/49ERS-NOTEBOOK-For-one-last-day-Rice-back-with-2513977.php |publisher=San Francisco Chronicle |date=2006-08-20 |access-date=2008-12-03}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Oliver Kelly''' (born September 15, 1978)<ref>{{cite web|title=31 Ben Kelly CB|url=http://www.patriots.com/alumni/index.cfm?ac=alumnibiosdetail&bio=15237|work=patriots.com|publisher=NFL|access-date=5 November 2010}}{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL), [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|Arena Football League]] (AFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the third round of the [[2000 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2000 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2000/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2000 - Round 3|url=http://www.nfl.com/draft/history/fulldraft?season=2000#round3|work=nfl.com|publisher=National Football League|access-date=5 November 2010}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado Buffaloes]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bits and pieces |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/st-louis-post-dispatch-bits-and-pieces/180503911/ |publisher=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |access-date=5 September 2025 |page=60 |date=9 Oct 1999}}</ref>

Kelly was an [[All-America]]n sprinter for the [[Colorado Buffaloes track and field]] team, running 2nd leg on their 7th-place [[4 × 400 meters relay]] team at the [[1999 NCAA Division I Indoor Track and Field Championships]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2 area tracksters get national honors |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-sentinel-2-area-tracksters-get/180503780/ |publisher=[[The Daily Sentinel (Grand Junction, Colorado)]] |access-date=5 September 2025 |page=16 |date=11 Mar 1999}}</ref>

Kelly was also a member of the [[New England Patriots]], [[Denver Broncos]], [[Los Angeles Avengers]], [[Calgary Stampeders]] and [[Grand Rapids Rampage]]. He earned a [[Super Bowl ring]] with the Patriots in [[Super Bowl XXXVI]] over the [[St. Louis Rams]].

Kelly is well represented in the [[Aloha Bowl]] record books after he returned a kickoff for a TD against Oregon on Dec. 25, 1998.{{citation needed|date=January 2014}}

'''Ben Allen Tamburello Jr.''' (born September 9, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] and [[Center (American football)|center]] for five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] from [[1987 NFL season|1987]] to [[1991 NFL season|1991]]. He was selected by the Eagles in the third round of the [[1987 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].

==Early life==
Tamburello was born in [[Birmingham, Alabama]].  He attended [[Shades Valley High School]] in [[Homewood, Alabama]], and [[Tennessee Military Institute]] in [[Sweetwater, Tennessee]].

==College career==
Tamburello was recruited by [[Paul "Bear" Bryant]] to play [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], but decided to play for [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]]. He played for the Tigers from 1983 to 1986. In [[1986 College Football All-America Team|1986]], he was named a unanimous  All-American. He won the SEC Lineman of the Year award in 1986 and was named a team captain.<ref name="Where are they now">{{cite news |author=Bean, Josh |title=WHERE ARE THEY NOW? Ben Tamburello: Former Auburn football player |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=j1QyAAAAIBAJ&sjid=yuUFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2093,2176544 |newspaper=Times Daily |date=January 17, 2005 |accessdate=April 25, 2010}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Tamburello was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the third round (65th overall) of the [[1987 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=September 25, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played for the Eagles from 1987 to 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Tamburello Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TambBe20.htm |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==After football==
Tamburello works in real estate and resides in Birmingham with his wife, Katy, and his three children: Ben III, Anna and Julia.<ref name="Where are they now"/>

'''Benjamin Ijalana''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|aɪ|dʒ|ə|ˈ|l|ɑː|n|ə}} {{respell|EYE|jə|LAH|nə}}; born August 6, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats football|Villanova Wildcats]] and was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the second round of the [[2011 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Ijalana's parents immigrated to the U.S. from Nigeria.<ref name="Philly Inq">{{cite news|last=Fernandez|first=Bernard|title=Too big for soccer, Villanova's Ijalana may be ready for NFL|url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-04-27/sports/29478784_1_ben-ijalana-villanova-s-ijalana-offensive-linemen|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120612025926/http://articles.philly.com/2011-04-27/sports/29478784_1_ben-ijalana-villanova-s-ijalana-offensive-linemen|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 12, 2012|access-date=August 4, 2011|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=April 27, 2011}}</ref>  A native of [[New Brunswick, New Jersey]], Ijalana attended [[Willingboro High School]] in his freshman and sophomore year, before moving to [[Hainesport Township, New Jersey|Hainesport Township]] and transferring to [[Rancocas Valley Regional High School]], where he was a two-way lineman, and district champion in wrestling.<ref>Cosentino, Dom. [http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2015/04/jets_re-sign_backup_offensive_tackle_ben_ijalana.html "Jets re-sign backup offensive tackle Ben Ijalana"], NJ Advance Media for [[NJ.com]], April 1, 2015. Accessed September 28, 2017. "Ijalana, 25, attended both Willingboro and Rancocas Valley high schools in South Jersey."</ref><ref>[https://villanova.com/story.aspx?filename=Ben_Ijalana_Drafted_By_The_Indianapolis_Colts&file_date=4/29/2011 "Ben Ijalana Drafted By The Indianapolis Colts"], [[Villanova Wildcats football]], April 29, 2011. Accessed July 18, 2019. "Ijalana, a native of Hainesport, N.J., and a graduate of Rancocas Valley High School, started all 53 games of his Villanova career and helped the Wildcats to a 40-13 record, three NCAA playoff appearances and the 2009 FCS National Championship."</ref>

==College career==
He started every game at left tackle since his [[true freshman]] year at Villanova.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.delcotimes.com/articles/2010/09/10/sports/doc4c89a1ada0a71549517727.txt |title=Ijalana tackles task of being top lineman at Villanova |newspaper=[[Delaware County Daily Times]] |date=September 10, 2010 |archive-date=March 15, 2012 |access-date=October 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315005544/http://www.delcotimes.com/articles/2010/09/10/sports/doc4c89a1ada0a71549517727.txt |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Ijalana was named to the 2010 [[Outland Trophy]] watch list as the only Football Championship Subdivision player.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2010/outland100621.html |title=2010 Outland Trophy Watch List Announced |date=June 21, 2010 |work=[[Football Writers Association of America|FWAA]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.philly.com/inquirer/sports/20100622_Villanova_s_Ben_Ijalana_named_to_Outland_Trophy_Watch_list.html |title=Villanova's Ben Ijalana named to Outland Trophy Watch list |newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=June 22, 2010 }}</ref>

''[[The Sporting News]]'' listed Ijalana as one of the five most "intriguing small-school prospects".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/feed/2011-01/2011-nfl-draft/story/five-sleepers-to-watch-at-nfl-scouting-combine |title=Five sleepers to watch at NFL Scouting Combine |work=Sporting News |date=February 20, 2011 |first=Dennis |last=Dillon |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110222194943/http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/feed/2011-01/2011-nfl-draft/story/five-sleepers-to-watch-at-nfl-scouting-combine |archive-date=February 22, 2011 }}</ref> 

Entering draft day, Ijalana was listed as a second round prospect with the possibility of jumping into the first round. He was projected as a right tackle, following his strong showing as a left tackle in college and his good arm length and hand size. Additionally, he had the ability to fall back as a guard.

===Indianapolis Colts===
On day two of the [[2011 NFL draft]], the [[Indianapolis Colts]] traded their 53rd and 152nd pick to the Redskins for the 49th pick to draft Ijalana. He was the highest selected Villanova Wildcat since [[Howie Long]] in [[1981 NFL draft|1981]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2019-02-26}}</ref>

Ijalana played four games in his rookie season before tearing his ACL and landing on [[injured reserve]].<ref name="Wilson">{{cite web|last=Wilson|first=Josh|url=http://www.stampedeblue.com/2012/8/1/3213935/ben-ijalana-waived-injured-colts-sign-ty-nsekh|title=Ben Ijalana waived, injured - Colts sign Ty Nsekh|website=StampedeBlue.com|date=August 2012 }}</ref>

A few weeks after being cleared to play, Ijalana tore his ACL again during training camp in 2012.<ref name="Wilson"/> Ijalana was eventually declared out for the 2012 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.indystar.com/article/20120731/SPORTS03/120731054/Colts-Ben-Ijalana-J-Edds-out-season-knee-injuries?odyssey=obinsite|title=Indianapolis Star|website=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|language=en|access-date=June 4, 2018}}</ref> He was waived/injured on August 1, 2012, and he was subsequently placed on injured reserve on August 5.

===New York Jets===
Ijalala was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Jets]] on September 1, 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=3 Arrive Via Waivers; 7 Added to Practice Squad |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-randylangefb/3-Arrive-Via-Waivers-6-Added-to-Practice-Squad/1f164acd-6a34-48b7-a1b8-16462d09fd80 |author=Lange, Randy |date=September 1, 2013 |publisher=New York Jets |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130904052057/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-randylangefb/3-Arrive-Via-Waivers-7-Added-to-Practice-Squad/1f164acd-6a34-48b7-a1b8-16462d09fd80 |archive-date=September 4, 2013 |access-date=September 1, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 9, 2016, Ijalana signed a one-year contract extension with the Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets re-sign offensive tackle Ben Ijalana|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2016/04/09/jets-re-sign-offensive-tackle-ben-ijalana/|author=Smith, Michael David|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=April 9, 2016|access-date=February 16, 2017}}</ref> On March 9, 2017, Ijalana signed a two-year, $11 million contract extension with the Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets To Sign Ben Ijalana On 2 Year $11 Mill Deal|url=http://www.ganggreennation.com/2017/3/9/14872472/jets-to-sign-ben-ijalana-on-2-year-11-mill-deal|author=Wyatt, David|website=GangGreenNation.com|date=March 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Re-Sign T Ben Ijalana|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-9/Jets-Re-Sign-T-Ben-Ijalana/b97e39a2-9de8-4a8c-995a-15a693d46114|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=March 24, 2017|access-date=March 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170414221323/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-9/Jets-Re-Sign-T-Ben-Ijalana/b97e39a2-9de8-4a8c-995a-15a693d46114|archive-date=April 14, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 19, 2018, the Jets declined the second-year option on Ijalana's contract, making him a free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Reports: Jets won't pick up Ben Ijalana's option in 2018|url=https://www.ganggreennation.com/2018/2/19/17030508/reports-jets-wont-pick-up-ben-ijalanas-option-in-2018|website=GangGreenNation.com|date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> However on March 16, 2018, Ijalana re-signed with the Jets on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign Ben Ijalana To One Year Deal|url=https://www.ganggreennation.com/2018/3/16/17131306/jets-sign-ben-ijalana-to-one-year-deal|website=GangGreenNation.com|date=March 16, 2018}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 15, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Place Veteran T Ben Ijalana on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-veteran-t-ben-ijalana-on-injured-reserve|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=August 15, 2018}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On August 11, 2019, Ijalana was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars make roster moves|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves-x8812|website=Jaguars.com|date=August 11, 2019|access-date=August 11, 2019|archive-date=August 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190811192420/https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves-x8812|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster reduction: Jaguars move to 53 players|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-reduce-roster-to-53-players|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref>

==Executive career==
On June 3, 2022, Ijalana was hired by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as a scouting assistant.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/new-york-jets/jets-eagles-streak-mean/|title=Former Jets 'Mean Streak' Starter Is Joining the Eagles: Report|first=Paul A. '''Benjamin John Lynch''' (born November 18, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (American football)|center]] for four seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{cite web  |title=NFL All-Time Players |url=https://www.nfl.com/players/profile?id=LYN071058 |work=NFL.com |accessdate=March 28, 2011}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[California Golden Bears football|California Golden Bears]].

==Professional career==

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Lynch was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the seventh round (211th overall) of the [[1996 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1996 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1996/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was released on August 20.<ref>{{cite news |title=Transactions |url=https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=F20C13F739540C728EDDA10894DE494D81 |newspaper=The New York Times |date=August 21, 1996 |accessdate=March 28, 2011}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Lynch was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on February 10, 1997.

===Frankfurt Galaxy===
Lynch was selected by the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] in the first round (second overall) of the 1998 [[NFL Europe]] Draft.

===Houston Texans===
The [[Houston Texans]] signed Lynch on August 4, 2003.<ref>{{cite news |title=Transactions |url=https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=F60C13F8355A0C768CDDA10894DB404482 |newspaper=The New York Times |date=August 5, 2003 |accessdate=March 28, 2011}}</ref> He suffered a season-ending knee injury in a preseason game against the [[San Diego Chargers]] on August 23. The Texans placed him on the [[injured reserve list]] on August 25.

'''Benjamin Todd Fricke''' (November 13, 1975 – February 21, 2011) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (American football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He also was a member of the [[Amsterdam Admirals]] in [[NFL Europe]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Houston]].

==Early life==
Fricke attended [[Anderson High School (Austin, Texas)|Anderson High School]], where he was an All-district selection on both offense and defense as a sophomore and junior.

As a senior, he was switched to [[Center (American football)|center]] and was the team's [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]]. He also practiced [[track & field|track]].

==College career==
Fricke received a football scholarship from the [[University of Houston]] to play as a [[defensive lineman]]. As a freshman, he was moved to [[Center (gridiron football)|center]].

He became a four-year starter and was named [[All-American]] as a senior, when he did not allow a sack.

==Professional career==
===New York Giants===
Fricke was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the seventh round (213th overall) of the [[1998 NFL draft]], after dropping because he was considered undersized for the position.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=January 3, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/20/sports/nfl-draft-98-giants-to-sign-brown-and-cut-hampton.html | title=N.F.L. DRAFT '98; Giants to Sign Brown and Cut Hampton | website=[[The New York Times]] | date=April 20, 1998 | access-date=January 3, 2023 | last1=Pennington | first1=Bill }}</ref> He was waived on August 23.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/08/24/sports/transactions-502359.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | date=August 24, 1998 | access-date=January 3, 2018}}</ref>

===Amsterdam Admirals===
In [[1999 Amsterdam Admirals season|1999]], he was selected by the [[Amsterdam Admirals]] in the 11th round of the [[NFL Europe]] draft. He was the starter at [[Center (gridiron football)|center]], helping [[running back]] [[David Thompson (American football)|David Thompson]] finish fourth in the league with 503 rushing yards.

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 3, [[1999 NFL season|1999]], he signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[Dallas Cowboys]], to provide depth in training camp because of injuries.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/news/bs-xpm-1999-08-04-9908040049-story.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] | date=August 4, 1999 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref> He was cut on September 22. He was re-signed on October 5.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/news/bs-xpm-1999-10-06-9910060129-story.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] | date=October 6, 1999 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref> He was released on October 27 and signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/10/28/sports/transactions-172561.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | date=October 28, 1999 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 19. He appeared in 3 games and was declared inactive in 4 contests.

In [[2000 NFL season|2000]], he was declared inactive in 7 of the first 9 games. He started five games at [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in place of [[Mark Stepnoski]], who suffered a sprained MCL in his left knee in the eleventh game against the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/dallas/nfl/news/story?id=6154107 | title=Reports: Ben Fricke dies | date=February 24, 2011 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref>

In [[2001 NFL season|2001]], he was tried at long snapper during [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]] to replace the recently released [[Dale Hellestrae]], but remained as a backup at [[Center (gridiron football)|center]], appearing in 7 games. He was cut on June 13, [[2002 NFL season|2002]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/14/sports/transactions-542075.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | date=June 14, 2002 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
In June [[2002 NFL season|2002]], he was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He was released on August 8.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/08/09/sports/transactions-324280.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | date=August 9, 2002 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fricke was the offensive coordinator and offensive line coach at [[Centennial High School (Frisco, Texas)|Centennial High School]] for three years.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/high-school/post/_/id/5157/frisco-centennial-coach-ex-cowboy-dies-of-cancer | title=Centennial coach, ex-Cowboy dies of cancer | date=February 24, 2011 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref> On February 21, 2011, he died at the age of 35 from colon cancer.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/former-cowboys-center-ben-fricke-dies-at-35 | title=Former Cowboys center Ben Fricke dies at 35 | date=February 23, 2011 | access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Jones''' (born July 2, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]]. He was selected by the [[Houston Texans]] in the fourth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
A native of [[Centreville, Alabama]], Jones attended [[Bibb County High School]], where he was a two-way lineman and team captain. He paved the way for running back [[Zac Stacy]], who rushed for 1,666 yards and 24 touchdowns. Regarded as a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Jones was listed as the No. 7 center prospect in his class.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-1827 |title=Archived copy |access-date=April 19, 2014 |archive-date=April 21, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140421080716/https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-1827 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Despite living only an hour away from [[Tuscaloosa, Alabama]], Jones grew up a Georgia Bulldog fan.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://georgia.scout.com/2/653238.html |title=Scout.com: Jones picks Georgia |access-date=December 12, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419233726/http://georgia.scout.com/2/653238.html |archive-date=April 19, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Jones became the Bulldog starting center three games into his freshman season (at No. 24 [[2008 Arizona State Sun Devils football team|Arizona State]]), after [[Chris Davis (offensive lineman)|Chris Davis]] was moved to left guard.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.accessnorthga.com/detail.php?n=212120 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130116062057/http://www.accessnorthga.com/detail.php?n=212120 | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 16, 2013 | title=Davis happy to play where needed along Bulldog OL }}</ref> The centerpiece of a young offensive line, Jones helped protect quarterback [[Matthew Stafford]], who threw for 3,459 yards (second most in school history) and 25 touchdowns (single-season record), while also clearing the way for running back [[Knowshon Moreno]] (1,400 rushing yards).

As a senior in 2011, Jones was named an [[All-American]] by [[ESPN]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/college-football/feature/video?id=7324158&_slug_=2011-all-america-team ESPN.com's 2011 All-America Team]</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===

Jones was considered one of the top center prospects for the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=83254&draftyear=2012&genpos=C |title=NFL Draft Scout |access-date=December 10, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120511145400/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=83254&draftyear=2012&genpos=C |archive-date=May 11, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' ranked him second among center prospects, behind only [[Peter Konz]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/draft-2012/breakdowns/by_position/C.html |title=View Draft by Positions - 2012 Draft Tracker - SI.com |access-date=December 12, 2012 |archive-date=May 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515061842/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/draft-2012/breakdowns/by_position/C.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
[[File: Ben Jones (center).JPG|thumb|Jones with the Houston Texans in 2012]]
Jones was drafted in the fourth round by the [[Houston Texans]] with the 99th overall pick. He was one of only three centers selected, the other two being Konz and [[David Molk]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Jones was expected to back up Pro Bowl center [[Chris Myers (American football)|Chris Myers]] while also seeing time at guard. Starting in Week 7 of the 2012 NFL season against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Jones became the starting right guard for the Texans.

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 10, 2016, Jones signed a four-year contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Agree to Terms with Former Texans OL Ben Jones|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Agree-to-Terms-with-Former-Texans-OL-Ben-Jones/2ef4c7bf-c69d-41d7-a467-2eae893ef605|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TitansOnline.com|date=March 10, 2016|access-date=March 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310212550/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Agree-to-Terms-with-Former-Texans-OL-Ben-Jones/2ef4c7bf-c69d-41d7-a467-2eae893ef605|archive-date=March 10, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2016, he started all 16 games for Titans as they finished with a 9-7 record, from a 3-13 record the previous season. He blocked for [[DeMarco Murray|Demarco Murray]] as the latter led the AFC in rushing yards.

In 2017, Jones remained the starting center for the Titans, starting all 16 regular season games; the team finished with another 9-7 record and qualified for the playoffs. Jones started in the AFC Wild Card game against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], blocking for [[Derrick Henry]] as the latter ran for 157 yards in a 22-21 comeback win; the Titans were in a 22-3 deficit at halftime. He also started the Divisional Round game against the [[New England Patriots]], which resulted in a 35-14 loss.

In 2018, Jones started all 16 regular season games for the Titans, who finished with a third consecutive 9-7 record. He blocked for Derrick Henry as he was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month in December, running for 585 yards in the final four games of the season, including running for a career-high 238 yards and four touchdowns in a 30-9 week 14 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

[[File:Ben Jones 2019 10-13.jpg|thumb|Jones with the [[Tennessee Titans]] in 2019]]
Jones signed a two-year, $13.5 million contract extension with the Titans on August 30, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001045824/article/titans-c-ben-jones-agree-on-contract-extension|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831013717/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001045824/article/titans-c-ben-jones-agree-on-contract-extension|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 31, 2019|title=Titans, C Ben Jones agree on contract extension|first=Grant|last=Gordon|date=August 30, 2019|access-date=August 30, 2019}}</ref> In 2019, Jones started 15 regular season games, missing the week 9 game against the Carolina Panthers with a concussion.<ref>{{cite web|work=MusicCityMiracles.com|url=https://www.musiccitymiracles.com/2019/11/1/20943988/ben-jones-ruled-out-for-titans-panthers-and-other-injury-updates-from-fridays-practice|title=Ben Jones, Delanie Walker, and Jurrell Casey ruled out for Titans-Panthers and other injury updates from Friday's practice|first=Mike B.|last=Herndon|date=November 1, 2019|access-date=April 17, 2020}}</ref> The Titans finishing with a fourth consecutive 9-7 record, with Jones blocking for Derrick Henry as he won the NFL rushing yards title. The Titans qualified for the playoffs, making it to the AFC conference championships and losing to eventual Super Bowl Champions Kansas City Chiefs. Jones started all three playoff games, and blocked for Henry as he ran for nearly 200 yards in each of the first two games.

In 2020, Jones started all 16 games in the regular season and blocked for Henry as he won his second rushing yards title and was named [[Offensive Player of the Year]] by becoming the eighth player in NFL history to run for more than [[2,000-yard club|2,000 yards in a season]]. The Titans won the AFC South with an 11-5 record. In the playoffs, Jones started for the Titans as they lost to the Baltimore Ravens in the wildcard round.

On March 15, 2022, Jones signed a two-year, $14 million contract extension with the Titans.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Agree to Terms on Multi-Year Contract Extension with Center Ben Jones|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-on-multi-year-contract-extension-with-center-ben-jones|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=March 15, 2022}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on December 22, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Place C Ben Jones, CB Terrance Mitchell on Injured Reserve While Signing OL Daniel Munyer to Active Roster|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-place-c-ben-jones-cb-terrance-mitchell-on-injured-reserve-while-signing-o|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=December 22, 2022}}</ref> In January 2023, Jones was named as a replacement player for [[Creed Humphrey]] to the [[2023 Pro Bowl]], his first Pro Bowl.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jim|last=Wyatt|title=Titans Center Ben Jones Named to Pro Bowl Roster|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-center-ben-jones-named-to-pro-bowl-roster|work=TennesseeTitans.com|date=January 30, 2023|accessdate=February 1, 2023}}</ref>

On March 10, 2023, Jones was released by the Titans.<ref>{{cite web|work=TennesseeTitans.com|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-part-ways-with-center-ben-jones|title=Titans Part Ways With Center Ben Jones|date=March 10, 2023|accessdate=March 11, 2023|first=Jim|last=Wyatt}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Scott Nelson''' (born August 21, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). He was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2003 and played in three games on [[special teams]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[St. Cloud State Huskies football|St. Cloud State Huskies]].

Nelson was  the [[AFL Rookie of the Year]] in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.stcloudstate.edu/news/scsunow/default.asp?storyID=19250 |title=Former Husky named AFL Rookie of the Year: Ben Nelson |access-date=August 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055648/http://www.stcloudstate.edu/news/scsunow/default.asp?storyID=19250 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 1, 2015, the SaberCats placed Nelson on reassignment. On June 2, 2015, he was claimed by the [[Spokane Shock]]. On June 3, 2015, Nelson was placed on recallable reassignment. On June 19, 2015, Nelson was assigned to the San Jose SaberCats.

'''Benjamin David Gardner''' (born April 29, 1991) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]] and was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the seventh round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[San Diego Chargers]].

==Early life==

Gardner graduated in 2009 from [[Homestead High School (Mequon, Wisconsin)|Homestead High School]]. As a senior in 2008–09, Gardner was a team captain and defensive end on the football team which won the Wisconsin Division I state championship.

He received numerous top honors including 2008 [[Associated Press]] 1st-team All-State;<ref>{{cite news | title=AP announces Wisconsin high school football all-state team | publisher=ABC News 9}}</ref> 2008 WFCA 1st-Team All-State;<ref name="GoStanford p. 29">{{cite web |url=https://gostanford.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7152 | title=Ben Gardner profile | access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref> 2008 all-North Shore Conference First;<ref name="GoStanford p. 29"/> and 2008 North Shore Conference Defensive Player of the Year.<ref name="GoStanford p. 29"/>

==College career==

[[Stanford Cardinal football]] is known for its [[3-4 defense|3–4 defense schemes]], more typically seen in the NFL.  Gardner was a three-year starter at [[defensive end]] in the Stanford 3–4 system, which was ranked among the nation's top defensive units.<ref>{{cite news | title=Top defensive units | publisher=Scout.com}}</ref>

Gardner did not see field action in his first year (2009). As a sophomore or "redshirt freshman" in 2010, Gardner saw action in 11 games on special teams and as a second-string defensive end. He logged three tackles, including two tackles for loss and one sack.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cfbstats.com/2010/player/674/1026154/index.html |title=Ben Gardner stats |access-date=April 3, 2023 |archive-date=November 23, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171123203032/http://www.cfbstats.com/2010/player/674/1026154/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2011, he started 12 of 13 games, including the [[Fiesta Bowl]] vs. 13th nationally ranked Oklahoma state. Gardner recorded 35 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks. He was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12]] Conference 2nd Team,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/pac12/post/_/id/30623/coaches-all-pac-12-teams-announced |title=Coaches All-Pac-12 teams announced | access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref> and received Stanford's Deswarte-Eller Award honoring the most outstanding (redshirt) sophomore. Gardner ranked 13th in the Pac-12 in tackles for loss per game, and 16th in sacks per game.<ref name="GoStanford p. 29"/> He had a season-high five tackles and one sack vs. California and a season-high 2.5 tackles for loss vs. Arizona.

Gardner started all 14 games of the 2012 season, including the [[2012 Pac-12 Football Championship Game|Pac-12 Championship Game]] vs. [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] and the [[2013 Rose Bowl]] vs. [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]]. Gardner tied for second on the Stanford team with 14.5 tackles for loss and 7.5 sacks.<ref name="GoStanford p. 29"/> He also ranked among the nation's top 75 in both categories.<ref name="GoStanford p. 29"/> Against #2-ranked [[USC Trojans football|USC]], Gardner won Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Week honors for registering 6 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss and one sack, holding USC to 26 rushing yards.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/pac12/post/_/id/45120/pac-12-players-of-the-week-15 |title=Pac-12 players of the week | access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref> Playing at #7-ranked [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], Gardner made two solo tackles, one fumble recovery, and one sack which caused a fumble that was recovered for a Stanford touchdown.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/notre-dame-football/post/_/id/10148/turnovers-alarming-but-still-work-in-progress |title=Turnovers alarming, but still work in progress | access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref> Gardner's season also included 49 tackles, 5 passes broken up, and 2 quarterback hurries.

He chose to return to Stanford for a fifth year in 2013, rather than enter the [[NFL draft]], but it ended early because of a torn pectoral muscle he suffered against [[Oregon State University]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://stanforddaily.com/2014/05/05/nfl-draft-profile-ben-gardner/ |title=NFL Draft profile: Ben Gardner | access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys===
Gardner was selected in the seventh round (231 overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref name=Drafted>{{cite news|title=Cowboys Go All Defense With Five Seventh-Rounders|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-go-all-defense-with-five-seventh-rounders-349081 |access-date=April 3, 2023|newspaper=Dallascowboys.com|date=May 10, 2019}}</ref> On August 26, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] after having surgery to repair torn ligaments in his left shoulder. The next year, the team brought in new talent at the [[defensive end]] position ([[Greg Hardy]], [[Randy Gregory]], [[Ryan Russell (American football)|Ryan Russell]]) and he was eventually waived on September 5, [[2015 NFL season|2015]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/vaughan-showers-among-notable-cuts-as-cowboys-meet-53-man-roster-limit-384546 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806020247/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2015/09/05/vaughan-showers-among-notable-cuts-cowboys-meet-53-man-roster-limit |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 6, 2017 |title=Vaughan, Showers Among Notable Cuts As Cowboys Meet 53-Man Roster Limit |last=Helman |first=David |date=September 5, 2015 |website=DallasCowboys.com |access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref>

===San Diego Chargers===
On November 4, [[2015 NFL season|2015]], Gardner was signed to the [[San Diego Chargers]] [[practice squad]] and switched to play [[outside linebacker]] in a [[3-4 defense]]. 
On September 3, [[2016 NFL season|2016]], he was cut by the Chargers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Cut Down Roster to 53|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-cut-down-roster-to-53-136471|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903074259/http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/03/chargers-cut-down-roster-53|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 3, 2017|last=Henne|first=Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=September 3, 2016|access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref> The next day, he was signed to the Chargers' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Announce 2016 Practice Squad|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-2016-practice-squad-136601|website=Chargers.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161126014220/http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/04/chargers-announce-2016-practice-squad|archive-date=November 26, 2016|url-status=dead|access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref> He was released on October 4.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bolts Add Trio to Practice Squad|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/bolts-add-trio-to-practice-squad-139016|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=October 4, 2016|access-date=April 3, 2023}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Koyack''' ({{Respell|KOY|ack}}; born April 9, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the seventh round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]].

==Early life==
Koyack attended [[Oil City Area School District|Oil City High School]] in [[Oil City, Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 1, 2010 |title=Koyack hits right tune on the football field |url=https://www.ctpost.com/sports/article/Koyack-hits-right-tune-on-the-football-field-642201.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202060947/https://www.ctpost.com/sports/article/Koyack-hits-right-tune-on-the-football-field-642201.php |archive-date=December 2, 2021 |access-date=May 20, 2023 |work=[[Connecticut Post]]}}</ref> He played [[high school football|football]] and [[baseball]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bodani |first=Frank |date=April 27, 2010 |title=PSU recruiting spotlight: Ben Koyack a rare talent |url=http://www.ydr.com/psu/ci_14711363 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141017124832/http://www.ydr.com/psu/ci_14711363 |archive-date=October 17, 2014 |website=[[York Daily Record]]}}</ref> In football, he played numerous positions, including [[tight end]], [[quarterback]], [[wide receiver]], [[defensive end]], and [[linebacker]]. He finished his career with a [[PIAA District 10]] record 152 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 2,591 yards. He was selected to play in the 2011 [[Under Armour All-America Game]] in [[St. Petersburg, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Phillips |first=Craig |title=Koyack to play in Under Armour All-American game |url=http://ocpafootball.tripod.com/id422.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141018213835/http://ocpafootball.tripod.com/id422.htm |archive-date=October 18, 2014 |website=OCPA Football|via=The Derrick/The News-Herald}}</ref>

Koyack was also a standout [[track & field]] athlete. He captured the state championship in the [[javelin throw|javelin]] with a throw of {{convert|192|ft|11|in|m|abbr=on}}. He also qualified for the district meet competing as a sprinter, posting bests of 11.49 seconds in the [[100 meters]] and 24.05 seconds in the [[200 meters]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Koyack {{pipe}} Notre Dame TE |url=https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/ben-koyack-785/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414001804/https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/ben-koyack-785/ |archive-date=April 14, 2015 |access-date=April 7, 2015 |website=Tracking Football}}</ref>

Koyack was ranked by [[247Sports]] as the fourth best tight end in his class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Koyack, Jacksonville Jaguars, Tight End |url=https://247sports.com/player/ben-koyack-1526/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150719053452/http://247sports.com/Player/Ben-Koyack-1526 |archive-date=July 19, 2015 |access-date=May 20, 2023 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Notre Dame]] in April 2010 to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Funk |first=Joshua |date=April 29, 2010 |title=Oil City Area TE Ben Koyack commits to Notre Dame |url=https://www.pennlive.com/westernpafootball/2010/04/oil_city_area_te_ben_koyack_co.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202060947/https://www.pennlive.com/westernpafootball/2010/04/oil_city_area_te_ben_koyack_co.html |archive-date=December 2, 2021 |access-date=May 20, 2023 |website=PennLive.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On December 22, 2014, it was announced that Koyack had accepted his invitation to play in the [[2015 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hansen |first=Eric |date=December 22, 2017 |title=Notre Dame's Ben Koyack accepts invite to Senior Bowl |url=https://www.ndinsider.com/football/notre-dame-s-ben-koyack-accepts-invite-to-senior-bowl/article_cbd66644-8a33-11e4-90a4-e3dfb2c74ba4.html |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=NDinsider.com}}</ref> Koyack impressed team representatives and scouts in practice while working with [[Tennessee Titans]] tight ends coach [[Mike Mularkey]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arkush |first=Arthur |date=January 24, 2015 |title=Notre Dame tight end Ben Koyack lauded for improvement during Senior Bowl week |url=http://www.profootballweekly.com/2015/01/24/notre-dame-tight-end-ben-koyack-lauded-for-improvement-during-senior-bowl-week/aqocj82/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223043129/http://www.profootballweekly.com/2015/01/24/notre-dame-tight-end-ben-koyack-lauded-for-improvement-during-senior-bowl-week/aqocj82/ |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=ProFootballWeekly.com}}</ref> On January 24, 2015, Koyack played in the [[Senior Bowl]] for Tennessee Titan's head coach [[Ken Whisenhunt|Ken Whisenhunt's]] North team and caught two passes for 19-yards and a touchdown. He caught a 10-yard touchdown reception on pass from [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]] quarterback [[Sean Mannion (American football)|Sean Mannion]] in the second quarter of the North's 34–13 victory over the South.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Reese's Senior Bowl |url=http://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400859832 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171206140226/http://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400859832 |archive-date=December 6, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was one of 19 collegiate tight ends to attend the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. Koyack opted to not perform at the combine and only meet with representatives from NFL teams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=James |first=Tyler |date=March 31, 2015 |title=Former Notre Dame TE Ben Koyack proving passion with heavy workload |url=https://www.ndinsider.com/football/former-notre-dame-te-ben-koyack-proving-passion-with-heavy/article_e704849c-d807-11e4-847e-23e9793b0d47.html |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=NDInsider.com}}</ref> On March 31, 2015, Koyack attended [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame's]] [[pro day]] along with 10 other teammates. Team representatives and scouts attended the pro day as he ran all of the combine drills.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2015 |title=2015 Fighting Irish Football Pro Day Coverage |url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/033115aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223043717/http://www.und.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/033115aaa.html |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=Notre Dame Fighting Irish – Official Athletics Website}}</ref> His time of 4.79s in the [[40-yard dash]] would've tied for fourth among all tight ends at the combine. His overall performance in combine drills was mediocre as his [[vertical jump]] ranked last of his position group and his [[bench press]] would've ranked ninth.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brady |first=James |date=February 22, 2015 |title=NFL Combine 2015: Full results for tight ends |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2015/2/22/8087821/nfl-combine-2015-full-results-tight-ends |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052154/https://www.sbnation.com/platform/amp/nfl/2015/2/22/8087821/nfl-combine-2015-full-results-tight-ends |archive-date=December 22, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Koyack was projected to be a fourth or fifth-round pick by NFL experts and scouts. He was ranked as the seventh best tight end prospect by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Koyack, DS #7 TE, Notre Dame |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=119436&draftyear=2015&genpos=TE |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223042942/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=119436&draftyear=2015&genpos=TE |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref>
