===2015===
The  [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] selected Koyack in the seventh round (229th overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He was the 14th tight end selected and the only player drafted from Notre Dame in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Ben Koyack Chosen in NFL Draft |url=https://und.com/ben-koyack-chosen-in-nfl-draft/ |access-date=May 20, 2023 |website=Notre Dame Fighting Irish – Official Athletics Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022150939/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |archive-date=October 22, 2018 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On May 14, 2015, the Jaguars signed Koyack to a four-year $2.35 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $69,300.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=June 8, 2015 |title=Jaguars rookie Ben Koyack's contract worth nearly $2.35 million |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/jacksonville-jaguars/post/_/id/13117/jaguars-rookie-ben-koyacks-contract-worth-nearly-2-35-million |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160909120006/http://www.espn.com/blog/jacksonville-jaguars/post/_/id/13117/jaguars-rookie-ben-koyacks-contract-worth-nearly-2-35-million |archive-date=September 9, 2016 |access-date=May 20, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

Throughout [[training camp]], he competed against [[Clay Harbor]], [[Nic Jacobs]], and [[Connor Hamlett]] for a roster spot.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Jacksonville Jaguars' depth chart: 07/01/2015 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/176/JAX |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223102110/http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/176/JAX |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 4, 2015, he was waived as a part of the Jaguars final roster cuts. The Jaguars opted to have only four tight ends on their active roster, including [[Marcedes Lewis]], [[Julius Thomas]], Nic Jacobs, and Clay Harbor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2015 |title=Roster moves: Eighteen done, four to go |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Roster-moves-Eighteen-done-four-to-go/580bdeae-b80c-4e0c-ac6b-7a9317c3bf49 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826071445/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Roster-moves-Eighteen-done-four-to-go/580bdeae-b80c-4e0c-ac6b-7a9317c3bf49 |archive-date=August 26, 2017 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> After clearing waivers, Koyack was signed to the Jaguars' [[practice squad]] on September 6, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2015 |title=Jaguars sign eight to practice squad |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-sign-eight-to-practice-squad/7bfafe23-7c40-4fa2-8b7f-f1abb75b2c7a |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907171006/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-sign-eight-to-practice-squad/7bfafe23-7c40-4fa2-8b7f-f1abb75b2c7a |archive-date=September 7, 2015 |access-date=September 7, 2015 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He spent his entire rookie season developing on the Jaguars' practice squad.

===2016===
On January 4, 2016, the Jaguars signed Koyack to a reserve/futures contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaye |first=Mike |date=January 4, 2016 |title=Koyack, Wolff among nine players to sign futures contracts with Jaguars |url=https://www.firstcoastnews.com/article/sports/koyack-wolff-among-nine-players-to-sign-futures-contracts-with-jaguars/77-17721039 |access-date=May 20, 2023 |website=First Coast News |language=en-US}}</ref>

He competed with Jacobs, [[Braedon Bowman]], and [[Neal Sterling]] throughout training camp for a roster spot. He made the active roster and was named the backup tight end behind Lewis and Thomas to start the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Jacksonville Jaguars' depth chart: 10/01/2016 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/188/JAX |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024152700/http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/188/JAX |archive-date=October 24, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Jaguars' season-opening 27–23 loss to the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Jacksonville Jaguars – September 11th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828231454/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110jax.htm |archive-date=August 28, 2017 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On September 24, 2016, Koyack underwent successful surgery to repair a slight tear in his [[meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]]. He suffered the tear four days earlier during practice and was inactive for the next two games (Weeks 3–4).<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 24, 2015 |title=Jaguars' Ben Koyack: Undergoes knee surgery |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-ben-koyack-undergoes-knee-surgery/amp/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223043230/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-ben-koyack-undergoes-knee-surgery/amp/ |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> On October 26, 2016, Koyack caught five passes for 41 yards during a 36–22 loss at the Titans. His first career reception came in the fourth quarter on a seven-yard pass by quarterback [[Blake Bortles]] before being tackled by Titans' defensive backs [[Daimion Stafford]] and [[Antwon Blake]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Tennessee Titans – October 27th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610270oti.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829161606/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610270oti.htm |archive-date=August 29, 2017 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Koyack saw an increased snap count after offensive coordinator [[Greg Olson (American football)|Greg Olson]] was fired on October 29, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carlyon |first=Hays |date=November 15, 2016 |title=Jaguars failing to properly utilize TE Julius Thomas |url=http://jacksonville.com/sports/2016-11-15/jaguars-failing-properly-utilize-te-julius-thomas |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223110729/http://jacksonville.com/sports/2016-11-15/jaguars-failing-properly-utilize-te-julius-thomas |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |access-date=December 22, 2017 |website=Jacksonville.com}}</ref> On November 13, 2016, he earned his first career start and caught three passes for 35-yards in a 24–21 loss to the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars – November 13th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611130jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108032656/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611130jax.htm |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 1, 2017, Koyack had three receptions for 25 yards and a touchdown during a 24–20 loss at the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He scored his first career touchdown during the game on a 14-yard pass by Blake Bortles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Indianapolis Colts – January 1st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701010clt.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828232710/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701010clt.htm |archive-date=August 28, 2017 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Koyack finished the 2016 season with 19 receptions for 161 receiving yards and a touchdown in 14 games and seven starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Koyack 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KoyaBe00/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180418033430/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KoyaBe00/gamelog/2016/ |archive-date=April 18, 2018 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

'''Benjamin N. Garland''' (born April 6, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Denver Broncos]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], and [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Air Force Falcons football|Air Force Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bengarland63.com/bio/military/ |title=Military Biography |publisher=bengarland63.com |access-date=May 4, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505015519/http://bengarland63.com/bio/military/ |archive-date=May 5, 2015 }}</ref> Garland was originally a [[defensive lineman]] before converting to an offensive lineman in 2012.<ref name="A"/>

==Early life==
Garland [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] four years in football and one in basketball for the [[Central High School (Grand Junction, Colorado)|Central High School]] Warriors of [[Grand Junction, Colorado]]. He earned first-team all-state honors in football as a senior. He was also an all-conference and all-district selection.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.goairforcefalcons.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/ben_garland_301597.html | title=Ben Garland93 | publisher=goairforcefalcons.com | access-date=November 10, 2014 | archive-date=November 10, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110195219/http://www.goairforcefalcons.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/ben_garland_301597.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Garland attended the [[United States Air Force Academy]] and played for the [[Air Force Falcons football|Falcons]] from 2006 to 2009. He totaled 115 tackles, 11.5 sacks, three forced fumbles, and two blocked kicks in 39 career games, starting 34 of them.<ref name="A">{{cite web | url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/team/roster/Ben-Garland/5a313eab-406c-4f4b-8dd3-3971214d7d9f | title=Ben Garland | publisher=denverbroncos.com | access-date=November 10, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110212202/http://www.denverbroncos.com/team/roster/Ben-Garland/5a313eab-406c-4f4b-8dd3-3971214d7d9f | archive-date=November 10, 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
Garland was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] on April 25, 2010, after going undrafted in the [[2010 NFL draft]]. The Broncos placed Garland on the reserve/military list on September 4, 2010, to serve his two-year military commitment.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.denverpost.com/broncos/ci_26904683/briefs-ben-garlands-debut-perfect-timing-broncos?source=infinite | title=Briefs: Ben Garland's debut perfect timing for Broncos | publisher=denverpost.com | date=November 10, 2014 | access-date=November 10, 2014}}</ref> He was released by the Broncos on August 31, 2012. He was signed to the Broncos' practice squad on September 1, 2012.

Garland signed a futures contract on January 15, 2013.<ref>{{cite news|work=DenverPost.com|url=http://blogs.denverpost.com/broncos/2013/01/15/ben-garland-air-force-dt-signs-futures-contract-broncos/18219/|title=Ben Garland, former Air Force DT, signs futures contract with Broncos|first=Jeff |last=Legwold|date=January 15, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2017}}</ref> He was released by the Broncos on August 30, 2013, and signed to the team's practice squad on September 4, 2013. Garland reached [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] with the Broncos, but the team lost 43–8 to the Seattle Seahawks. Garland signed a futures deal with the Broncos on February 4, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/23139/nfl/news |title=Ben Garland |publisher=kffl.com |access-date=November 10, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204181727/http://www.kffl.com/player/23139/nfl/news |archive-date=December 4, 2014 }}</ref> He made his NFL debut on November 9, 2014, against the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GarlBe00/gamelog// | title=Ben Garland | publisher=Sports Reference LLC | work=pro-football-reference.com | access-date=November 10, 2014}}</ref> He was released by the Broncos on September 5, 2015.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.denverpost.com/broncos/ci_28764068/denver-broncos-roster-cuts-53 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905175458/http://www.denverpost.com/broncos/ci_28764068/denver-broncos-roster-cuts-53 | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 5, 2015 | title=Steven Johnson, Ben Garland among Broncos' roster cuts | publisher=denverpost.com | date=September 5, 2015 | access-date=September 5, 2015 | author=Jhabvala, Nick}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
Garland was signed to the [[Atlanta Falcons]]' practice squad on September 9, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/article-1/Falcons-Sign-G-Garland-to-Practice-Squad/44bbd8ac-a855-41c5-96ae-73945514e284 |title=FALCONS SIGN G GARLAND TO PRACTICE SQUAD |publisher=atlantafalcons.com |date=September 9, 2015 |access-date=September 9, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910021555/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/article-1/Falcons-Sign-G-Garland-to-Practice-Squad/44bbd8ac-a855-41c5-96ae-73945514e284 |archive-date=September 10, 2015 }}</ref> On December 15, 2015, he was signed to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/S-Moore-Placed-on-IR-WR-Hankerson-Waived-/c643a409-7212-467a-89d1-fed41d72e74b |title=S Moore Placed on IR, WR Hankerson Waived |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |date=December 15, 2015 |access-date=December 16, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151216180601/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/S-Moore-Placed-on-IR-WR-Hankerson-Waived-/c643a409-7212-467a-89d1-fed41d72e74b |archive-date=December 16, 2015 }}</ref> On January 14, 2017, Garland lined up at defensive tackle and recorded his first career safety after downing [[Russell Wilson]] during the NFC Divisional Playoff against the [[Seattle Seahawks]].

The following week, Garland and the Falcons reached [[Super Bowl LI]] after winning the NFC Championship. Against the [[2016 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in Super Bowl LI, the Falcons lost 34–28 in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201702050atl.htm|title=Super Bowl LI - New England Patriots vs. Atlanta Falcons - February 5th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=August 6, 2017}}</ref>

In 2017, Garland played in all 16 games, starting three at left guard in place of the injured [[Andy Levitre]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Garland 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GarlBe00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=2025-05-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 12, 2018, the Falcons placed a second-round restricted free agent tender on Garland.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons use second-round tender on Ben Garland as well|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/12/falcons-use-second-round-tender-on-ben-garland-as-well/|author=Alper, Josh|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=March 12, 2018}}</ref> He played in 14 games in 2018, starting four at right guard.

===San Francisco 49ers===
On April 23, 2019, Garland signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. Garland was moved to center in week 15 following an injury to starting center [[Weston Richburg]].<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign OL Ben Garland|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-ol-ben-garland|website=49ers.com|date=April 23, 2019}}</ref> Garland helped the 49ers reach [[Super Bowl LIV]], but they lost 31–20 to the [[2019 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]].

On March 30, 2020, Garland re-signed with the 49ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers bring back center Ben Garland|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/18/49ers-bring-back-center-ben-garland/|author=Gantt, Darin|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=March 18, 2020}}</ref> He started five games at center before being placed on injured reserve on October 20, 2020, with a calf strain.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-add-parnell-motley-place-ben-garland-ir|website=49ers.com|date=October 20, 2020}}

On February 3rd, Garland won the Steven Cheah BOY Award for his block against the Colts from the regular season.</ref>

==Military career==
===U.S. Air Force===
Garland was stationed at [[Scott Air Force Base]] as a [[Public affairs (military)|Public Affairs Officer]] from 2010 to 2012 while assigned to the Denver Broncos Military Reserve players list. Garland held the rank of [[second lieutenant]] during this time.

===Colorado Air National Guard===
Garland was approved for his separation from active duty in May 2012 and joined the [[Colorado Air National Guard]] as a Public Affairs Officer with the 140th Wing stationed at [[Buckley Air Force Base]] in [[Aurora, Colorado]]. He is currently a [[Major (United States)|Major]] and fulfills his military obligations between NFL seasons.

==Personal life==
Garland is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Garland |url=https://mobile.twitter.com/BenGarland63/status/1079374171711389703 |website=Twitter |access-date=3 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Garland |url=https://mobile.twitter.com/BenGarland63/status/1175787944386281477 |website=Twitter |access-date=3 February 2020}}</ref> Garland is a supporter of Waterboys, a charity that tries to provide clean, accessible drinking water to communities in need around the world.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Garland |date=January 27, 2020 |url=https://waterboys.org/player/ben-garland/ |access-date=3 February 2020}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Earl Garry''' (February 11, 1956 – June 24, 2006) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] who played two seasons with the [[Baltimore Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the Colts in the sixth round of the [[1978 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Southern Mississippi]].

==Early life==
Benjamin Earl Garry was born on February 11, 1956, in [[Hazlehurst, Mississippi]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/g/garr03600.html | title=Ben Garry | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He attended Pascagoula High School in [[Pascagoula, Mississippi]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

==College career==
Garry was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Mississippi Golden Eagles]] of the [[University of Southern Mississippi]] from 1974 to 1977.<ref name="Pfa"/> He rushed 90	times for 379 yards and three touchdowns his freshman year in 1974.<ref name="Sr">{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ben-garry-1.html?__hstc=223721476.cf5f44155f2e36f92dc58b684a6e9a44.1694291523663.1735019795943.1735090670708.1004&__hssc=223721476.4.1735090670708&__hsfp=3542455373 | title=Ben Garry | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> In 1975, he recorded 178 carries for 846 yards and nine touchdowns, and nine catches for 47 yards and one touchdown.<ref name="Sr"/> He totaled 236	rushing attempts for 1,236 yards and eight touchdowns in 1976 while also catching for 15 passes for 126 yards.<ref name="Sr"/> As a senior in 1977, Garry rushed 219 times for 1,134 yards and ten touchdowns, earning honorable mention [[All-American]] and [[Associated Press]] first-team All-South Independent honors.<ref name="Sr"/><ref name="Sm"/> His 3,595 career rushing yards set a school record.<ref name="Sm"/> He played in the [[Senior Bowl]] after his senior season.<ref name="Sm">{{cite web | url=https://southernmiss.com/news/2006/8/22/Former_Golden_Eagles_To_Be_Honored_At_All_American_Football_Foundation_s_79th_Banquet_Of_Champions | title=Former Golden Eagles To Be Honored At All-American Football Foundation's 79th Banquet Of Champions | publisher=southernmiss.com | date=August 22, 2006 | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> Garry was inducted into Southern Miss' M-Club Sports Hall of Fame in 1998.<ref name="Sm"/>

==Professional career==
Garry was selected by the [[Baltimore Colts]] in the sixth round, with the 161st overall pick, of the [[1978 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GarrBe20.htm | title=Ben Garry | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He did not sign with the team until December 20, 1978.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/g/garr03600.html | title=Ben Garry NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://virginiachronicle.com/?a=d&d=SNH19781221.1.9&e=-------en-20--1--txt-txIN-------- | title=Colts Sign Running Back | work=[[Suffolk News-Herald]] | date=December 21, 1978 | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He played in 11 games for the Colts in 1979, totaling 13 carries for 41 yards, three receptions for nine yards, and eight kick returns for 135 yards.<ref name="Pfr"/> Garry appeared in three games for the Colts during the 1980 season, recording one catch for nine yards, three kick returns for 55 yards, one fumble, and one fumble recovery.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was placed on injured reserve on October 9, 1980.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released by the Colts on July 13, 1981.<ref name="transactions"/>

Garry signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] on July 17, 1981, but was later released.<ref name="transactions"/>

==Death==
Garry died in a car accident on June 24, 2006, in [[Mobile, Alabama]].<ref name="Pfa"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.vicksburgpost.com/2006/06/28/go-go-garry-prolific-usm-running-back-dies-at-5062806/ | title=‘Go-Go’ Garry, prolific USM running back, dies at 50 | publisher=vicksburgpost.com | date=June 28, 2006 | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="Sm"/> He posthumously received the Bill Wade Unsung Hero Award at the All-American Football Foundation's 79th Banquet of Champions in August 2006.<ref name="Sm"/>

'''Ben Heeney''' (born May 13, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas Jayhawks]].

==Early life==
Heeney attended [[Hutchinson High School (Kansas)|Hutchinson High School]] in [[Hutchinson, Kansas]]. Helping to lead the Salthawks to three state titles. He played [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] and [[running back]]. As a senior, he ran for a school record 2,083 yards and 39 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Deters | first=Jeff | title=KU's Ben Heeney looking to leave lasting impression in final season | website=The Topeka Capital-Journal | date=2014-08-17 | url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/2014/08/17/kus-ben-heeney-looking-leave-lasting-impression-final-season/16659549007/ | access-date=2025-07-20}}</ref> He also had 143 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and four [[interceptions]]. Heeney committed to the [[University of Kansas]] to play [[college football]].

==College career==
Heeney played at Kansas from 2011 to 2014. As a [[true freshman]], he played in all 12 games and had eight tackles. As a [[sophomore]] in 2012, Heeney started all 12 games, recording 112 tackles and a [[Quarterback sack|sack]].<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article1275834.html Linebacker Ben Heeney is a diamond on a rough KU football team]</ref> As a junior in 2013, he played and started in 10 games, missing two due to injury. He finished the season with 88 tackles, two sacks and three interceptions. As a senior in 2014, Heeney again started all 12 games, finishing with 127 tackles, 1.5 sacks and one interception.<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article10775270.html Kansas linebacker Ben Heeney wouldn’t mind being the next Chris Borland]</ref><ref>[http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2014/sep/02/ben-heeney-diabolical-defender/ Ben Heeney is … ‘The Diabolical Defender’]</ref><ref>[http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2014/oct/23/heeney-earns-respect-ex-ku-players/ Ben Heeney, an appreciation]</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oakland Raiders===
Heeney was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the fifth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]] with the 140th overall pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Take Kansas LB Ben Heeney in the 5th Round|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/2015-Draft/article-1/Raiders-Take-Kansas-LB-Ben-Heeney-in-the-5th-Round/ab9e6fbe-7a1c-48ce-a89d-9a08a4733cc7|website=Raiders.com|date=May 2, 2015|access-date=June 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909011429/http://www.raiders.com/news/2015-Draft/article-1/Raiders-Take-Kansas-LB-Ben-Heeney-in-the-5th-Round/ab9e6fbe-7a1c-48ce-a89d-9a08a4733cc7|archive-date=September 9, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on October 4, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Sign LB Perry Riley Jr.; Heeney To Reserve/Injured List|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-LB-Perry-Riley-Jr-Heeney-To-ReserveInjured-List/1b503a7c-c225-4ef5-b277-f762cba2a909|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911211704/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-LB-Perry-Riley-Jr-Heeney-To-ReserveInjured-List/1b503a7c-c225-4ef5-b277-f762cba2a909|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 11, 2017|website=Raiders.com|date=October 4, 2016}}</ref> On July 25, 2017, the Raiders placed Heeney on the [[non-football injury list]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Place TE Cooper Helfet & LB Ben Heeny On NFI List|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/raiders-place-te-cooper-helfet-ben-heeny-nfi-list/|author=Bouda, Nate|date=July 25, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/f671cc9c-caa3-429f-992e-5629667b4dec|website=Raiders.com|date=September 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171209084351/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/f671cc9c-caa3-429f-992e-5629667b4dec|archive-date=December 9, 2017|url-status=dead|access-date=September 8, 2017}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On September 22, 2017, Heeney was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints sign linebacker Ben Heeney to the practice squad: source|url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2017/09/saints_sign_linebacker_ben_hee.html|website=NOLA.com|date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 27, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints place David Parry on injured reserve, promote Ben Heeney from practice squad|url=http://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/sports/saints/article_6cfb5c46-a3cc-11e7-a327-57d437e642e5.html|author=Underhill, Nick|website=TheAdvocate.com|date=September 27, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on October 3, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=October 3, 2017 |title=Saints Cut DL Kendall Langford & LB Ben Heeney |url=http://nfltraderumors.co/saints-cut-dl-kendall-langford-lb-ben-heeney/ |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On October 4, 2017, the [[Houston Texans]] claimed Heeney off waivers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans claim Ben Heeney off waivers from Saints|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/10/04/texans-claim-ben-heeney-off-waivers-from-saints/|author=Williams, Charean|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=October 4, 2017}}</ref> The team placed him on injured reserve on November 29, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans place Chris Clark, Ben Heeney on IR|url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-place-Chris-Clark-Ben-Heeney-on-IR/e4ecc0cd-ded4-4cc5-9aed-9f981570146b|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=November 29, 2017|access-date=November 30, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201041159/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-place-Chris-Clark-Ben-Heeney-on-IR/e4ecc0cd-ded4-4cc5-9aed-9f981570146b|archive-date=December 1, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 26, 2018, Heeney re-signed with the Texans.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans re-sign Ben Heeney, cut Deante' Gray|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/26/texans-re-sign-ben-heeney-cut-deante-gray/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=March 26, 2018}}</ref> On August 29, 2018, he was waived with an injury designation by the Texans after having ankle surgery. After going unclaimed on waivers, was placed on the Texans injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans linebacker Ben Heeney out for the season after ankle surgery|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/08/29/texans-linebacker-ben-heeney-out-for-the-season-after-ankle-surgery/|author=Gantt, Darin|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 29, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 8, 2018.

===New York Guardians===
Heeney was selected by the [[New York Guardians]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] in round one of phase three of the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2858156-xfl-draft-2019-results-rosters-day-1-selections-for-each-team|title=XFL Draft 2019 Results: Rosters, Day 1 Selections for Each Team|first=Tim|last=Daniels|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=October 15, 2019|access-date=October 16, 2019}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

'''Ben Gottschalk''' (born February 15, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU Mustangs]], and subsequently played in the NFL with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

==Early life==
Gottschalk is Jewish, and is from [[Sherman Oaks, Los Angeles]], California.<ref name="ers1">{{cite web |url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-WaiveInjured-OL-Ben-Gottschalk/b8787c9a-f503-4603-8c93-bc341c9378a5 |title=49ers Waive/Injured OL Ben Gottschalk |website=49ers.com |date= |accessdate=September 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012071627/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-WaiveInjured-OL-Ben-Gottschalk/b8787c9a-f503-4603-8c93-bc341c9378a5 |archive-date=October 12, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jewishjournal.com/bloggish/item/jewish_football_players_of_the_year_and_sporty_rabbis |title=Jewish Football Players of the Year (and Sporty Rabbis) | Bloggish |work=[[The Jewish Journal of Greater Los Angeles|Jewish Journal]] |date=January 28, 2014 |accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref>  He has two older brothers, Adam and William.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.dailynews.com/preps/2009/09/10/hs-foot-q-and-a-with-notre-dam/ |title=HS FOOT: Q and A with Notre Dame offensive lineman Ben Gottschalk | Daily News High School Sports Spotlight |website=Blogs.dailynews.com |date=September 10, 2009 |accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-nov-01-sp-sondheimer1-story.html |title=Notre Dame's Kasdorf is the new king of sling |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=November 1, 2008 |access-date=September 4, 2016}}</ref>

He was a three-star Rivals.com and Scout.com prospect out of [[Notre Dame High School (Sherman Oaks, California)]], Class of 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/collegesheadlines/2015/04/09/ex-smu-ol-ben-gottschalk-signs-with-tampa-bay-buccaneers |title=College Sports: Ex-SMU OL Ben Gottschalk signs with Tampa Bay Buccaneers | SportsDay |website=Sportsday.dallasnews.com |date= April 9, 2015|accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref><ref name="smumustangs1">{{cite web|url=http://www.smumustangs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/gottschalk_ben00.html |title=Archived copy |accessdate=March 15, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315115959/http://www.smumustangs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/gottschalk_ben00.html |archivedate=March 15, 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://247sports.com/player/ben-gottschalk-4369 |title=Ben Gottschalk, Tampa Bay, Pro-Style Quarterback |website=247sports.com |date= |accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref>  He was ranked as the 94th-best player in California and the 14th-best center in the US by Rivals, was All-CIF Pac-5 Division First-team, was a Serra League Most Valuable Lineman, and was a member of the 2008 GSP Super All-State Underclass Team.<ref name="smumustangs1"/>  He also threw the [[shot put]] in the 2009 and 2010 seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/Athlete.aspx?AID=1168681#/L0 |title=Ben Gottschalk - CA Track and Field Profile |website=Athletic |date=October 8, 2013 |accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Gottschalk played [[college football]] at [[Southern Methodist University]] for the [[SMU Mustangs football|Mustangs]], playing in 47 games, with 24 starts (starting all the team's games his junior and senior years), on the offensive line<ref name="ers1"/><ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Buccaneers-Add-Two-to-Roster/342f2c2a-e19e-483b-8caa-b13ec07cbcb9 |title=Buccaneers Add Two to Roster |website=Buccaneers.com |date=April 9, 2015 |accessdate=September 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160327130827/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Buccaneers-Add-Two-to-Roster/342f2c2a-e19e-483b-8caa-b13ec07cbcb9 |archive-date=March 27, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a member of the 2012 ''[[Jewish Sports Review]]'' college football All-American team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/varsitytimesinsider/2013/03/football-gabe-marks-is-on-jewish-sports-reviews-all-america-team.html |title=Football: Gabe Marks is on Jewish Sports Review's All-America team |website=Latimesblogs.latimes.com |date=March 7, 2013 |accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Kansas City Chiefs===
Gottschalk was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on May 19, 2014.<ref name="ers1"/> On August 27, 2014, he was waived.<ref name="ers1"/>

On August 31, 2014, he was signed to the Chiefs' [[practice squad]].<ref name="ers1"/> On September 9, 2014, he was waived.<ref name="ers1"/>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (first stint)===
Gottschalk signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on April 9, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Scott|title=Buccaneers Add Two to Roster|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Buccaneers-Add-Two-to-Roster/342f2c2a-e19e-483b-8caa-b13ec07cbcb9|accessdate=April 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150412015925/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Buccaneers-Add-Two-to-Roster/342f2c2a-e19e-483b-8caa-b13ec07cbcb9|archive-date=April 12, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On May 28, 2015, he was waived.<ref name="ers1"/><ref name="csnbayarea1">{{cite web|url=http://www.csnbayarea.com/49ers/49ers-part-ways-ol-ben-gottschalk |title=49ers part ways with OL Ben Gottschalk | CSN Bay Area |accessdate=March 15, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315100730/http://www.csnbayarea.com/49ers/49ers-part-ways-ol-ben-gottschalk |archivedate=March 15, 2016 }}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On June 6, 2015, he was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] to a two-year contract.<ref name="ers1"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sacramento.cbslocal.com/2015/06/16/49ers-sign-ol-ben-gottschalk-and-2-more-waive-2-others/ |title=49ers Sign OL Ben Gottschalk And 2 More, Waive 2 Others  |website=CBS Sacramento |date=June 16, 2015 |accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref> On August 6, 2015, while injured he was waived a few days after undergoing foot surgery.<ref name="ers1"/><ref name="csnbayarea1"/> On August 7, 2015, he was placed on injured reserve. On August 13, 2015, he was waived from injured reserve. The 49ers paid him an injury settlement worth $56,118.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ninersnation.com/2015/8/18/9173607/49ers-ben-gottschalk-agree-to-56118-injury-settlement |title=49ers, Ben Gottschalk agree to $56,118 injury settlement |publisher=Niners Nation |date=August 18, 2015 |accessdate=September 4, 2016}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (second stint)===
On November 25, 2015, Gottschalk was signed to the Buccaneers' practice squad. On January 5, 2016, he signed a reserve/future contract with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite news|title = Buccaneers sign 9 players to reserve/futures contracts|url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/buccaneers-sign-9-players-to-reservefutures-contracts/2016/01/05/f9c33020-b3f7-11e5-8abc-d09392edc612_story.html|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190114153401/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/buccaneers-sign-9-players-to-reservefutures-contracts/2016/01/05/f9c33020-b3f7-11e5-8abc-d09392edc612_story.html|url-status = dead|archive-date = January 14, 2019|newspaper = The Washington Post|date = January 5, 2016|access-date = January 7, 2016|issn = 0190-8286|language = en-US|agency = Associated Press}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Jermaine Talley''' (born July 14, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[New York Giants]] and [[Atlanta Falcons]]. He was selected by the Giants in the fourth round of the [[1995 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]].

==Early life==
Benjamin Jermaine Talley was born on July 14, 1972, in [[Griffin, Georgia]].<ref name="pfr"/> He attended [[Griffin High School (Georgia)|Griffin High School]] in Griffin.<ref name="A">{{Cite web |title=Ben Talley |url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/tall00300.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518075135/http://www.profootballarchives.com/tall00300.html |archive-date=May 18, 2015 |access-date=May 15, 2015 |website=Pro Football Archives}}</ref>

==College football==
Talley played at the [[University of Tennessee]] from 1991 to 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 10, 2004 |title=Leak among grads |url=https://247sports.com/college/tennessee/Article/leak-among-grads-104090189/amp/ |access-date=February 25, 2024 |website=247sports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rhoden |first=William C. |date=September 18, 1994 |title=COLLEGE FOOTBALL; Florida's Passing Drenches Tennessee |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/09/18/sports/college-football-florida-s-passing-drenches-tennessee.html |access-date=February 25, 2024 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He started all twelve games for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Volunteers]] his senior year in 1994, the third year he did so. He also earned [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] second-team honors after recording 72 tackles and 5.5 sacks in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Talley |url=http://www.tradingcarddb.com/GalleryP.cfm/pid/22475/Ben-Talley |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150516011430/http://www.tradingcarddb.com/GalleryP.cfm/pid/22475/Ben-Talley |archive-date=May 16, 2015 |access-date=May 15, 2015 |website=Trading Card Database}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Talley was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the fourth round, with the 133rd overall pick, of the [[1995 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1995 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1995/draft.htm |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was a member of the Giants from 1995 to 1996, appearing in four games for the team during the [[1995 NFL season|1995 season]]. He played in eight games with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in 1998.<ref name="pfr">{{Cite web |title=Ben Talley Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TallBe20.htm |access-date=February 25, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ben Malena''' (born May 29, 1992) is an American former [[gridiron football|football]] [[running back]]. He was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] after the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.rantsports.com/nfl/2014/06/29/dallas-cowboys-2014-training-camp-profile-ben-malena/|title=Dallas Cowboys 2014 Training Camp Profile: Ben Malena|last=Flores|first=Jesus|website=www.rantsports.com|access-date=2016-05-14}}</ref> He played [[college football]] at [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M]].

== Professional career ==

=== Dallas Cowboys (first stint)===
On May 12, 2014, Malena signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref name=":0" /> On August 9, 2014, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4731465/cowboys-roster-at-89-players|title=Cowboys cut two, sign one; roster at 89|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2016-05-14}}</ref>

=== Houston Texans ===
On August 29, 2014, Malena was signed to the [[Houston Texans]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/nfl/texans/story/1474191-texans-sign-ben-malena-to-the-practice-squad|title=Texans Sign Ben Malena to the Practice Squad|website=Scout.com|access-date=2016-05-14}}</ref> On December 29, 2014, Malena signed a reserve/future contract with the Texans.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-sign-nine-to-reservefutures-contracts/62c78488-15b2-438b-833e-ea45b63f0b90|title=Texans sign nine to reserve/futures contracts|website=www.houstontexans.com|access-date=2016-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616225836/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-sign-nine-to-reservefutures-contracts/62c78488-15b2-438b-833e-ea45b63f0b90|archive-date=2016-06-16|url-status=dead}}</ref> On May 8, 2015, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2015-05-08 |title=Texans Waive S Josh Aubrey, DE Keith Browner, & RB Ben Malena |url=http://nfltraderumors.co/texans-waive-s-josh-aubrey-de-keith-browner-rb-ben-malena/ |access-date=2016-05-14 |website=NFL Trade Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Dallas Cowboys (second stint) ===
On May 15, 2015, Malena signed with the Cowboys.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dal.247sports.com/Bolt/Report-Cowboys-sign-RBs-Ben-Malena-Michael-Hill-38760610|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817004211/http://dal.247sports.com/Bolt/Report-Cowboys-sign-RBs-Ben-Malena-Michael-Hill-38760610|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 17, 2015|title=Report: Cowboys sign RBs Ben Malena, Michael Hill|website=Dallas Cowboys|access-date=2016-05-14}}</ref> On September 5, 2015, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2015/09/05/vaughan-showers-among-notable-cuts-cowboys-meet-53-man-roster-limit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806020247/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2015/09/05/vaughan-showers-among-notable-cuts-cowboys-meet-53-man-roster-limit|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 6, 2017|title=Vaughan, Showers Among Notable Cuts As Cowboys Meet 53-Man Roster Limit|date=September 5, 2015|website=Dallas Cowboys|access-date=May 14, 2016}}</ref>

On December 2, 2015, Malena signed to the Cowboys' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2015/12/02/moore-green-promoted-active-roster-four-other-roster-moves|title=Moore & Green Promoted To Active Roster; Four Other Roster Moves|date=2015-12-02|website=Dallas Cowboys|access-date=2016-05-14}}</ref> On January 4, 2016, Malena signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/01/04/cowboys-sign-eight-practice-squad-players-futures-contracts|title=Cowboys Sign Eight Practice Squad Players To Futures Contracts|date=2016-01-05|website=Dallas Cowboys|access-date=2016-05-14}}</ref> On May 6, 2016, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/05/06/cowboys-make-five-roster-moves-announce-undrafted-free-agents|title=Cowboys Make Five Roster Moves; Announce Undrafted Free Agents|date=May 6, 2016|website=Dallas Cowboys|access-date=May 14, 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905095847/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/05/06/cowboys-make-five-roster-moves-announce-undrafted-free-agents|archivedate=September 5, 2017}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
On September 14, 2016, Malena signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]].

== Personal life ==
At [[Texas A&M University]], Malena majored in recreation, parks, and tourism science.

'''Benjamin Gedeon''' (born October 16, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] and was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the fourth round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. He played for the Vikings for four seasons, with his last season being in 2020.

==College career==
Gedeon appeared in 51 games and made 14 starting assignments at [[linebacker]], ultimately recording 176 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]], 6.5 [[qb sack|sacks]], 21 [[tackles-for-loss]] and two pass breakups. As a senior, he posted a career best 106 tackles, 15.5 tackles-for-loss, 4.5 sacks and two pass breakups. 
Following the [[2016 Michigan Wolverines football team|2016]] season, Gedeon was named to the [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] defensive second-team by the media.<ref>{{cite news|title=Peppers, Lewis Lead All 11 Defenders Honored by B1G|publisher=CBS Interactive|work=MGoBlue.com|access-date=April 29, 2017|date=November 29, 2016|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112916aaa.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622192605/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112916aaa.html|archive-date=June 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Gedeon was ranked as the No. 9 [[inside linebacker]] in the [[2017 NFL draft]] by [[CBSSports.com]] and was projected to go in the fourth or fifth round according to [[NFL.com]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Ben Gedeon Draft profile|work=NFL.com|access-date=May 6, 2017|date=April 9, 2017|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112916aaa.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622192605/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/112916aaa.html|archive-date=June 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Gedeon was one of the top performers at the [[NFL Scouting Combine|2017 NFL Combine]]. Gedeon finished atop all linebackers in the [[bench press]], lifting 225 pounds 27 times. He also tied for the best [[20-yard shuttle]] (4.13 seconds), was third in the 60-yard shuttle (11.58 seconds), had the seventh-best [[vertical jump]] (34.5 inches), was ninth in the [[three-cone drill|3-cone drill]] (6.98 seconds) and was twelfth with a 119-inch [[broad jump]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Snyder | first=Mark | title=Wolverines' Ben Gedeon impresses with NFL combine testing | website=Detroit Free Press | date=2017-03-07 | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2017/03/07/michigan-football-ben-gedeon/98851366/ | access-date=2025-08-22}}</ref>

===2017===
The [[Minnesota Vikings]] selected Gedeon in fourth round (120th overall) of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Quartet of Wolverines Go So Far on Third Day of NFL Draft|publisher=CBS Interactive|work=MGoBlue.com|access-date=April 29, 2017|date=April 29, 2017|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/042917aag.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622183228/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/042917aag.html|archive-date=June 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Select Michigan LB Ben Gedeon|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Select-Michigan-LB-Ben-Gedeon/da3ef89f-06fb-49ed-9089-d368bdf5d5d6|website=Vikings.com|date=April 29, 2017|access-date=May 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170429195936/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Select-Michigan-LB-Ben-Gedeon/da3ef89f-06fb-49ed-9089-d368bdf5d5d6|archive-date=April 29, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was the first of two linebackers drafted by the Vikings in 2017, along with [[Elijah Lee]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 26, 2017, the Vikings signed a Gedeon to a four-year, $3.03 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $633,147.<ref>{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Ben Gedeon contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/ben-gedeon-21862/| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

}}

Throughout [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Gedeon competed against [[Emmanuel Lamur]], [[Edmond Robinson]], [[Elijah Lee]], and Kentrell Brothers for the job as the starting weakside linebacker after it was left vacant due to the retirement of [[Chad Greenway]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Zimmer Confirms Open Competition at Will Linebacker| url=https://www.vikingsterritory.com/2017/general-news/zimmer-not-opposed-to-young-guy-starting-at-lb/amp| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=vikingsterritory.com| author=Borman, Sean| date=June 7, 2017}}</ref> Head coach [[Mike Zimmer]] named Gedeon the starting weakside linebacker, along with [[Anthony Barr (American football)|Anthony Barr]] and [[middle linebacker]] [[Eric Kendricks]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Vikings first depth chart features 3 rookies in starting roles| url=http://vikingswire.usatoday.com/2017/09/05/vikings-first-depth-chart-features-3-rookies-in-starting-roles/| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=vikingswire.usatoday.com| author=Horstman, Terry| date=September 5, 2017}}</ref>

He made his regular season debut and first career start in the Vikings' season-opener against the [[New Orleans Saints]] and recorded a solo tackle during their 29–19 victory. On December 31, 2017, Gedeon collected a season-high six combined tackles in the Vikings' 23–10 win against the [[Chicago Bears]]. Gedeon finished his rookie season with 37 combined tackles (23 solo) in 16 games and nine starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Ben Gedeon (career)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bengedeon/2558033/gamelogs| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

The Minnesota Vikings finished first in the [[NFC North]] with a 13–3 record and received a first round bye. On January 14, 2018, Gedeon played in first career playoff game and assisted on one tackle in a 29–24 victory against the Saints in the NFC Divisional round. They lost to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] who became the eventual [[Super Bowl LII|Super Bowl LII Champions]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Ben Gedeon (2017)| website=[[NFL.com]]| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bengedeon/2558033/gamelogs| access-date=February 25, 2018}}</ref>

===2018===
Gedeon entered training camp slated as the starting weakside linebacker. Head coach Mike Zimmer named Gedeon and Anthony Barr the starting outside linebackers. They started alongside middle linebacker Kendricks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings Depth Chart |url=https://kfgo.com/blogs/news-from-the-vikes/6680/minnesota-vikings-depth-chart/ |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=KFgO.com |archive-date=January 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190105094155/https://kfgo.com/blogs/news-from-the-vikes/6680/minnesota-vikings-depth-chart/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In Week 14, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles during a 21–7 loss at the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He finished the season with 53 combined tackles (29 solo) and two pass deflections in 15 games and eight starts.<ref name="career"/>

===2019===
Gedeon opened the 2019 season as a starting linebacker for the Vikings. He played in eight games with five starts before suffering a concussion in Week 11. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 2, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings putting Ben Gedeon on IR|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/12/02/vikings-putting-ben-gedeon-on-ir/|author=Gantt, Darin|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=December 2, 2019}}</ref>

===2020===
Gedeon was placed on the active/[[physically unable to perform list]] (PUP) at the start of training camp on August 3, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves to Set Roster at 80 Players |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/pj-hall-anthony-barr-ifeadi-odenigbo-quartney-davis-roster-moves |website=Vikings.com |date=August 3, 2020 |access-date=August 3, 2020}}</ref> He was moved to the reserve/PUP list to start the regular season on September 5.<ref>{{cite news |author=Peters, Craig and Eric Smith |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/2020-roster-53-man-announced |website=Vikings.com |date=September 5, 2020 |access-date=September 17, 2020}}</ref> He was waived with a failed physical designation on November 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Activate LB Todd Davis from Reserve/COVID-19; Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/todd-davis-activate-reserve-covid-19-announce-roster-moves|website=Vikings.com|date=November 10, 2020}}</ref>

'''Ben Niemann''' (born July 27, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]] was signed as an undrafted agent by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].

==Early life==
Niemann is the son of [[Jay Niemann|Jay]] and Lou Ann Niemann. He was born in [[Des Moines, Iowa]] and moved several times growing up due to his father's job as a football coach. He attended [[Sycamore High School (Sycamore, Illinois)|Sycamore High School]], in [[Sycamore, Illinois]] where he played [[high school football|football]] and basketball. In football, he played [[wide receiver]] and [[safety position|safety]] and was named first-team all-state as a junior and senior.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2012 |title=Football: 2012 IFCA All-State teams |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/ct-xpm-2012-11-16-ct-spt-1117-prep-foot-ifca-all-state-20121116-story.html |access-date=October 23, 2019 |website=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lange |first=Millie |date=November 22, 2013 |title=IHSA All-State Football Teams Named |url=http://www.thexradio.com/news/sports/football/8669-ihsa-all-state-football-teams-named |access-date=October 23, 2019 |website=[[WXEF|TheXRadio.com]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Niemann played four seasons for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]], making 53 appearances and starting the last 40 games of his career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDowell |first=Sam |date=August 13, 2018 |title=This Chiefs player was arguably the biggest standout in the preseason opener |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article216582515.html |access-date=October 26, 2018 |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |publisher=KansasCity.com}}</ref> He played mostly on [[special teams]] and as a reserve [[linebacker]] as a [[true freshman]], blocking a [[punt gridiron|punt]] and returning the ball for a [[touchdown]] against [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern]]. Niemann became a starter at [[outside linebacker]] for Iowa going into his sophomore year and garnered honorable mention [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] honors after making 45 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] (4.5 for loss), four [[qb sack|sacks]] and two pass break-ups. He was named honorable mention All-Big Ten again as a senior after making 80 tackles (six for loss), a sack, five passes broken up and two forced [[fumbles]]. Over the course of his career, Niemann accumulated 201 tackles, 17 tackles for loss, two [[interceptions]], and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Roster-44 Ben Niemann-Stats |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6953 |access-date=October 26, 2018 |website=HawkeyeSports.com}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
Niemann signed with the Cardinals on June 16, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban, Darren |date=June 16, 2022 |title=Cardinals Sign Josh Jackson, Ben Niemann After Tryouts |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-tryout-players-cornerback-josh-jackson-linebacker-ben-niemann |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> In 2022, Niemann played in all 17 games for Arizona with nine starts and made career-high 70 tackles with two tackles for loss, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arias |first=Greg |date=April 17, 2023 |title=Titans Agree To Terms With Linebacker Ben Niemann |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/titans/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-linebacker-ben-niemann |access-date=May 1, 2023 |website=[[SI.com]]}}</ref>

On September 1, 2023, Niemann was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=September 1, 2023 |title=Broncos sign LB Ben Niemann to practice squad |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-lb-ben-niemann-to-practice-squad |access-date=September 30, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 30.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos promote ILB Ben Niemann to active roster|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-ilb-ben-niemann-to-active-roster|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=October 30, 2023}}</ref> In seven games for Denver, he logged two combined tackles and only played on special teams.

'''Benjamin Powers''' (born October 29, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]].

==Early life==
Powers attended high school in [[Wichita, Kansas]] at [[Kapaun Mt. Carmel Catholic High School]].  He got [[varsity letters]] in football and wrestling and finished second in the state wrestling finals. As a junior in high school, Powers, already 6 ft 4ins tall and weighed 280 pounds, played both on the offensive line and defensive line.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kapaun Mt. Carmel 2013 Football Roster |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/kapaun-mt-carmel-crusaders-(wichita,ks)/football-fall-13/roster.htm |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=maxpreps.com |publisher=Max Preps}}</ref> After his senior football season, Powers received no scholarship from any major college or university.<ref name="Ravens">{{Cite web |title=70 Ben Powers |url=http://ftp.ravenspr.com/player_bios/ben_powers.pdf |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=baltimoreravens.com |publisher=Baltimore Ravens}}</ref>

== College career ==
After one year at [[Butler Grizzlies|Butler Community College]], Powers enrolled at the [[University of Oklahoma]]. Following the 2018 season, Powers was named a [[2018 College Football All-America Team|consensus first-team All-American]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ben Powers Bio |url=http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=210821986&DB_OEM_ID=31000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201120036/http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=210821986&DB_OEM_ID=31000 |archive-date=2019-02-01 |work=OU Athletics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bender |first=Bill |date=December 13, 2018 |title=Alabama's Tua Tagovailoa heads 2018 consensus All-America Team |work=Sporting News |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ca/ncaa-football/news/alabamas-tua-tagovailoa-2018-consensus-all-american-team/u4gei2bnxvig1jmptsbwhsj97}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
The [[Baltimore Ravens]] selected Powers with the 123rd overall pick in the fourth round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Downing |first=Garrett |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Fourth Round (123): Ravens Select Oklahoma Offensive Guard Ben Powers |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/fourth-round-123-ravens-select-oklahoma-offensive-guard-ben-powers |access-date=2024-10-16 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> His draft pick also became famous because [[Baltimore]] sports fan [[Mo Gaba]], announced the pick on a draft card written in [[Braille]]. After making the active roster, he was placed on the inactive list for the first six weeks of his rookie season before making his debut in Week 17, playing the majority of snaps at right guard in the Ravens' 28–10 win over the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].

After beginning the 2020 season as a backup, he was named the starting right guard midseason due to injuries. He was the primary left guard in 2021, and was the full-time starter in 2022.

===Denver Broncos===
On March 16, 2023, Powers signed a four-year, $51.5 million contract with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=March 16, 2023 |title=Broncos sign G Ben Powers |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-g-ben-powers |access-date=2024-10-16 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

On October 6, 2025, Powers was placed on injured reserve after sustaining a biceps injury during the Broncos' Week 5 victory against the [[2025 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], with the expectation to return in December.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Parker |date=2025-10-05 |title=Broncos sending LG Ben Powers back to Denver after biceps injury vs. Eagles |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/10/05/ben-powers-broncos-injury-update/ |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=The Denver Post |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Broncos activate DT Malcolm Roach from IR, place G Ben Powers on IR|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-dt-malcolm-roach-from-ir-place-g-ben-powers-on-ir|access-date=November 29, 2025|website=denverbroncos.com|language=es}}</ref> On December 20, Powers was activated from injured reserve ahead of the team's Week 16 matchup against the [[2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Broncos acrivate G Ben Powers from IR, elevate QB Sam Ehlinger and S Delarrin Turner-Yell for Week 16 game vs. Jaguars|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-g-ben-powers-from-ir-elevate-qb-sam-ehlinger-and-s-delarrin-turner-yell-for-week-16-game-vs-jaguars|access-date=January 20, 2026|website=denverbroncos.com|language=en}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]] and [[James Madison Dukes football|James Madison Dukes]] and was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the NFL in the seventh round of the [[2020 NFL draft]]. He has also played for the [[Seattle Sea Dragons]] in the [[XFL (2020–2023)|XFL]] in 2023, leading them to the playoffs. He is currently a college football commentator for [[CBS Sports]]. ==Early life== DiNucci attended [[Pine-Richland High School]] in [[Gibsonia, Pennsylvania]], where he played [[high school football]].{{Cite web |title=Ben DiNucci, Pine-Richland, Pro-Style Quarterback |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Ben-DiNucci-61185/high-school-106326/ |access-date=October 29, 2020 |website=247Sports}} As a sophomore, he became a starter at [[quarterback]]. As a senior, he threw for a [[Western Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic League|WPIAL]]-record 4,269 yards becoming the first player in Pennsylvania history to throw for over 4,000 yards in a season with 46 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. He led his team to a 15–1{{Cite web|date=January 26, 2015|title=Pitt Football Lands Local Quarterback Recruit|url=https://pittsburgh.cbslocal.com/2015/01/26/pitt-football-lands-local-quarterback-recruit/|access-date=April 26, 2020|work=CBS Pittsburgh}} record, and a state AAAA championship game appearance. He received 2014–2015 Gatorade Player of the Year for the state of Pennsylvania, second-team USA TODAY All-American, Pennsylvania Sports Writers Class AAAA Player of the Year, Pennsylvania Football News Class AAAA Offensive Player of the Year honors. DiNucci finished his high school career with 548 of 809 completions for 7,619 yards, and 72 touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Ben DiNucci's High School Football Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/ben-dinucci/wA5bc_TpEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/football/stats.htm |access-date=October 29, 2020 |website=MaxPreps.com}} ==College career== Although he originally intended to enroll at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], DiNucci decommitted and accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Pittsburgh]], after [[Pat Narduzzi]] was hired as the new head coach.{{Cite web|last=Tepper|first=Jeremy|date=March 2, 2015|title=DiNucci passes over Penn for Panthers|url=https://pittnews.com/article/1795/sports/dinucci-passes-over-penn-for-panthers/|access-date=April 26, 2020|website=The Pitt News}} As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] freshman, he was a backup quarterback behind [[Nathan Peterman]]. His first game experience came in the final offensive series against [[Duke University]]. In the [[2016 Pinstripe Bowl]], he relieved an injured Peterman late in the third quarter, posting three of nine completions for 16 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and two carries for 18 yards in a 31–24 loss against [[Northwestern University]]. As a sophomore, he was named the starting quarterback before the seventh game against [[North Carolina State University]], after senior [[Max Browne]] suffered a season-ending right shoulder injury.{{Cite web|last=Zuk|first=Abbot|date=October 10, 2017|title='DiNucci is the guy': Narduzzi announces quarterback changes|url=https://pittnews.com/article/123422/sports/football/narduzzi-announces-quarterback-changes/|access-date=April 26, 2020|website=The Pitt News}} He was platooned during the year and eventually lost the starting position to true freshman [[Kenny Pickett]], for the season finale 24–14 victory against the previously undefeated No. 2 [[University of Miami]]. He finished with 88 of 158 completions for 1,091 yards, five touchdowns and five interceptions. In December, he announced his decision to transfer to [[James Madison University]].{{Cite web|last=Mondell|first=Jordan|date=December 14, 2017|title=DiNucci announces transfer from Pitt|url=https://pittnews.com/article/125729/top-stories/dinucci-announces-transfer-pitt-football/|access-date=April 26, 2020|website=The Pitt News}} As a junior at James Madison, he started all 13 games at quarterback, posting 211 of 309 completions for 2,275 yards, 16 passing touchdowns, 12 interceptions, 433 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns (leading the team). He received third-team All-CAA honors. He had a career-high 316 passing yards against [[Elon University]]. He passed for a career-best four touchdowns against the [[University of Rhode Island]]. He rushed for career highs of 104 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns at [[Towson University]]. As a senior, he started all 16 games at quarterback, passing for 3,441 yards, 29 passing touchdowns, completed nearly 71% of his throws, had 122 carries for 569 yards and seven rushing touchdowns. He earned All-CAA, CAA Offensive Player of the Year and AFCA first-team All-American honors. He led the Dukes to the FCS Championship Game, where the team lost to [[North Dakota State University]].{{Cite magazine |last=Amaranthus |first=Bri |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Cowboys Select Quarterback Ben DiNucci in First Round of NFL Draft |magazine=Sports Illustrated |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cowboys/news/cowboys-select-quarterback-ben-dinucci-in-final-round-of-nfl-draft |access-date=April 25, 2020}} In the title game, DiNucci completed 22 of 33 passes for 204 yards, two touchdowns and one interception.{{Cite news |last=Barrerra |first=Zeke |date=April 25, 2020 |title=2020 NFL Draft: Cowboys take 7th-round flyer on little known, championship game QB |work=Cowboys Wire |url=https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/2020/04/25/2020-nfl-draft-cowboys-take-7th-round-flyer-on-little-known-championship-game-qb/ |access-date=April 25, 2020}} He finished his career at James Madison (cropped).jpg|thumb|DiNucci in 2020]] DiNucci was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the seventh round (231st overall) of the [[2020 NFL draft]], after it became apparent that he was considering signing with either the [[Cleveland Browns]] or the [[Chicago Bears]] if he were to become an [[undrafted free agent]].{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2020/draft.htm |access-date=October 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}} On October 19, 2020, DiNucci made his NFL debut in relief of [[Andy Dalton]] against the [[Arizona Cardinals]].{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys – October 19th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010190dal.htm |access-date=October 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}} On October 25, 2020, against the [[Washington Football Team]], DiNucci came into the game after Dalton left the game with a concussion in the third quarter. DiNucci threw his first completed pass, for 32 yards, to [[Amari Cooper]]. He completed 2 out of 3 attempts for 39 yards during the 3–25 loss, while taking three sacks in 12 snaps.{{cite web |last=Walker |first=Patrik |date=October 25, 2020 |title=Cowboys vs. Washington score, takeaways: Andy Dalton knocked out of game as Washington rolls |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-vs-washington-score-takeaways-andy-dalton-knocked-out-of-game-as-washington-rolls/live/ |access-date=October 26, 2020 |website=[[CBSSports.com]]}} On October 31, 2020, the Cowboys announced that DiNucci would make his first career start against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] due to Dalton being in concussion protocol.{{cite web |title=Dalton Ruled Out vs. Philly; 2 Veterans Activated |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/dalton-ruled-out-vs-philly-2-veterans-activated |website=www.dallascowboys.com |access-date=November 1, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Rapoport |first1=Ian |title=New Cowboys starter Ben DiNucci has 'got an edge' |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-cowboys-starter-ben-dinucci-has-got-an-edge |website=NFL.com |access-date=November 1, 2020}} DiNucci completed 21-of-40 passes for 180 yards, lost two fumbles and was sacked 4 times, as the Cowboys lost 23–9 and failed to score a touchdown in back-to-back games for just the fourth time in franchise history, even though the Cowboys' defense had caused four Eagles' turnovers during the contest.{{cite news |last1=Lopez |first1=Selby |title=National reaction to Cowboys-Eagles: Ben DiNucci was bad, but Carson Wentz may have been worse |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/cowboys/2020/11/01/national-reaction-to-cowboys-eagles-ben-dinucci-was-bad-but-carson-wentz-may-have-been-worse/ |access-date=November 2, 2020 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |date=November 1, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Cowboys' ineptitude continues in loss to Eagles |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4772435/cowboys-ineptitude-continues-in-loss-to-eagles |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 1, 2020}} DiNucci was passed on the depth chart by [[Garrett Gilbert]] for the backup job for the rest of the season.{{cite web |title=Who will back up quarterback Dak Prescott for the Dallas Cowboys? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4773193/who-will-back-up-quarterback-dak-prescott-for-the-dallas-cowboys |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 5, 2021}} On August 31, 2021, DiNucci was waived by the Cowboys, but added to the practice squad the next day.{{cite web |title=Cowboys Make 28 Moves; Roster Cut Down To 53 |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-make-28-moves-to-set-initial-53-man-roster |author=Phillips, Rob |website=DallasCowboys.com |date=August 31, 2021}}{{cite web |title=QB Ben DiNucci Among Practice Squad Additions |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/qb-ben-dinucci-among-practice-squad-additions |author=Phillips, Rob |website=DallasCowboys.com |date=September 1, 2021}} DiNucci signed a reserve/future contract with the Cowboys on January 18, 2022. On August 30, 2022, DiNucci was waived by the Cowboys.{{cite web |title=Cowboys Make 28 Moves To Reach Roster Limit |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-make-28-moves-to-reach-roster-limit |author=Eatman, Nick |website=DallasCowboys.com |date=August 30, 2022}} ===Seattle Sea Dragons=== DiNucci was allocated in the opening phase of the [[2023 XFL draft]]. Outside of [[A. J. McCarron]], DiNucci was the only quarterback in the draft pool to have had NFL regular season experience.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-14 |title=What's next for the XFL 2023? QBs to watch in the draft pool |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/35002634/next-xfl-2023-qbs-watch-draft-pool-roster-sizes-new-teams |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=ESPN.com}} On November 15, 2022, DiNucci was selected by the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]]'s [[Seattle Sea Dragons]]. He started 10 games and guided the team to a playoff berth with a 7–3 record. He led the league in passing yards (2,671), attempts (374), completions (272), and interceptions (13), while ranking second in passing touchdowns (20). He was released from his contract on May 15, 2023.{{cite web |title=XFL Transactions |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |access-date=May 18, 2023 |archive-date=March 16, 2020 Over the next year, Ellefson immersed himself in coaching, working with the Vikings' tight ends and contributing to game planning, play charting, and run game preparation. https://www.si.com/nfl/vikings/news/matthew-coller-ben-ellefson-has-found-his-second-dream-job-on-vikings-coaching-staff-01jc9sraxgqf Ellefson’s inspiration to coach was shaped early by his tight ends coach at North Dakota State, [[Tyler Roehl]], who taught him the importance of technique and discipline. As he developed in his new role, Ellefson embraced the demanding nature of coaching and was promoted to an offensive assistant. He continues to grow on the Vikings' staff, known for his attention to detail, strong work ethic, and ability to connect with players.https://www.si.com/nfl/vikings/news/matthew-coller-ben-ellefson-has-found-his-second-dream-job-on-vikings-coaching-staff-01jc9sraxgqf == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://gobison.com/sports/football/roster/ben-ellefson/8436 North Dakota State Bison football bio] {{2017 NDSU Bison football navbox}} {{2018 NDSU Bison football navbox}} {{2019 NDSU Bison football navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Ellefson, Ben}} [[Category:1996 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Hawley, Minnesota]] [[Category:Players of American football from Minnesota]] [[Category:American football tight ends]] [[Category:North Dakota State Bison football players]] [[Category:Jacksonville Jaguars players]] [[Category:Minnesota Vikings players]] [[Category:Minnesota Vikings coaches]] [[Category:Coaches of American football from Minnesota]]

He became a starter going into his sophomore year and finished the season with 45 catches for 644 yards and five touchdowns.{{Cite web |last=Greenstein |first=Teddy |date=August 23, 2018 |title=Bonded by blood, Northwestern's Ben Skowronek and TJ Green hope to find home in the end zone |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-tj-green-ben-skowronek-northwestern-20180823-story.html |access-date=November 16, 2020 |website=[[Chicago Tribune]]}} Skowronek recorded 45 reception for 562 yards and two touchdowns in his junior season. He also recorded 13 tackles on special teams. ===Houston Texans=== On May 9, 2024, the Rams traded Skowronek and a seventh-round pick to the [[Houston Texans]] in exchange for a sixth-round pick.{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=May 9, 2024 |title=Rams trade Ben Skowronek to Texans |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-trade-ben-skowronek-to-texans |access-date=August 14, 2024 |website=TheRams.com}} He was waived on August 27.{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (08-27-2024) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-08-27-2024 |access-date=2024-09-19 |website=HoustonTexans.com}} ===Pittsburgh Steelers=== ====2024 season==== On August 29, 2024, Skowronek was signed to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] practice squad.{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=August 30, 2024 |title=Steelers sign eight to practice squad |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-seven-to-practice-squad |access-date=2024-09-19 |website=Steelers.com}} He was signed to the active roster on September 17, but placed on injured reserve the following day.{{Cite web |last=Kozora |first=Alex |date=September 18, 2024 |title=Steelers Sign WR Ben Skowronek From Practice Squad To 53-Man Roster |url=https://steelersdepot.com/2024/09/steelers-sign-wr-ben-skowronek-from-practice-squad-to-53-man-roster/ |access-date=18 September 2024 |website=Steelers Depot}} He was active for the November 10 game against the [[2024 Washington Commanders|Washington Commanders]] and recovered a fumbled punt. Skowronek recorded 5 receptions on 5 targets for 69 yards, along with recording 2 fumble recoveries and 7 [[special teams]] tackles. In addition to playing wide receiver, Skowronek also played [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]], [[H-back|H-Back]], and [[tight end]]. Steelers offensive coordinator [[Arthur Smith (American football, born 1982)|Arthur Smith]] would frequently have Skowronek move around the offense by using pre-snap motion. ====2025 season==== [[File:Ben Skowronek.jpg|thumb|Skowronek with the Steelers in 2025]] On March 13, 2025, Skowronek re-signed with the Steelers.{{cite web | title=Steelers bring back wide receivers Scotty Miller and Ben Skowronek | website=AP News | date=2025-03-17 | url=https://apnews.com/article/pittsburgh-steelers-free-agency-4507ec711f9d7b0ccfa7776b50099678 | access-date=2026-03-04}} In the Steelers' season opener against the [[2025 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], Skowronek caught the team's first touchdown pass of the season from [[Aaron Rodgers]].
