===Miami Dolphins===
On April 30, 2022, Stille signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] as an undrafted free agent following the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Barry |title=BEN STILLE DL, MIAMI DOLPHINS |url=https://www.nbcsportsedge.com/football/nfl/player-news/10737076?category=headlines |website=NBC sports edge.com |access-date=23 November 2022}}</ref> On August 30, the Dolphins released Stille,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Masala |first=Mike |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Report: Dolphins release UDFA DL Ben Stille |url=https://dolphinswire.usatoday.com/2022/08/30/dolphins-release-ben-stille/ |access-date=23 November 2022 |website=Dolphins Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> On September 1, Stille was re-signed to the Dolphins' [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Brian |title=Miami Dolphins begin filling out practice squad after waiver claim |url=https://phinphanatic.com/2022/09/01/miami-dolphins-begin-filling-out-practice-squad-after-waiver-claim/ |website=Phin Phanatic.com |date=September 2022 |access-date=23 November 2022}}</ref> On October 22, the Dolphins elevated Stille to their active roster.<ref>{{cite web |title=Miami Dolphins make roster moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-x0966 |website=Miami Dolphins.com |access-date=23 November 2022}}</ref> The next day, Stille made his NFL debut, playing nine snaps and totaling two tackles.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Stille Stats, Height, Weight, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StilBe00.htm |website=Pro Football Reference.com |access-date=23 November 2022}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On November 15, 2022, the [[Cleveland Browns]] signed Stille off the Dolphins' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Browns sign DT Ben Stille |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-dt-ben-stille |website=Cleveland Browns.com |access-date=23 November 2022}}</ref> On May 9, 2023, Stille was waived by the Browns.<ref>{{cite web |title=Browns waive 2 players|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-waive-stille-stevenson |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |date = 9 May 2023|access-date=9 May 2023}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On May 10, 2023, Stille was claimed off waivers by the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Claim Another In Defensive Lineman Ben Stille|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-claim-another-in-defensive-lineman-ben-stille|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=May 10, 2023}}</ref> He was waived on August 30, and re-signed to the practice squad. He was promoted to the active roster on November 21.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Place Leki Fotu On Injured Reserve|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-place-leki-fotu-on-injured-reserve-kyzir-white|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> Stille was released on November 28 and re-signed to the practice squad two days later.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Urban |first1=Darren |title=Cardinals Release Keaontay Ingram |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-release-keaontay-ingram |website=azcardinals.com |access-date=29 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Root |first1=Jess |title=Cardinals release TE Zach Ertz after his request |url=https://cardswire.usatoday.com/2023/11/30/cardinals-release-te-zach-ertz-after-his-request/ |website=Cardinals Wire |date=30 November 2023 |access-date=30 November 2023}}</ref> He was promoted back to the active roster on January 5, 2024.

Stille was waived by the Cardinals on August 27, 2024, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Trim Roster To Get To 53 For Regular Season|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-trim-roster-to-get-to-53-for-2024-regular-season|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Announce Initial Practice Squad For 2024|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-announce-initial-practice-squad-for-2024|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

On October 3, 2024, Stille was signed to the Arizona Cardinals practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Root |first1=Jess |title=Cardinals re-sign familiar face on defensive line |url=https://cardswire.usatoday.com/2024/10/03/cardinals-re-sign-familiar-face-on-defensive-line/ |website=Cardinals Wire |access-date=4 October 2024}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Arizona on January 6, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Sign 7 Players To Futures Deals|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-7-players-to-futures-deals|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=January 6, 2025}}</ref> On May 22, Stille was waived by the Cardinals.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Root |first1=Jess |title=Arizona Cardinals cut DL Ben Stille |url=https://cardswire-eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/cardinals/2025/05/22/arizona-cardinals-waive-dl-ben-stille/83803625007/ |website=Cardinals Wire |access-date=23 May 2025}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins (second stint)===
On June 5, 2025, Stille signed with the Miami Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-06052025 |website=miamidolphins.com |access-date=6 June 2025}}</ref> He was waived on August 26 as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-08262025 |website=miamidolphins.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On November 11, 2025, Stille signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Urben |first1=Matt |title=Falcons sign defensive lineman to practice squad, release two players |url=https://thefalconswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/falcons/2025/11/11/atlanta-falcons-ben-stille/87215792007/ |website=Falcons Wire |access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Atlanta on January 5, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign 7 players to reserve/future contracts for 2026|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-7-players-reserve-future-contracts-2026|author=McElhaney, Tori|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=January 5, 2026}}</ref> Stille was released by the Falcons on May 11.<ref>{{cite web|title= Falcons sign 4 players following rookie minicamp |url= https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-roster-moves-rookie-minicamp-2026 |author=McElhaney, Tori|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=May 11, 2026}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Sinnott''' ({{IPAc-en|'|s|ɪ|n|ə|t}} {{respell|SIN|ət}}; born June 14, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State Wildcats]], earning two [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12]] honors prior to being selected by the Commanders in the second round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Sinnott was born on June 14, 2002, in [[Waterloo, Iowa]], later attending [[Columbus High School (Waterloo, Iowa)|Columbus High School]].<ref name="TheBeast">{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2024 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2024/04/11162958/TheBeast2024_MasterFile-8.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240411212702/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2024/04/11162958/TheBeast2024_MasterFile-8.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 11, 2024 |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 14, 2024 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=97–98}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinett |first=Kellis |date=December 29, 2022 |title=How Ben Sinnott became a star tight end at Kansas State after starting out as walk-on |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/kansas-state/article270509977.html |access-date=January 11, 2023 |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]]}}</ref> He committed to play [[college football]] for the [[South Dakota Coyotes football|South Dakota Coyotes]] before changing to the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State Wildcats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kwwl.com/sports/sailor-star-ben-sinnott-switches-to-kansas-state/article_75e717e8-e045-5625-bcee-f55838bd3cfe.html|title=Sailor Star Ben Sinnott Switches to Kansas State|first=Rick|last=Coleman|website=[[KWWL (TV)|KWWL.com]]|date=January 30, 2020|access-date=December 20, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
Sinnott [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his true freshman season at Kansas State.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Green |first=Arne |date=September 29, 2022 |title=K-State football's Ben Sinnott looks to build off strong Oklahoma game |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/cat-zone/2022/09/29/kansas-state-kstate-football-ben-sinnott-schedule-oklahoma-game/69524248007/ |access-date=December 20, 2022 |website=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]]}}</ref> He caught two passes for 15 yards and rushed three times for 12 yards and one touchdown during his redshirt freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Green |first=Arne |date=November 17, 2022 |title=Kansas State football tight end Ben Sinnott turning heads as receiver |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/cat-zone/2022/11/17/kansas-state-football-wildcats-tight-end-ben-sinnott-turning-heads-as-receiver-chris-klieman-big-12/69654063007/ |access-date=December 20, 2022 |website=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]]}}</ref> Sinnott was named first-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12 Conference]] as a redshirt sophomore after catching 31 passes for 447 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kwch.com/2022/11/30/ku-k-state-football-combine-put-26-all-big-12-teams/|title=KU, K-State football combine to put 26 on All-Big 12 teams|website=[[KWCH-DT|KWCH.com]]|date=November 30, 2022|access-date=December 20, 2022}}</ref>

Sinnott was the 2023 Lowman Trophy award winner, which is an award for the best college fullback in the country as presented by the [[Barstool Sports]] podcast, [[Pardon My Take]] (hosted by [[Dan Katz (podcaster)|Dan Katz]] and [[PFT Commenter]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gould |first=Bobby |date=2024-01-13 |title=Ben Sinnott could thaw Washington’s tight end deep freeze |url=https://www.hogshaven.com/2024/1/13/24028793/ben-sinnott-could-thaw-washingtons-tight-end-deep-freeze |access-date=2026-01-09 |website=Hogs Haven |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Professional career==

Sinnott was selected by the [[Washington Commanders]] in the second round (53rd overall) of the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Selby |first=Zach |date=April 26, 2024 |title=Commanders draft TE Ben Sinnott with No. 53 overall pick |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-draft-te-ben-sinnott-with-no-53-overall-pick |access-date=28 April 2024 |website=Commanders.com}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract on June 14, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Commanders wrap up 2024 draft signings with Jayden Daniels, Ben Sinnott, Brandon Coleman |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-wrap-up-2024-draft-signings-with-jayden-daniels-ben-sinnott-brandon-coleman |access-date=June 14, 2024 |date=June 14, 2024 |website=Commanders.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Sinnott recorded his first career catch, a three yard touchdown, in Week 6 against the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://commanderswire.usatoday.com/2024/10/21/commanders-te-ben-sinnott-nfl-touchdown-zach-ertz-jayden-daniels/|website=Commanders Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|title=Commanders TE Ben Sinnott's first touchdown will be the first of many|first=Bryan|last=Manning|date=October 21, 2024|accessdate=October 21, 2024}}</ref>

Ben Sinnott’s rookie season with the Washington Commanders in 2024 was marked by limited production and playing time, despite being a second-round draft pick. He appeared in all 17 regular-season games but recorded just five receptions for 28 yards and one touchdown on five targets. He also added a notable 23-yard catch on a fake punt during the NFC Championship Game.<ref>{{cite web | title=Commanders' Ben Sinnott: Buried on depth chart all season | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-01-28 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/commanders-ben-sinnott-buried-on-depth-chart-all-season/ | access-date=2026-03-04}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Ujean Hanks''' (born July 31, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] and [[Detroit Lions]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Florida Gators football|Florida]]. He was also a member of the [[Rhein Fire (NFL Europe)|Rhein Fire]] of [[NFL Europe]] and the [[New York/New Jersey Hitmen]] of the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]].

==Early life==
Benjamin Ujean Hanks was born on July 31, 1972, in [[Miami, Florida]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/h/hank00500.html | title=Ben Hanks | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Miami Senior High School]], [[letterman (sports)|lettering]] in football, baseball, and track.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref name="Xfl"/> In football, he earned all-state and Dade County MVP honors.<ref name="Xfl"/>

==College career==
Hanks was a member of the  [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]] from 1991 to 1995.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was [[redshirted]] in 1991.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was then a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1992 to 1995.<ref name="Pfa"/> He garnered [[Associated Press]] (AP) second-team and Coaches first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] recognition as a junior in 1994.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/2579436/the_indexjournal/|work=The Index-Journal|date=November 29, 1994|page=7|title=Crimson Tide, Gators and war Eagles dominate All-SEC squad|accessdate=June 8, 2015|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1320&dat=19941207&id=dYA1AAAAIBAJ&sjid=heoDAAAAIBAJ&pg=1115,1807353&hl=en|title=Carter, Johnson highlight Gator group named All-SEC|work=Gainesville Sun|date=December 7, 1994}}</ref> He was named first-team All-SEC by both the AP and the coaches his senior year in 1995.<ref name=95allsec>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1842&dat=19951206&id=i2keAAAAIBAJ&sjid=fsgEAAAAIBAJ&pg=2387,885436&hl=en|work=Times Daily|date=December 6, 1995|title=All-SEC|page=2D}}</ref> He set a school record for longest fumble return touchdown with a 95-yarder.<ref name="Xfl"/> He graduated from Florida with a degree in public recreation.<ref name="Xfl">{{cite web | url=https://www.all-xfl.com/nynjhitmen/team/roster/benhanks.htm | title=Ben Hanks | publisher=all-xfl.com | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1996 NFL draft]], Hanks signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on April 22.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/h/hank00500.html | title=Ben Hanks NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He played in 12 games for the Vikings during the 1996 season, recording three solo tackles and two assisted tackles, before being placed on injured reserve on December 20, 1996.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HankBe20.htm | title=Ben Hanks | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He was waived by the Vikings in 1997.<ref name="transactions"/>

Hanks was claimed off waivers by the [[Detroit Lions]] on August 25, 1997.<ref name="transactions"/> He appeared in two games during the 1997 season before being waived on September 30.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HankBe20/gamelog/1997/ | title=Ben Hanks | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He was re-signed by the Lions on December 23 and later played in one playoff game for them that year.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr"/> Hanks became a free agent after the season and re-signed with the team on March 26, 1998.<ref name="transactions"/> He was waived on August 25, 1998.<ref name="Pst">{{cite web | url=https://prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Ben+Hanks&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref>

Hanks played for the [[Rhein Fire (NFL Europe)|Rhein Fire]] of [[NFL Europe]] in 1999, totaling 19 defensive tackles, six special teams tackles, one sack, and two forced fumbles.<ref name="Pfa"/>

Hanks played in nine games, starting five, for the [[New York/New Jersey Hitmen]] of the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]] in 2001, posting 17 tackles and one sack.<ref name="Pfa"/>

==Personal life==
In December 2024, Hanks' son, Ben Hanks Jr., committed to play college football for the Florida Gators.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://247sports.com/player/ben-hanks-jr-46134668/ | title=Ben Hanks Jr. | publisher=247sports.com | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] at [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland]]. He also played for the [[Ohio Glory]] of the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF), and the [[Las Vegas Posse]] and [[Shreveport Pirates]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). ==Early life== William Benjamin Jefferson was born on January 15, 1966, in [[New Rochelle, New York]]. By seventh grade, he was already 6'3" and 250 pounds.{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1985/09/13/grown-up-hes-larger-than-life/d08116c6-be0f-4fc2-aef0-c3fc2fdb14e0/ | title=Grown Up, He's Larger Than Life | work=[[The Washington Post]] | date=September 12, 1985 | accessdate=25 December 2024 | author=[[Michael Wilbon|Wilbon, Michael]]}} Due to his size, he was not allowed to play football until eighth grade. He played [[high school football]] at [[New Rochelle High School]]. ==College career== Jefferson was a member of the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]] from 1984 to 1988. He [[redshirted]] in 1984. In 1985, he was featured in an edition of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' as one of the biggest players in college football. He was a [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] in 1985, 1987, and 1988. He missed the 1986 season due to being placed on academic probation.{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1986/09/12/jefferson-is-likely-out-for-season/d92fc7c5-2195-4db3-affc-3672ed356aa2/ | title=Jefferson Is Likely Out For Season | work=[[The Washington Post]] | date=September 12, 1986 | accessdate=25 December 2024 | author=Nicklas, Ed, and Asher, Mark}} ==Professional career== Jefferson signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] after going undrafted in the [[1989 NFL draft]].{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/j/jeff00700.html | title=Ben Jefferson NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}} He was released on September 5 and signed to the practice squad the next day. He was released again on October 19, 1989. Jefferson was signed to the practice squad of the [[Cleveland Browns]] on November 8, 1989. He was released on January 29, 1990, but re-signed on February 27, 1990. He played in four games, all starts at guard, for the Browns during the 1990 season before being placed on injured reserve on October 22, 1990.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JeffBe20.htm | title=Ben Jefferson | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=25 December 2024}} Jefferson was released the next year on August 26, 1991. Jefferson was a starter for the [[Ohio Glory]] of the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF) in 1992.{{cite web | url=https://www.tcdb.com/GalleryP.cfm/pid/177509/Ben-Jefferson | title=Ben Jefferson | publisher=tcdb.com | accessdate=25 December 2024}} He signed with the [[New England Patriots]] on July 28, 1992, before being released on September 1, 1992.{{cite web |title=Ben Jefferson |url=https://www.prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Ben+Jefferson&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&ILChkBx=yes&NBADLChkBx=yes&InjuriesChkBx=yes&PersonalChkBx=yes&DisciplinaryChkBx=yes&LegalChkBx=yes&submit=Search |website=Pro Sports Transactions |access-date=2 June 2024}} Jefferson was signed by the [[Los Angeles Raiders]] on June 10, 1993. He was waived on August 24, 1993. He played in nine games for the [[Las Vegas Posse]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) in 1994. === Pittsburgh Steelers ===
Sauls signed with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] as an undrafted free agent on April 26, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers agree to terms with free agents|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-agree-to-terms-with-free-agents-x9953|website=Steelers.com|date=April 26, 2025}}</ref> He was waived on August 25.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make additional roster moves|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-additional-roster-moves-x1485|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=August 25, 2025}}</ref>

=== Atlanta Falcons ===
On September 23, 2025, the [[Atlanta Falcons]] signed Sauls to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falcons sign kicker, wide receiver to practice squad |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/ben-sauls-deven-thompkins-signed-practice-squad-week-4 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was released on November 4.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Waack |first1=Terrin |title=Falcons bring back familiar face on offensive line |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/andrew-stueber-signed-offensive-lineman |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |access-date=5 November 2025}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On November 11, 2025, Sauls signed with the [[New York Giants]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Sauls: Finds work with G-Men |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/ben-sauls-finds-work-with-g-men/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref>
On December 21, 2025, Sauls made his first professional start against the Minnesota Vikings, becoming the first left footed kicker in the league to appear in a regular season game since [[Sebastian Janikowski]] in the [[2018 NFL season|2018 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/why-giants-lefty-kicker-ben-185003917.html|title=Why Giants have a new lefty kicker Ben Sauls instead of Younghoe Koo|publisher=Yahoo Sports|accessdate=22 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Botte | first=Peter | title=Ben Sauls 'excited' for Giants debut and chance to be NFL's first lefty kicker in seven years | website=New York Post | date=2025-12-20 | url=https://nypost.com/2025/12/19/sports/rookie-kicker-ben-sauls-excited-for-giants-debut-vs-vikings/ | access-date=2026-04-01}}</ref> He was signed to the active roster on December 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants place 4 players on IR, activate 6 for Week 17|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-place-andrew-thomas-john-michael-schmitz-tyler-nubin-on-ir-among-series-of-roster-moves|website=Giants.com|date=December 27, 2025}}</ref>

'''Ben Nikkel''' (born September 24, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[McPherson Bulldogs]] and [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]].

==Early life==
Nikkel was born September 24, 1999 in [[McPherson, Kansas]].<ref name="pfr">{{cite web |title=Ben Nikkel Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NikkBe00.htm |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250406044302/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NikkBe00.htm |archive-date=April 6, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Nikkel, Indianapolis Colts, DB |website=[[CBS Sports]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/players/26700047/ben-nikkel/ |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250913174129/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/players/26700047/ben-nikkel/ |archive-date=September 13, 2025}}</ref> He attended [[McPherson High School]], graduating in 2018. Nikkel played on the school's [[High school football|football]] team as a [[wide receiver]] and [[defensive back]].<ref name="adastra">{{cite web |last=Gillespie |first=Lane |title=Former McPherson High & College Football Star Signs with NFL’s Washington Commanders |website=Ad Astra Radio |url=https://www.adastraradio.com/adastra-sports/former-mcpherson-high-college-football-star-signs-with-nfls-washington-commanders/ |date=April 28, 2024 |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327025500/https://www.adastraradio.com/adastra-sports/former-mcpherson-high-college-football-star-signs-with-nfls-washington-commanders |archive-date=March 27, 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
Nikkel enrolled at [[McPherson College]] to play [[college football]] for the [[McPherson Bulldogs]]. He played [[wide receiver]] for three seasons from 2018 to 2020, recording 107 [[reception (gridiron football)|reception]]s for 1,570 [[Receiving yards|yards]] and 14 [[touchdowns]] in that time.<ref name="adastra" /> Nikkel was a [[team captain]] and a two-time all-conference selection at McPherson.<ref name="isu">{{cite web |title=Ben Nikkel |website=Iowa State University Athletics |url=https://cyclones.com/sports/football/roster/ben-nikkel/12502 |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251221194719/https://cyclones.com/sports/football/roster/ben-nikkel/12502 |archive-date=December 21, 2025}}</ref> He then [[College transfer|transferred]] to play for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]]. He played [[defensive back]] and [[special teams]] as a [[walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] at Iowa State. He [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]ed in 2021 before being awarded a [[scholarship]] and being named a team captain in 2023.<ref name="adastra" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Gray |first=Rob |title=Former NAIA transfer Ben Nikkel embraces ‘controlled chaos’ as Iowa State special teams standout |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |url=https://www.thegazette.com/cyclone-football/former-naia-transfer-ben-nikkel-embraces-controlled-chaos-as-iowa-state-special-teams-standout/ |date=August 11, 2023 |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251221194750/https://www.thegazette.com/cyclone-football/former-naia-transfer-ben-nikkel-embraces-controlled-chaos-as-iowa-state-special-teams-standout/ |archive-date=December 21, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Osen |first=Nick |title=Senior safety Ben Nikkel details memorable week, earning scholarship from the Cyclones |website=[[247Sports]] |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa-state/article/iowa-state-football-ben-nikkel-scholarship-interview-214080241/ |date=August 10, 2023 |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251221195114/https://247sports.com/college/iowa-state/article/iowa-state-football-ben-nikkel-scholarship-interview-214080241/ |archive-date=December 21, 2025}}</ref> Nikkel played in all 12 games in 2022 and recorded three [[tackle (football move)|tackle]]s; in 2023, he played in 12 games with two [[Starting lineup|starts]], recording 40 tackles, one tackle for loss, and three [[pass breakup]]s, as well as a [[blocked punt]] recovery.<ref name="isu" />

Nikkel was not selected in the [[2024 NFL draft]]. He was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Washington Commanders]] on October 22, 2024, and the Commanders signed him to a future contract on January 28, 2025. He was released from the Commanders on August 26.<ref name="pfr" />

The [[Indianapolis Colts]] signed Nikkel to the team's practice squad on August 28, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last=Arthur |first=Jake |title=Colts Sign Receiver with Ties to Alec Pierce, Brian Mason |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/colts/news/colts-sign-receiver-ties-alec-pierce-brian-mason |date=August 28, 2025 |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250829130635/https://www.si.com/nfl/colts/news/colts-sign-receiver-ties-alec-pierce-brian-mason |archive-date=August 29, 2025}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Indianapolis on January 5, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts sign 16 players to reserve/future contracts, sign LB Austin Ajiake to one-year contract extension|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-16-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-sign-lb-austin-ajiake-to-one-year-contract-extension|website=Colts.com|date=January 5, 2026 |access-date=January 5, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106034607/https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-16-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-sign-lb-austin-ajiake-to-one-year-contract-extension |archive-date=January 6, 2026}}</ref>
